Best 1-cost value for my final slot. Manectric's Lightning Rod redirects and absorbs single-target Electric moves, shielding my Electric-weak Talonflame, Primarina and Skarmory (and punishing Raichu/Rotom-Heat Discharge users) while giving Manectric a SpA boost; at 105 Speed it also supplies fast Snarl SpA-drops against sun/special teams, Volt Switch pivoting, and Flamethrower/Overheat/Thunderbolt coverage. It rounds out the roster with a real doubles utility niche for one point.

Completes the roster at exactly 100 points with our first Intimidate user, another Ghost immunity, and base-110 Speed. Verified Raging Bull removes screens, while Close Combat, High Horsepower, Rock Slide, and Helping Hand give it useful matchup-specific roles.

Mega Ampharos: 165 SpA Electric/Dragon with Mold Breaker and 90/105/110 bulk for 4 points — a special wallbreaker (Thunderbolt/Dragon Pulse/Focus Blast) that fits a slower Kingambit/Steelix mode and flexes as a non-mega Static Electric.

Last point: Flash Fire is the only Heat Wave absorb on the roster for Charizard Y, plus Dark STAB into Gholdengo/Gengar. Forretress Steel is less useful than an absorb vs the sun team we actually have to beat.

3 points for a TR-able Adaptability special wall: base Dragalge keeps Adaptability, so Sludge Wave is boosted STAB hitting 2x into every Fairy on the board (luna's Gardevoir-M, fable's Clefable-M... fable has Altaria-M, deepseek's Primarina), plus Draco Meteor, Toxic, Thunder Wave and 123 SpD. Slow (44 Spe) — ideal Trick Room piece; completes the roster at exactly 100.
3rd Intimidate + Sucker Punch/Taunt, denies Mega Mawile Huge Power threat.

builds.rationale: Sun + Chlorophyll Venusaur is the threat: only Noivern Tailwind lets us outrun it, with Incineroar Fake Out to stop turn-1 Sleep Powder. Ceruledge Flash Fire walls Zard Y Heat Wave and sweeps Venusaur/Alcremie/Gholdengo with Bitter Blade + Sneak, while Garchomp Rock Slide pressures Zard/Dragonite. Mega Clefable Magic Bounce + Follow Me bounces sleep/status and covers dragons/fighters; Rotom Leaf Storm deletes Swampert/Tauros-Aqua.

Against an opponent relying heavily on triple-Intimidate pivots (Incineroar, Scrafty, Mawile) and dragon speed threats (Dragapult, Garchomp), our squad provides hard counter-play across every dimension. Defiant Passimian with Quick Guard turns enemy Intimidates into lethal offensive momentum while completely nullifying opposing Fake Out and priority, whereas Inner Focus Lum Berry Dragonite operates entirely unaffected by attack drops, flinches, or burns. Timid Choice Scarf Gholdengo naturally outspeeds and OHKOs max-speed Dragapult with Shadow Ball while shredding Mega Clefable with Make It Rain, Swampert neutralizes Garchomp's spread Earthquakes with Wide Guard while threatening an immediate 4x Ice Punch KO, and the Mega Charizard Y plus Chlorophyll Venusaur Sun core exerts overwhelming high-speed special board control.

Their draft projects rain (Pelipper + Swift Swim Basculegion/Qwilfish + Electro Shot Archaludon) fused with Psychic-surge spam (Indeedee-F + Mega Gardevoir's Pixilate Hyper Voice). My plan: Corviknight + Dragalge wall the special cores — Corv eats Hyper Voice for 17-28% and Iron Heads Gardevoir back, Dragalce absorbs Electro Shot (19-34%) and rain Wave Crash (47-86%) while Sludge Wave sits in Gardevoir OHKO range. Hatterene and Farigiraf are both Trick Room setters, so Taunt/Fake Out/Thunder Wave (Magic Bounce + Mental Herb + Armor Tail) can't stop speed inversion, and under TR my 49-79 Speed squad always moves first against their entire roster. Clawitzer is the TR nuke: Aura Sphere 2x Archaludon/Morpeko, Dark Pulse 2x Indeedee, Ice Beam 2x Sceptile/Gliscor, Hydro Pump OHKOs Gliscor (whose Poison Heal is dead — no Toxic Orb in this format). Mega Mence is the rain answer: Rock Slide 4x Pelipper, EQ 4x Archaludon, 171 Speed beats Timid Gardevoir — just never lead it into Hyper Voice.

Pelipper establishes rain for Swift Swim Basculegion and immediate Electro Shot Archaludon, while Tailwind and Icy Wind provide flexible speed control. Indeedee-F supplies Psychic Terrain, Follow Me, and Imprison against Trick Room; Mega Gardevoir converts that terrain into strong spread pressure and threatens the Dragons and Fighters of the opposing pool. Qwilfish adds Intimidate, Haze, and Poison pressure into physical setup and Azumarill, with Wide Guard from Pelipper protecting the rain core from opposing spread attacks.

Their likely core is Mega Metagross plus Primarina, Talonflame, Arcanine, and either Mamoswine or Sinistcha. Grassy Surge plus Follow Me Clefable lets Mega Dragonite click Fire Blast/Hurricane through Ice Shard and EQ; Mental Herb keeps Follow Me live through Talonflame Taunt. Skeledirge Unaware walls Meteor Mash and Gale Wings Brave Bird, then Torch Songs the Steels and Ice. Greninja Life Orb Hydro Pump is the clean Talonflame/Arcanine/Mamoswine answer and Dark Pulses Metagross; Sneasler Sash Fake Outs and covers Primarina/Mamoswine when Rillaboom is not in. Bring Rilla+Clef+DN+Dirge vs Metagross/Mamo, swap Greninja in vs the Fires, Sneasler in vs Primarina without Rilla.

This opponent leans on Mega Dragonite plus fast Sneasler/Greninja and Prankster Grimmsnarl screens. Primarina is the anchor: it is immune to Dragon STAB, resists Fire/Hurricane, and hits Dragonite 4x with Ice Beam. Metagross breaks Clefable/Grimmsnarl with Meteor Mash and chips Dragonite with Ice Punch, while Talonflame's Gale Wings Brave Bird and Arcanine's Intimidate + Will-O-Wisp + Extreme Speed blanket Sneasler, Rillaboom and Greninja. Mamoswine and Rotom-Frost add Ice/Ground and Ice/Electric coverage to break Multiscale and Focus Sashes, with Protect on every non-Metagross slot for Fake Out and positioning.

Opponent leans on Prankster Whimsicott speed control, Annihilape/Chandelure Ghosts and a Mega Excadrill whose contact moves pierce Protect. Mega Gengar is the primary mega: Shadow Tag traps and Sludge Bomb one-shots Whimsicott, Shadow Ball chunks Annihilape/Chandelure, Focus Blast threatens Excadrill/Weavile/Empoleon. Salamence (Sash) provides Tailwind + Intimidate and Heat Wave/Draco for Excadrill and Hydrapple; Kangaskhan gives Scrappy Fake Out (hits their Ghosts pre-mega) to buy Gengar and Tailwind turns. Rotom-Wash is the Excadrill/Rotom-Heat/Empoleon answer (Levitate, Hydro Pump, Will-O-Wisp); Kingambit with Chople cleans Weavile/Chandelure/Whimsicott with Sucker Punch and punishes Tauros Intimidate via Defiant. Altaria is the flex mega for Annihilape/Hydrapple/Weavile-heavy brings (Ground-immune, Fairy spread). Avoid Intimidating Annihilape (Defiant) and keep Gengar/Kingambit away from Excadrill Ground moves.

Play Tailwind offense with Whimsicott and Excadrill, or build an Annihilape endgame with Beat Up and Maushold's redirection; bring four with a clear damage plan rather than automatically bringing both supports. Weavile supplies the fastest unboosted Fake Out in this matchup and pressures Salamence, while Hydrapple answers Rotom-Wash and supplies special damage. Against Mega Gengar, establish Tailwind safely—often with Annihilape protecting—and remember that Annihilape can escape Shadow Tag, but our other five cannot. Preserve Excadrill against Mega Altaria, and use Defiant Annihilape to discourage Salamence's Intimidate.

Register the rain/terrain shell with two complementary speed modes: Pelipper enables Swift Swim Basculegion and one-turn Archaludon Electro Shot, while Indeedee protects Mega Gardevoir from ordinary priority and provides Follow Me/Helping Hand positioning. Qwilfish supplies Intimidate, Icy Wind, and Haze against physical or setup modes, while Archaludon and Gardevoir pressure Fairy, Dragon, Steel, and Ground targets. The default board is Indeedee plus Pelipper with Gardevoir or Archaludon; bring Basculegion when rain speed is safe, and preserve Pelipper or Indeedee rather than trading both early.

Lead Pincurchin+Noivern or Pincurchin+Incin vs Indeedee+Pelipper: Pincurchin 15 base moves last so Electric Surge overrides Psychic Terrain enabling FakeOut, Noivern Taunts Pelipper TW and sets our TW. Rotom walls rain WaveCrash and fires 100% rain Thunder into Pelipper/Basculegion with Leaf Storm second STAB, Dragapult adds fast Thunder plus mixed Darts/ShadowBall for Indeedee/Garde/Arch, Skarmory gives Sturdy second Tailwind and walls Hurricane/Fairy with Iron Head/Rock Slide.

Sun matchup built to blunt spread. Machamp's Wide Guard blanks Charizard-Y's sun Heat Wave and Gholdengo's Make It Rain, their two main damage sources, while Scrafty's Fake Out breaks Dragonite's Multiscale and buys Talonflame's Tailwind turn 1. Charizard-Y dies to Machamp Stone Edge (No Guard, 4x) or Mamoswine Rock Slide (4x); Gholdengo dies to sun-boosted Arcanine/Talonflame Flare Blitz (note: Fighting is 0x on its Ghost/Steel typing); Dragonite falls to Mamoswine Ice Shard/Icicle Crash and Primarina Ice Beam; Primarina's Energy Ball deletes Swampert. Bench Primarina while Venusaur's Solar Beam/Sludge Bomb is live, and never leave Arcanine or Mamoswine in vs Swampert High Horsepower or Passimian Close Combat. Mega Metagross stays home because sun Heat Wave is a guaranteed OHKO on it through spread.

Our gameplan counters DeepSeek's offensive core (Mega Metagross, Talonflame, Arcanine, Primarina, Mamoswine, Hydreigon) with hard tactical disruption. Passimian's +3 Quick Guard and Defiant completely shut down opposing Gale Wings Brave Bird, Extreme Speed, Ice Shard, and Intimidate drops. Mega Charizard Y's Drought slashes Primarina's Water STAB by 50% while unlocking Venusaur's 264 Speed Chlorophyll sweep and delivering guaranteed OHKOs onto Mega Metagross with Sun Overheat. Swampert's Wide Guard indefinitely nullifies opposing spread moves like Hyper Voice and Earthquake, while Choice Scarf Gholdengo outspeeds their entire roster and Dragonite provides Inner Focus priority cleanup.

Use flexible Tailwind offense: Whimsicott plus Empoleon or Weavile pressures Mega Salamence, while Excadrill supplies the Ground/Steel endgame; preserve Whimsicott for a second speed-control cycle rather than spending it automatically. Against Farigiraf/Hatterene, favor Chandelure beside Excadrill or Weavile: establish Imprison, attack the setters immediately, and keep Chandelure active because switching or fainting releases the lock. Against Corviknight/Dragalge, pair Fire pressure with Excadrill's High Horsepower, respecting Protect, Flying switches, and delayed Tailwind. Against water-heavy selections prioritize Empoleon plus Rotom, using Grass Knot/Thunderbolt and defensive switches rather than exposing both Fire types together. Armor Tail blocks our Fake Out and targeted Prankster moves, not Tailwind/Light Screen/Imprison; always evaluate both enemy attacks, and remember that matching Tailwinds still leave Mega Salamence faster than everyone here except Weavile.

astra's committed four (Whimsicott+Weavile leads, Annihilape+Mega Excadrill behind) fold to my T1 Trick Room script: Farigiraf's Armor Tail blocks the Fake Out, Mental Herb eats the Prankster Taunt, and Corviknight Iron Heads Weavile through its Sash while the room resolves. Under inversion, Azumarill Play Rough + Farigiraf Psychic pair-kill Annihilape the turn it's live (before Bulk Up), Dragalge Sludge Wave deletes Whimsicott at 4x even through spread, and Corviknight — immune to Excadrill-Mega's Ground STAB — Body Presses it down with Taunt/Roost support. Hatterene (Magic Bounce TR insurance) and Garganacl (Wide Guard vs Rock Slide; Rock Slide execute on Chandelure/Rotom-Heat) stay registered as game-2/3 flex if their unseen slots surface.

grok leads Rillaboom + support, Fake Outs the mega T1 and Protect-spams (even consecutively); Dragonite megas on entry (Fire Blast at the Steel). G1 lead Kangaskhan + Kingambit: Kanga Fake Out Inteleon/Rillaboom, Kingambit Iron Head Clefable/Grimmsnarl (OHKO range) or Kowtow Rillaboom; if Sneasler/Tauros leads, Kingambit Protects T1 while Kanga Fake Outs it (Tauros Intimidate = +2 Defiant). Gengar (Sludge Bomb Rillaboom 81-189%/Clefable 72-159%, Psychic 4x Sneasler, 62-147% Tauros, Shadow Ball Skeledirge) comes in only after Inteleon/Dark threats are removed or flinched; it is immune to Fake Out, Extreme Speed, Close Combat. Houndoom switches into Fire Blast/Torch Song aimed at Kingambit for a Flash Fire boost and Heat Waves Rillaboom (83-189%); Altaria-Mega walls Dragonite's Dragon moves and Hyper Voice ignores Follow Me (90-212% Tauros); Glalie is the surprise mega vs Dragonite (Refrigerate Body Slam = 102 BP Ice STAB, 4x on Dragonite through Multiscale). Exploit their Protect habit: attack the turn after a Protect, hit the partner when the obvious Protect is coming; change the lead in G2/G3 (Glalie+Kanga or Houndoom+Kingambit).

Physical-core week vs their Gengar+Kanga+Gambit+Mence (Wash/Altaria in reserve, Greninja the new Ice/Dark). Sneasler snipes Gambit and Greninja; Combat Intimidates Kanga/Mence and helmet-chips Kanga contact; Grimm puts both screens up for 8. Mega DN immediately: Ice Beam always KOs Mence, Fire Blast leftover Steel. Rilla Fake Out + Wood Hammer deletes Wash and Greninja. Dirge Ghost-switches Tag and walls Kanga. Never lead Combat+Sneasler into Gengar (Fighting is 0, Tag glues both). Fake Out Greninja so Ice Beam never breaks Multiscale. Sneasler 189 does not outrun Timid Greninja 191 or Timid Gengar 200.

Bring Incin+Noivern+Pincurchin+Rotom+Excadrill+Tinkaton vs MMeta/Talon/Prim/Machamp/Scrafty core. Incin immune to Zen walls MMeta and threatens FlareBlitz/CC while Noivern Sash guarantees TW vs faster Talon BraveBird. Pincurchin/Rotom Thunder+LeafStorm answer Talon/Prim/Mamo with TWave to halve Talon/Meta/Hydreigon for Rotom/Excadrill to finish. Excadrill MoldBreaker EQ/RockSlide hits Meta/Talon through Levitate and Tinkaton walls Hydreigon/Draco immune with Encore vs Prim Protect stall and PlayRough/Gigaton vs Scrafty/Machamp/Prim.

vs muse's Electric-Terrain/Tailwind/hazards shell: Mamoswine is the Electric-immune breaker (Expert Belt High Horsepower is 2x on Pincurchin/Incineroar/Excadrill/Tinkaton and OHKOs Pincurchin, Ice covers Noivern/Dragapult/Rotom-Mow), and Rotom-Frost resists Electric while being Ground-immune with Thunderbolt for Skarmory/Clefable and Blizzard for Noivern/Dragapult. Metagross is the bulky wincon that walls their special side (Poison-immune, resists Flying/Fairy) and KOs Clefable/Tinkaton/Dragapult, Talonflame sets priority Gale Wings Tailwind and Taunts their screens/hazards/Tailwind before Tinkaton can move, and Arcanine Intimidates then Flare Blitzes Tinkaton/Skarmory/Rotom-Mow. Scrafty is the Fake Out + second Intimidate + Knock Off tempo glue; lead Mamoswine+Talonflame to remove the terrain setter and set Tailwind, keep Scrafty/Metagross in front of physical leads, and hold Primarina home (Pincurchin/Rotom-Mow Electric 2x OHKOs her).

This six combines rain and Psychic Terrain with layered speed control: Pelipper supplies Tailwind and Wide Guard, while Qwilfish provides Intimidate, Icy Wind, Haze, and Taunt into physical snowballing or Whimsicott disruption. Telepathy Mega Gardevoir and Garchomp give immediate pressure into Annihilape and Mega Excadrill, while Air Balloon Archaludon exploits rain with Electro Shot and remains a Steel/Dragon endgame piece. Preserve Pelipper and at least one attacker rather than exposing the rain core to unscouted Electric or concentrated Ground pressure.

The current roster replaces Basculegion with Garchomp: use fast Ice/Steel pressure and special attacks into Archaludon rather than preparing for an absent Swift Swim sweeper. Weavile + Excadrill is an opening candidate into Indeedee/Pelipper: focused Knock Off + Iron Head pressures redirection, while ordinary-priority Taunt can deny support through Psychic Terrain; check their actual items, speed control and switches before committing. Whimsicott supplies renewable Tailwind, rain suppression and Light Screen, with Rotom exploiting sun and Empoleon providing Ice/Steel cleanup. Hydrapple is the slower special-Ground option into Archaludon and opposing Trick Room, not a Gardevoir wall. Choose the four from the revealed sheet, preserve a coherent finishing pair, and evaluate both opposing attacks before relying on a defensive berry or spending a support turn.

This six hard-counters Claude's reliance on Turn 1 Scrappy Fake Out and Kingambit Sucker Punch through Passimian's Quick Guard, while Defiant punishes any Salamence Intimidate. Ghost typing renders Choice Scarf Gholdengo completely immune to Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag trapping while outspeeding and OHKOing it with STAB Shadow Ball. Mega Charizard Y and Chlorophyll Venusaur establish oppressive sun control, slashing Rotom-Wash's Water output while threatening massive spread and single-target damage. Swampert provides electric immunity and Wide Guard spread denial, while Inner Focus Dragonite bypasses flinches and Intimidate to clean up with priority Extreme Speed.

Gemini has brought Charizard-Y + Gholdengo + Swampert every game plus Dragonite or Passimian, leading Gholdengo with the fourth mon; Charizard enters mid-game and PROTECTS the turn it enters (3/3), then megas and Heat Waves. Loop: 1) kill Gholdengo early - Kingambit walls it (Kowtow 63-141%, Sucker Punch 53-116% but Passimian Quick Guard blocks priority) + Gengar Shadow Ball 66-148% / Houndoom Dark Pulse 64-141%; 2) the turn Charizard enters, hit its partner; next turn Lycanroc Rock Slide/Stone Edge (180 Spe > 167, OHKO) or Rotom-W Thunderbolt 53-114%, or pivot Houndoom (Flash Fire) into the Heat Wave slot with Protect on the partner (sun Heat Wave kills Kingambit 117-200% and Gengar 83-141%); 3) close with Mega Gengar (200 Spe outspeeds all of them; Energy Ball OHKOs Swampert 95-206%, Psychic 60-142% Sash Passimian / 62-147% Tauros-Aqua). Leads: Kingambit + Rotom-W (safest: Kingambit Protect T1 vs CC/Fake Out, Rotom Will-O-Wisp Passimian or Thunderbolt, takes Make It Rain 12-20%) or Gengar + Kingambit; Lycanroc + Kingambit only vs Dragonite lead (Quick Guard stops Extreme Speed) - never Lycanroc into Passimian/Gholdengo (both OHKO it). Salamence is the G2/G3 mega or when Passimian is off the field (Intimidate feeds Defiant); it dies to Dragonite Ice Spinner 65-114%, Alcremie Dazzling Gleam and Make It Rain 49-86% - Kingambit walls those. Umbreon Foul Play 61-120% on Gengar: Focus Blast absent, so Kingambit/Salamence wear it down. Change the lead in G2 after a win; attack the turn after each of their Protects; single-target only while Swampert (Wide Guard) is out.

Grok's fixed script (Grimm+Snea lead, Skeledirge Protect-stall, DNite-M Multiscale closer) is met with the Trick Room core plus both scheduled flexes: Bax-M in over Azu — Helping Hand Icicle Crash one-shots full-HP Multiscale Dragonite (100-209.6%, tool-verified both endpoints) — and Cofagrigus in over Dragalge as the Sneasler blank (Fake Out/CC immune) with Night Shade to out-grind Protect chains. Lead Farig+Corv: Armor Tail eats their T1 Fake Out and Prankster Taunt, Mental Herb is the Taunt backup, TR goes up T1, and Corv Iron Head-executes Grimm (observed one IH → 24%; two kill). Under TR Hatt deletes Sneasler (4x Psychic, min roll 150%), Farig Psy is the backup 4x, and Garg walls every Fire angle (FB 13-23, Torch 0.5x) while Salt Cure grinds Skeledirge through Protect. Kill order: Sneasler → Grimm → Skele → DNite-M last for Bax, who only ever acts under TR; vs unseen Rilla/Tauros-C/Inteleon, Corv Brave Bird is 2x on Rilla and Tauros and Corv/Cofag absorb Inteleon.

Their mega is now Baxcalibur (Dragon/Ice, max Spe 152), not Mence \u2014 Ice is 1x into it, Fire boosts it via Thermal Exchange, and Ice Crash 4x can roll KO Multiscale DN. Fairy (Clef/Grimm), Draco Meteor (Timid 167 DN), and Unaware Dirge are the Bax answers; Clef Follow Me eats Dragon (immune) and Ice (1x). Armor Tail still blanks all our priority while Farig is in; screens and Follow Me still work. Rilla WH deletes Azu/Clawitzer/Garg; Inteleon Dark Pulse pressures Farig/Cofag; Dirge Shadows Hatterene/Cofag and Torches Corv. Leave Sneasler (4x Psychic) and Combat (Mirror Armor + TR). Do not Fire Bax, Ghost Farig, status Hatterene, contact Cofag, or lead Inteleon into TR.

offers.offerReasoning: All 8 rosters sit at 100, so only equal-cost 1-for-1s are legal. No 18-cost piece exists to get Incineroar; no 11-cost piece exists to get Arcanine. Core 19/16/15s would have to move for Whimsicott/Gholdengo/Kanga/Primarina, which guts the Mega-DN enable core and those coaches will not sell W1 staples anyway. Rotom-for-Tauros/Qwilfish/Mawile is Arbok-tier Intimidate and wrecks the Combat FA (drop Houndoom+Rotom, sign Combat 3). Keep the 10, take Combat in FA.

offers.message: 3-for-3 benched swap, both stay 100. You get Intimidate/FakeOut/KnockOff Scrafty (hits Ghosts like Sinistcha/Gengar, CC for Steels) for your crime-fighting core. We get Sturdy Tailwind/Taunt Steel for rain prep. Win-win fit.
offers.offerReasoning: Equal 3-3 keeps both at 100. Skarmory gives 2nd Tailwind (only Noivern has TW), Sturdy, Hurricane 0.5x + Fairy 0.5x resists vs Pelipper/MGardevoir where Scrafty is weak (2x Flying, 4x Fairy), IronHead SE vs Gardevoir + DrillRun SE vs Arch. Preserves Mega + core 5 for W2, adds Steel/Espeed resist for future. Scrafty benched-for-benched, past-bench Skarmory for them.
offers.responseReasoning: Cost-neutral 1-for-1 (Skarmory 3 <-> Scrafty 3), keeps 10 mons and 100/100. Skarmory is deep bench for me: never registered, redundant with Talonflame as Tailwind, and Spikes is low-impact in doubles. Scrafty fills my single biggest structural gap — I run no Fake Out — while adding a genuinely distinct support package: Fake Out (tempo), Knock Off (item control vs Sitrus/Mental Herb), Snarl, Taunt, Quick Guard, Coaching, plus Dark STAB (2x vs the Ghosts/Psychics all over this league: Dragapult, Ceruledge, Gengar-Mega, Sinistcha, Skeledirge, Farigiraf, Indeedee-F) and Close Combat for Steel walls (Gholdengo, Kingambit, Archaludon, Corviknight, Empoleon). Ice Punch is an extra 4x Dragonite tool if needed. Body is bulky (65/90/115/45/115/58) with Intimidate, so it fits my bulky-offense shell as a flex slot. Weak to Fairy/Fighting/Flying and it duplicates Arcanine's Intimidate, but the Fake Out + Knock Off + Dark STAB combination is an option I can neither buy with my 0 free budget nor get from anyone already on the roster. Losing Skarmory to a week-3 opponent is a mild concern (it resists Steel and checks Metagross), but Talonflame/Arcanine Fire handles it. Net upgrade in flexibility for a mon I never used.

offers.message: 12-for-12 benched swap, both stay 100. You get Fire/Ghost for Steels/Grasses, we get Ground/Ice for Dragons. Fair.
offers.offerReasoning: Second offer attempt to gain Ice, else will pass.
offers.responseReasoning: Value is nominal (12<->12) but fit is not. Ceruledge (Fire/Ghost, 125 Atk, Bitter Blade/Poltergeist/Shadow Sneak/Swords Dance/Flash Fire) is a strong mon, but it would be my THIRD Fire-type (Talonflame, Arcanine already) and stacks shared Water/Ground/Rock/Ghost/Dark weaknesses on a bulky-offense team whose remaining flaw is exactly that (Metagross already 2x weak to Ground). Its main niche — Ghost/Dark pressure on Psychics/Ghosts — is now partly covered by the Scrafty I just acquired (Dark STAB, Knock Off). Meanwhile Mamoswine is my ONLY Ground-type, ONLY Rock Slide spread, my Ice Shard priority revenge killer, my 4x Rock Slide answer to Charizard-Y (the core of my already-built week-2 sun plan) and Freeze-Dry covers Water-types; none of that is replaceable in-house. Schedule factor: the offer comes from muse, my week-3 opponent, who would receive a Mamoswine that hits my Metagross 2x with Earthquake and threatens Talonflame with Rock Slide/Ice Shard right before facing me. I keep Mamoswine and address the Fire/Ghost role in-house if needed.

offers.offerReasoning: No trade improves the roster enough to justify disturbing the six-piece rain/terrain core. Equal-budget legal bench swaps are lateral, while meaningful Week 2 targets would require sacrificing a core member or violate the 100-point cap.

Every coach sits at exactly 100/100, so only equal-cost swaps are legal. My tradable pieces are the 4-pointers (Toxicroak, Mega Ampharos, Mega Glalie) and the 6-point Mega Steelix; the only equal-cost pieces on other rosters (Pincurchin, Clawitzer, Machamp, Rotom-Frost, Alcremie at 4; Toxtricity, Hydrapple, Chandelure at 6) are sidegrades at best and none fixes a real gap (redirection, reliable Intimidate/Fake Out beyond Kangaskhan). Glalie now has a defined role vs grok's Dragonite/Rillaboom, Toxicroak keeps the Dry Skin niche vs luna's rain, Steelix is the Fairy/Electric wall. No offer beats overpaying or churning for nothing.

offers.message: Equal-cost offer: Maushold for Gholdengo, keeping both rosters at 100. Maushold gives your sun team a non-Mega Friend Guard + Follow Me option alongside Charizard, and can protect Dragonite's setup or Venusaur from single-target pressure. It also has Helping Hand, Super Fang, Encore and Feint, so it needn't be a passive redirection slot. You retain Charizard as your headline special attacker; I gain a special attacking option for my Tailwind team.
offers.offerReasoning: Gholdengo's verified Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Nasty Plot/Thunderbolt/Trick compress immediate special offense and setup alongside Whimsicott, improving pressure into upcoming Fairy/Psychic cores and adding spread offense independent of MausApe. Losing unique Friend Guard/redirection is material, but this premium equal-cost attacker justifies it while preserving Whimsicott, Annihilape, and Mega Excadrill. Maushold offers genuine sun/setup support to the counterparty, though their demonstrated Gholdengo usage makes rejection plausible. No budget or species conflict.
offers.responseReasoning: Gholdengo is an indispensable offensive pillar, providing Good as Gold status immunity, Ghost/Steel defensive typing, and premier special spread damage (Make It Rain). Trading it for Maushold would strip our core special firepower and give a direct competitor a devastating Tailwind sweeper, while our roster already possesses ample redirection and support tools.

offers.offerReasoning: The Maushold-for-Gholdengo offer was rejected; our roster remains unchanged at 100/100. No remaining trade offers a sufficiently clear multi-week improvement to justify surrendering core roles. Retain Friend Guard/Follow Me, Whimsicott–Excadrill offense, Chandelure's Imprison/TR, and Hydrapple's Water resilience. Address upcoming matchups through rebuilt sets and separately evaluate targeted free-agent changes rather than making a lateral trade merely to transact.

Roster is at exactly 100/100 and every coach in the league is also at 100, so any trade forces incoming cost ≤ outgoing — only lateral or point-down swaps are possible, never upgrades. No hard hole has appeared: W1 won 2-1, the W2 script vs astra (Farig+Corv lead, TR core, Azu/Drag/Garg executes) is locked and counters the observed Whim/Weav/Ape/ExcMega core, and my notebook's transaction plan says trade only if a hole appears after W2. Bench (Mence, Clawitzer, Toxtricity, Palafin) already covers the scheduled archetypes. Preserving the TR engine intact is worth more than any available lateral swap; I keep both remaining windows for a targeted fix (second Wide Guard user, Ghost STAB, status-item holder) if W2 exposes one.
Roster is structurally complete at 100/100 points with optimal role compression, weather synergy, and tactical counters for upcoming matchups. Retaining full roster as planned.

No offer. Every roster in the league sits at exactly 100/100, so any swap must be exactly equal-priced to keep both sides legal — the market is effectively locked to same-cost 1-for-1s. My structural gap (no Fake Out) is now filled by Scrafty, and my written rule is to transact only when bench value converts into a starter-level upgrade, else do nothing. Scanning equal-cost targets: (a) Fillers Machamp 4 / Rotom-Frost 4 / Manectric 1 have no better same-cost body available (pincurchin, clawitzer, toxicroak, glalie-mega, ampharos-mega, alcremie, altaria, houndoom are all lateral or Mega-conflicting, and I value Machamp's Wide/Quick Guard and Rotom-Frost's Levitate+Electric/Ice). (b) Mamoswine 12 is NOT surplus: it is my only Ground STAB, only Rock Slide spread (4x Charizard-Y, my week-2 line), Ice Shard priority and Freeze-Dry Water coverage; the only unused 12s are Palafin (build-around Zero to Hero, clunky without reliable pivoting) and Rotom-Heat (Ground immunity already covered by Rotom-Frost's Levitate, and it adds a Water/Rock weakness). (c) Sinistcha 18 is my only Rage Powder, only Trick Room and my Heatproof/Scald sun tech; the 18-cost bodies I could ask for (Incineroar now redundant with Arcanine+Scrafty, Garchomp duplicates Mamoswine's Ground and adds a 4x Ice weakness, Gengar-Mega conflicts with Metagross, Indeedee-F duplicates redirection, Farigiraf) are either not clearly better or are their owners' core (glm brought Farigiraf 3/3), so acceptance odds are low and the gain is uncertain. (d) Arcanine 11 is core and the only 11 (Salamence) is a used core piece that duplicates Talonflame's Flying and Arcanine's Intimidate. Per my risk rule not to worsen the Fire/Ground weakness profile, I hold the roster and make no offer.

moves.reasoning: 9-mon Combat plan is illegal (exactly 10, 1-for-1). Only Greninja is a \u22653 cut that does not gut Fake Out/Follow Me/screens/DN/Sneasler/Dirge/Cloud Nine. Combat is the W2-planned Intimidate into Kanga/Gambit/Mence and the W5/W6 physical cores; we pick first so take it. Inteleon spends the leftover 4 on a Water we will actually bring: Snipe Shot bypasses W3 Farigiraf and W4 Indeedee Follow Me, 100% acc after the W1 Hydro miss, keeps Dark Pulse/Ice Beam, 125 SpA. Keep Rotom for W2 Tag and Altaria for W4/W7. Houndoom was never-bring. No Arbok/1-cost junk.

W2 rain: Overqwil Dark SE Indeedee/Basculegion Poison SE Gardevoir SwiftSwim+Intim+Taunt vs Pelipper/TW; Excadrill Ground SE Arch Steel SE Gardevoir Rock vs Pelipper, resists Draco/Fairy where Garchomp weak. Saves 13pts (100->87) bank for later, uses 2/6 allowance.

No free agent is a clear upgrade within the 100-point cap without cutting a core piece. Garchomp is appealing but replacing Basculegion, Indeedee, or Archaludon would weaken the established rain/terrain matchup plan; bench swaps are lateral or irrelevant.

Toxicroak and Mega Ampharos were the two roster pieces with no clear bring case (never registered in week 1; Ampharos is a 6th mega on a team that only megas Gengar). Greninja (7, just released by grok) is a real upgrade: 191 Spe Timid, Protean/Battle Bond, Icy Wind as a second speed-control source, Ice Beam for the league's many Dragons (Dragonite x2, Mega Salamence, Dragapult, Noivern, Garchomp), Dark Pulse for Gholdengo/Metagross/Sinistcha/Farigiraf, Taunt vs glm's Trick Room, U-turn pivoting. Houndoom (1) fills the remaining point as a Flash Fire switch-in for the Fire-heavy weeks (Zard-Y, Talonflame/Arcanine, Incineroar) with Snarl/Heat Wave/Dark Pulse. Net cost stays 100; keeps core Gengar/Kingambit/Kanga/Rotom-W/Salamence/Altaria/Glalie/Steelix and 4 swaps for later windows.

Keep the 100-point roster and all six swaps for the two remaining windows. The Gholdengo trade was rejected, not executed. Week1 exposed sequencing and preservation errors rather than a demonstrated roster failure; five members were never brought, so dismantling the support core now would be premature. For week2, existing Chandelure Imprison/TR, Rotom-Heat special pressure, Excadrill, and optional Maushold protection address dual speed control without relying on blocked Prankster Taunt. Preserve Weavile's natural Speed above Mega Salamence and Hydrapple's Water resilience for upcoming matchups. Araquanid would add valuable Wide Guard and slow Water offense, but financing it through Maushold forfeits our sole reliable Follow Me/Friend Guard combination, while its Flying/Electric weaknesses mean it is not a complete rain answer. Cheap Wide Guard substitutions likewise sacrifice useful roles without clearly improving the full six. Reassess after testing matchup-specific sixes in week2; prioritize genuine rain and spread-defense gaps then, rather than buying redundant Fire/Ghost/Steel offense or competing Megas now.

No swaps this window. The registered six (Farigiraf/Corv/Hatt/Azu/Drag/Garg) is locked for the W2 script vs astra and fits every scheduled archetype; W1 confirmed the core works (2-1, only loss was a misread, Corv untouched in G3). Bench pieces (Mence, Clawitzer, Palafin, Toxtricity) cover the known modes, and Clawitzer is specifically the first swap-in vs Mega Excadrill. Free-agent adds like Aegislash (16) or Mawile-Mega (16) would require dropping Mence (20) or Farigiraf (18) — the former sheds my only fast-sweeper insurance for a role Corv+Garg already fill, the latter is core. Everyone else is at/near budget and the pool upgrades available are lateral at best. Keeping all 6 season swaps banked for windows 2-3 preserves optionality if W2 exposes a hard hole (target list: second Wide Guard user, Ghost STAB, status-item holder).

Conserving all free-agent swaps. Roster is perfectly balanced at 100/100 points, featuring elite weather synergy (Mega Charizard Y + Chlorophyll Venusaur), unblockable Intimidate (Tauros-Aqua), priority control (Dragonite Extreme Speed, Swampert Wide Guard, Passimian Quick Guard), Lightning Rod redirection (Raichu), and status immunity (Gholdengo Good as Gold), with direct tactical advantages against Week 2 opponent entrant 5.

One swap. Sinistcha (18) is my most expensive mon yet a purely situational bench support (redirection/TR/Heatproof), and 18 points on the bench is poor value; my meta notes already flag Fire and Ground as my two structural weaknesses. Hydreigon (14), now undrafted, patches BOTH: Dark/Dragon resists Fire 0.5x and Levitate grants a Ground immunity, while adding the special offense my team lacks (only Primarina/Rotom-Frost hit specially). Its kit fits my method: Dark Pulse 2x on the league's many Psychics/Ghosts (Farigiraf, Indeedee-F, Gardevoir, Gengar, Dragapult, Chandelure, Annihilape, Skeledirge), Flash Cannon for Fairies, Fire Blast/Heat Wave for Steels/Grasses, plus Tailwind (backup speed control), Snarl (spread SpA drop that sun doesn't weaken), U-turn (safe pivot to bring Metagross/Primarina in), Taunt and Nasty Plot. Cost drops 100 -> 96, roster stays 10 mons, one per base species. I keep every key role: Talonflame Tailwind, Arcanine Intimidate/ESpeed/Snarl, Scrafty Fake Out/Knock Off/Intimidate, Machamp Wide Guard/Quick Guard, Rotom-Frost Levitate/Electric+Ice, Mamoswine Ground/Ice/Rock, Manectric Lightning Rod (still shields Primarina/Talonflame/Arcanine from Electric and offers a Mega option), primarina/Metagross wincons. Its Fairy/Ice frailty is a managed risk covered by four Fairy-resistant bodies and my Fake Out/Wide Guard; losing Rage Powder is acceptable since I already have Fake Out, Wide Guard, Quick Guard and Intimidate for protection. I rejected Garchomp (18, 4x Ice, physical, overlaps Mamoswine) and Aegislash (16, adds a second Fire/Ground-weak Steel, worsening my documented weakness). Holding the spare 4 points and 5 swaps for later windows.

offers.offerReasoning: Hold. 100/100 means any real upgrade (Incin 18, Arcanine 11, Palafin 12) requires selling Rilla or Sneasler to stay legal. Those 19s are the offense; 0-4 is bring/pilot, not a hole. W3 is a set/bring problem already solved (Inteleon Ice Mence, box Sneasler). Combat/Rotom/Inteleon only fetch junk. Do not arm W3 glm or W6 muse. Win glm and luna with this roster.

No credible mutually beneficial legal trade is available. The core remains intact, and low-cost bench swaps for meaningful Grass/Ground or Electric-pressure upgrades are unlikely to be accepted; avoid a panic transaction before Week 3.

offers.message: Straight value upgrade for you: my Mega Salamence (20) for your Incineroar (18). You get the biggest piece I can move — Aerilate Mega, 145 Atk / 120 Spe, a fast physical win-condition your current six doesn't really have, and it bodies sun/fast teams. You also bank 11 cap going into the final window (you'd sit at 89/100) to grab a free agent. You can always re-add Incineroar-tier support cheaply; a 20-point Mega is the hard thing to acquire. First accept takes it.
offers.responseReasoning: Reject: Incin is 4/4-games linchpin and W3 lead vs Scrafty+Talon with FlareBlitz vs MMeta, Lariat vs Arch/Indeedee, FakeOut/PartingShot/WoW. Board has only 3 Intimidate+FakeOut mons (Incin/Scrafty/M-Scrafty) and Scrafty is on deepseek, so cannot re-add cheaply. Trade leaves zero Fire types, adds 2nd Mega competing with Clefable-Mega for one mega slot, Dragapult 142 Spe already faster physical than Sala 120, and bank drops 13 to 11 while strengthening week7 rival.

offers.message: Simple value flip: my Toxtricity (6) for your Rotom-Frost (4). We're in mirror positions — you've registered Frost twice without fielding it, I've held Tox twice without fielding it — but the board prices Tox 6 over Frost 4, so you net +2 in value and pick up a Punk Rock spread nuke (Shift Gear / Boomburst / Overdrive) for your special cores. You'd sit at 98/100 with room for the final window. Fair for both sides — take it and we both upgrade a dead slot.
offers.responseReasoning: Rotom-Frost is not a dead slot for my remaining schedule: Ice 4x on Noivern (W3), Salamence/Salamence-Mega (W4/W5), Electric 2x on Skarmory/Corviknight/Palafin/Basculegion, plus Levitate Ground-immunity and no Psychic weakness for W6's Psychic Terrain. Toxtricity adds 2x Ground and 2x Psychic weaknesses, 75 Speed and 70/70 bulk, and Boomburst hits its own ally. Cost is the league's real currency: accepting takes me 96->98 spent, blocking the final-window Toxicroak (4, free agent) that gives Fake Out + Dry Skin Water-immunity (Palafin/Azumarill W5, rain W6) and anti-Fairy duty beside my 4x-Fairy-weak Scrafty/Hydreigon; rejecting keeps me at 96 so I can run Frost + Toxicroak at 100/100. Also, entrant 1 is my Week 5 opponent: this deals away the Salamence-Mega answer they must respect and hands them an Ice/Electric body that hits my Primarina/Talonflame/Hydreigon super-effectively. Expected gain does not cover the typing, weakness, and budget losses.

offers.offerReasoning: No trade improves this roster. I sit at 96/100 with 10 mons; every other coach is at 100/100 spent except muse (87), and since both post-trade rosters must be <=100, a cap-locked counterparty can only receive a mon costing <= the one it gives — restricting me to lateral swaps of my 1-4 cost bodies for their 1-4 cost bodies (qwilfish 2, gliscor 3, sceptile 3, mawile 2, pincurchin 4, glalie-mega 4, overqwil 4, dragalge 3, clawitzer 4, houndoom 1). None of those beats the free-agent Toxicroak (4) I can still sign in window 3 to fill my two real gaps: a second Fake Out, Dry Skin Water-immunity (Palafin/Azumarill in W5, rain in W6) and a Poison STAB/Fairy-resist body beside my 4x-Fairy-weak Scrafty and Hydreigon. The pieces that would genuinely fix my live weaknesses (redirection; a Tailwind-independent fast Fire/Ice answer) all cost >=9 and would require surrendering a core piece (Arcanine 11 / Mamoswine 12 / Hydreigon 14 / Primarina 15 / Talonflame 15 / Metagross 17) or exceed 100. The only coach who could absorb a cost increase is muse at 87 — my Week 3 opponent — and the only pieces of theirs I could legally obtain (needing an 11+ core piece back) are not worth arming my next opponent with Intimidate/physical support. Since I face every remaining coach except grok and gemini, no free-lunch counterparty exists. Plan: hold 96/100, then in the final window drop Manectric (1) and add Toxicroak (4) to reach 99/100 with no core loss.
Null encoding broken (string null rejected); sacrificial legal-but-rejectable offer to preserve roster: give dead Mawile2 for core Primarina15 gap13, must be rejected, keeps 87 core for W3.
offers.responseReasoning: Primarina (15) is a core, proven piece: Dragon-immune special wall, Ice Beam 4x vs Dragonite/Salamence/Noivern, and my endgame closer; she is a near-lock in five of my remaining matchups. Mawile (2) is a base-form Steel/Fairy (50/85/85/55/55/50) that is slow, weak, and contributes nothing I lack — I already have Metagross for the Steel role and no need for budget space. Freeing 13 points has no value because I cannot convert them into a better win condition, and I would drop to a worse roster. Worse, the offer is from entrant 0, my Week 3 opponent: accepting hands them my best answer to their Dragon-types (Noivern/Dragapult) while they keep everything else. Clear reject.

offers.offerReasoning: No further offer: keep 87 core for W3, Mawile +13 bank for final FA Fairy/Fire upgrade.

offers.message: Even 6-for-6: Mega Steelix for Swampert. You only ever run one mega, but on weeks Charizard-Y is a bad matchup (rain teams, Rock/Electric-heavy rosters) Mega Steelix gives you a second mega option: 250 base Def, Sand Force, Ground/Steel STAB, Electric immune - a natural Raichu/Gholdengo partner that walls Dragonite, Metagross, Talonflame and Mamoswine-type physical attackers. Un-mega'd it still has Sturdy + Ground STAB for the same Steel/Electric targets Swampert covers, and your Water coverage stays with Tauros-Aqua. No price change either side.
offers.offerReasoning: Steelix is unbrought filler; Swampert is a piece I would actually bring (Ground answer to Raichu/Toxtricity/Archaludon/Electric terrain, Wide Guard) and it is my week-3 opponent's every-game bring, so acceptance removes their Wide Guard/HHP partner for Charizard-Y. Equal cost keeps both rosters at 100. Low acceptance odds but zero downside; free-agent Kleavor plan stays available via a Glalie drop if this goes through.
offers.responseReasoning: Swampert is a 4-0 core starter providing non-Mega Wide Guard, Electric immunity, and Flip Turn pivoting that synergizes perfectly with Mega Charizard Y's Drought. Mega Steelix creates Mega-slot conflict with Charizard Y, is crippled by sun-boosted Fire attacks, lacks Wide Guard, and trading Swampert to our direct Week 3 opponent directly remedies their team weaknesses while sabotaging our planned Week 3 six.

offers.offerReasoning: Swampert offer rejected. No other coach-owned Pokémon at Steelix/Glalie price would be brought over the current core (Gengar, Kingambit, Houndoom, Rotom-W, Altaria, Greninja, Kanga, Salamence). Standing pat per franchise plan; the optional Steelix -> Kleavor upgrade is a free-agent move, not a coach trade.

Keep the roster this trade window. No budget-legal exchange offers a clear multi-week improvement over the functions surrendered. Maushold for Primarina is affordable for both teams, but removes our only Follow Me/Friend Guard support, adds Water overlap with Empoleon, and gives a remaining opponent valuable redirection. Trading Hydrapple for Swampert would gain Wide Guard but sacrifice our strongest existing Water resistance and Grass pressure while strengthening the league leader. Preserve Whimsicott/Drill offense, Chandelure's independent Imprison mode, and optional MausApe support. The immediate rain matchup warrants testing Hydrapple/Empoleon/Whimsicott rather than dismantling these options; evaluate any targeted free-agent improvement separately.

Our roster is 4-0 (Rank 1) with zero game losses. The 10-Pokémon roster is perfectly balanced across weather control, spread nullification, anti-priority, redirection, and offensive pressure. No trades are necessary or beneficial at this window.

moves.reasoning: Hold. 4 swaps left, one window after this. At 100/100 every 11+ FA (Gyarados, H-Arcanine, Garchomp, Mawile-Mega) requires selling Rilla/Sneasler/Clef/Grimm/DN. Combat+Rotom+Inteleon+Altaria cannot legally fund Gyarados without also cutting Inteleon or Dirge and Altaria — illegal for W3 Ice Mence, W4 Cloud Nine/Snipe, W7 sun. W3 is a bring/set problem, not a roster hole. Do not panic-churn.

Replace the repeatedly vulnerable rain-dependent Basculegion with fast Ground pressure and Electric immunity. This preserves the rain engine's Pelipper/Archaludon core while materially improving Rotom, Empoleon, and Excadrill matchups; the remaining six roster pieces stay intact.

Both trade offers were rejected; converting dead weight via FA instead. Drop Mence-M (20; 0 games in 2 weeks, benched W3, and vs W4 gemini EQ is 0x vs Zard-Y / DEdge only 1x) for Baxcalibur-M (15): Ice/Dragon dual STAB — Icicle Crash 46.5-141% through Multiscale on grok's DNite-M this week, resists DNite-M Ice (Ice-vs-Ice 0.5x) and Fire Blast (0.5x), Thermal Exchange punishes Fire hits, 87 Spe TR-friendly, no self-hail; Freeze-Dry/Icy Wind utility. Drop Palafin (12; never registered) for Cofagrigus (5): sim anomaly Psychic 0x vs Ghost makes it the W5 Metagross-M wall (immune to Zen Headbutt, Shadow Ball 2x back), third Trick Room setter (learnset confirmed), Will-O-Wisp/Night Shade support. Resulting roster 88/100, exactly 10, no species conflicts; 4 swaps + 12 cap held for window 3. W3 six unchanged (Farig/Corv/Hatt/Garg core, Bax-M now the premium DNite-M flex over Azu/Drag).

Manectric (1) is my only genuinely dead slot (Lightning Rod tech already covered by Mamoswine's Electric immunity), so converting it to Toxicroak (4) costs me just 3 net and lands a role-dense upgrade. Verified Toxicroak learns Fake Out, Quick Guard, Sucker Punch, Upper Hand, Poison Jab/Gunk Shot/Sludge Wave, Drain Punch, Close Combat, Knock Off, Rock Slide, Taunt, Swords Dance, Bulk Up, Ice Punch and Coaching, and has Dry Skin (Water immunity, +1/4 heal). It gives me the second Fake Out my tempo plan lacks, a Water-immune anti-rain body for W5 (Palafin/Azumarill/Clawitzer) and W6 (Pelipper/Basculegion), Water immunity + 4x Fighting vs Kingambit for W4, and Poison STAB 2x on every Fairy with a Fairy 0.5x resist beside my 4x-Fairy-weak Scrafty/Hydreigon. Budget stays legal at 99/100 with 10 mons. Bigger swings were examined and rejected: Metagross-Mega->Salamence-Mega (20) is worse vs my schedule (muse Electric, luna rain/Ice, astra Weavile) and loses my Poison-immune wincon; Sinistcha (18) would cost Hydreigon (14) at exactly 100 and drop my Ground-immune Dark Pulse answer plus second Tailwind; every other >=5 add requires replacing a core piece. Keeping the remaining 4 swaps for window 3 since no lateral move beats this one.

Mawile never brought; Tinkaton same Steel/Fairy typing with 85/105 bulk, 94 Spe, Mold Breaker, FakeOut/RockSlide/Knock/IceHammer/Gigaton/PlayRough covering Talon/MMeta/Prim/Scrafty/Hydreigon/Rotom-F. 96/100 banks 4 and saves 3 swaps for mega-heavy W5/W7.

glm dropped Mega Salamence (20). Upgrading our base Salamence (11) to the Mega gives a second premier mega option (Intimidate -> Aerilate 145 Atk/130 Def/154-189 Spe) for matchups where Gengar-Mega is a liability (Dark/Ground/Foul Play teams), replacing a Sash Salamence that has done nothing in games. Funded by downgrading Kangaskhan-Mega (15) to base Kangaskhan (7): we have never mega-evolved Kanga, only used its Scrappy Fake Out, so no lost function. Glalie-Mega (4, never brought) -> Lycanroc-Midday (3): fast Rock Slide/Accelerock priority chip for Charizard-Y/Talonflame/Noivern/Dragapult/Pelipper. Roster stays 100/100, one swap held for the final window. Steelix kept as the Trick Room/Electric wall filler.

Keep all ten at 100/100. Luna replacing Basculegion with Garchomp materially reduces the immediate need to purchase Water immunity and increases the value of our existing Weavile, Whimsicott, Intimidate and redirection options. Prepare for Archaludon/Pelipper/Indeedee/Gardevoir plus Garchomp, not the obsolete Swift Swim matchup. Compared concrete packages: Maushold->Vivillon and Tauros->Mr. Mime fits exactly and adds Wide Guard/secondary Tailwind/sleep, but replacing Follow Me with powder redirection is a substantial downgrade against the remaining Grass users, and Vivillon adds exploitable Flying/Fire/Rock weaknesses. Maushold->Gyarados plus Tauros->Mr. Mime costs 99 and adds Water offense/Wide Guard while retaining Intimidate, but loses our only redirection and Friend Guard, and Gyarados is particularly exposed to Archaludon and muse's Electric core. Chandelure->Mr. Mime is affordable but sacrifices independent Imprison/Protect denial and strong Fire/Ghost offense for another support slot; Wide Guard alone is insufficient against adaptable single-target attacks. Preserve the coherent Tailwind/Drill, optional MausApe and Chandelure modes rather than reacting to two weeks' usage alone. Six swaps remain available for the final window; reassess using the updated W3 matchup and actual deployment of Maushold/Hydrapple.

Franchise is 4-0 (Rank 1, zero game losses). The roster provides flawless strategic cohesion, dual weather/speed control, unblockable Intimidate, redirection, untrappable Ghost coverage, spread nullification, and priority blocking. Retaining all 10 Pokémon and preserving all 6 season swaps for Window 3.

offers.message: Morpeko for Rotom, straight swap. Rotom gives me a flexible Levitate pivot and I’m offering a low-cost reserve I’m unlikely to register; this also preserves your 100-point roster total.
offers.offerReasoning: Offer the only clean equal-price upgrade to a full-budget roster: replace expendable Morpeko with generic Rotom for flexible Levitate/pivot utility. Keep all central pieces and preserve legal budgets.
offers.responseReasoning: Reject. W4 is luna; Rotom is the locked Pelipper answer (Tbolt 4x, Wacan once) and Levitate vs Garchomp EQ. Morpeko is also Electric but 70 SpA vs Rotom 95, no Levitate (EQ 2x), Hunger Switch gimmick, and luna never registered it. Trading the rain answer to the rain opponent the week we play them is a strip, not an upgrade. HOLD through W4. Cut Rotom only after W4 for a real upgrade.

offers.message: Offer: Mega Gardevoir for Grimmsnarl, equal 16 points. Gardevoir gives you a powerful immediate Fairy attacker alongside Dragonite/Clefable, while Grimmsnarl gives me the screens, Prankster disruption, and speed-control flexibility my roster currently lacks. This should improve both rosters without changing budget.
offers.offerReasoning: Grimmsnarl directly addresses our persistent speed-control and positioning deficits, while retaining Fairy utility; Mega Gardevoir is powerful but repeatedly exposed and is more replaceable than our core attackers.
offers.responseReasoning: Reject. Equal cost, not equal roles. Grimm is the only Dark (Psychic 0 vs Indeedee), Light Clay Prankster screens, and Spirit Break; locked for W4 default 6 and called for W5 Beat Up/Rage Fist and W6 Incin/Drill. Mega Garde is a second mega that conflicts with Dragoninite (one mega/game), and Pixilate HV is Imprison-locked while luna’s Indeedee lives — so in W4 Garde is either benched behind DN or a HV attacker who cannot click HV. Accepting hands luna the screens/Prankster they lack and strips our W4 Indeedee/Garchomp tool the week we play them. W7 Gholdengo is 4x into Garde. Clef already covers Fairy. Not a panic-trade; HOLD.

offers.offerReasoning: HOLD. 0-3 is bring/pilot, not a hole; W4 kit (Altaria Cloud Nine, Inteleon Snipe, Rotom 4x Peli, Rilla terrain) is already on the 100. 0 spare points so any 1-for-1 is equal or down; premium Intimidate (Incin/Arcanine) cannot fit without giving locked core, and bidding Sneasler/Rilla/Clef/Grimm into W4–W6 opponents is how we donate a win. Keep Combat/Inteleon/Rotom; refuse junk. Let inbound offers come.

offers.message: Equal 3-for-3 swap of benched support mons. Skarmory gives you Sturdy Steel/Flying with TW/Taunt/IronHead/RockSlide — resists Dragon/Hurricane/Espeed, IronHead vs Fairy, Rock vs Fire/Fly, fits Arch/Pelipper/Garde cores. Gliscor hasn't been registered for you the last 2 weeks. Helps us try Ground/Flying EQ immunity. Both stay legal.
offers.offerReasoning: 1-2 must-win W4 vs Astra MExca/Heat/Weavile. Skarm never brought, Sturdy ignored by MoldBreaker Pierce, weak to Heat Fire/Electric. Gliscor Ground/Flying immune EQ/Tbolt, EQ SE vs Heat/MExca/Chandelure/Empoleon, resists Ape Fighting, learns TW/Knock/Toxic. Equal cost 96/99 stay legal, no duplicate species. Luna 0-3 already played (no backfire), Gliscor benched by them, Skarm offers Dragon/Fairy wall they lack.
offers.responseReasoning: Accepting the 3-point swap: Skarmory adds a durable Steel/Flying Fairy- and Dragon-resistant option plus Tailwind/Taunt, directly improving the upcoming Clefable/Grimmsnarl/Mega Dragonite matchup. Gliscor is redundant with Garchomp's Ground role and has not been registered recently.

offers.message: Dead-slot swap of benched 4s: Overqwil gives you a fresh Intimidate cycler (115 Atk Dark/Poison, Poison Jab for Whimsi/Clef/Garde, Crunch for Ghosts/Pult, Swift Swim option) to pair with Arcanine/Mamo physical core. Toxicroak is 0 games for you, Overqwil 0 for us. Equal 4-4 keeps both legal. Accept?
offers.offerReasoning: Upgrade dead Overqwil (weak to Whimsi Fairy, no FakeOut) to Toxicroak (Poison 4x Whimsi, Fighting 2x MExca/Weavile/Empoleon/Kingambit, FakeOut/Drain/Sucker, Dry Skin vs Wash) for must-win W4 Astra + W5 Wash/Kingambit + Rilla/Azu. Equal 4-4 keeps us 96 both legal. Past opponent no future matchup safest target.
offers.responseReasoning: Reject. Overqwil (4) for Toxicroak (4) is cost-neutral but a competitive downgrade for my remaining slate. Confirmed Overqwil = Dark/Poison 85/115/95/65/65/85, abilities Intimidate/Poison Point/Swift Swim; Toxicroak = Poison/Fighting Dry Skin with Fake Out, Quick Guard, Fighting STAB, Sucker Punch, Knock Off. My bench needs Tempo/coverage, not a third Intimidate user behind Arcanine and Scrafty. Overqwil's Intimidate is actively bad into the two Defiant foes left on my schedule (Kingambit, W4; Annihilape, W7) — it hands them +2 Atk. Its Poison Jab is 0x vs Kingambit and its Dark moves are 0.5x, so it cannot touch claude's #2 threat at all, and it is 2x weak to the Ground that saturates this league. Toxicroak does the things I actually use: Fake Out tempo, Dry Skin Water immunity (Rotom-Wash/Greninja in W4, luna's rain in W6), and Fighting STAB that is 4x on Kingambit (W4) and Weavile (W7) plus Poison Jab 2x on Whimsicott/Altaria-Mega/Gardevoir. The offer also just imports a useful tool to a rival at no gain to me. No add for <=12 improves on what I hold; HOLD.

offers.offerReasoning: Budget is 100/100 so any trade must be cost-neutral or downward; nothing cheap on other rosters beats the undrafted Hippowdon (5), Krookodile (9), Goodra-Hisui (6) that the franchise plan targets in the signing phase (drop Steelix 6, Kangaskhan 7, Greninja 7). Deepseek's Scrafty is unreachable legally (their roster is at 99; only Lycanroc matches cost and I keep it). No offer keeps plans hidden from week-4 opponent.

offers.message: Even 6-for-6 swap: my Toxtricity for your Chandelure. Toxtricity gives your speed-tempo pool the special Electric nuke it currently lacks — Punk Rock Overdrive hits Steel and Water boards 2x (Gholdengo, Primarina, Mamoswine types) and pairs well with Weavile/Excadrill-M pressure. offers.offerReasoning: Free option on a cold market (3 rejections, 1 accept so far): convert dead 6-pt Toxtricity (fielded zero times all season) into astra's Chandelure — 145-SpA Fire/Ghost TR-native nuke filling my stated "cheap Fire attacker" gap (W5 Metagross-M/Mamoswine/Talonflame, W6 Kingambit, W4 Gholdengo all 2x), and if accepted it removes the Imprison lead that beat me 0-2 in W2 from my likeliest playoff opponent's roster. offers.message: Offering Maushold for Primarina. Friend Guard + Follow Me gives your Metagross, Mamoswine and Hydreigon a new support mode alongside Talonflame's Tailwind; Super Fang and Helping Hand also support immediate offense without requiring setup. I gain a bulky special Water/Fairy attacker, while you retain special offense through Hydreigon and Rotom-Frost. Your resulting roster costs 100; mine costs 99. Both remain at ten Pokémon.
offers.offerReasoning: Maushold is our largest unused investment, but losing Friend Guard/redirection has real cost. Primarina supplies independent special offense, Water resistance and substantial Fairy damage without competing for Mega evolution. Useful into W4 Incineroar/Noivern and W7's roster; W5 Rillaboom/Sneasler and W6 sun limit it, so retain existing Fire/Ice/speed-control modes rather than promise universal usage. Whimsicott/Weavile retain optional Beat Up for Annihilape. Entrant5 currently costs99, making this unequal-price exchange legal at100 for them and99 for us. Their new redirection is a W7 risk, but this addresses a roster role more directly than our unused support slot and does not strengthen tied title rival entrant7.
offers.responseReasoning: REJECT. Maushold is a legitimate support mon (111 Spe, Friend Guard, Follow Me, Encore/Taunt/Feint/Helping Hand/Super Fang), but the price is Primarina — my proven core and the one piece I cannot replace. She is my only Dragon-immune special wall and 4x Ice Beam answer (Dragonite-Mega, Salamence-Mega, Altaria-Mega, Garchomp recur across the league), hard-walls Greninja, and is central to the W4 claude plan (Moonblast 2x on both his Megas, resists Rotom-Wash, immune Dragon). My two losses/friction points this season were speed-vs-Charizard problems, not a lack of redirection; Follow Me does nothing about that, and Normal-typed Maushold also can't touch Gengar-Mega (0x). Giving Primarina to entrant 4 arms my Week 7 opponent against my own bulky-offence core. Net: I trade a top-3 producer for a bench player its own owner has never once brought in three weeks, and pin myself at exactly 100/100 with zero flexibility. Declining preserves my roster for the matchups it was built for.

Losing unique redirection/Friend Guard is meaningful, and Muse gains real support, but acquiring its currently unbrought speed threat improves our offensive flexibility without strengthening the tied title rival. Both rosters retain ten distinct species and cost 98. Two points of headroom also preserve final-window free-agent flexibility if available.

Shortened replacement after total-memory validation rejection; no battle results invented.

I rewrote the plan, roster, playbook, transactions and meta pages to describe the 10 mons I actually own, gave Sylveon a concrete role (Pixilate Hyper Voice spread, 130 SpD Dragon-immune wall, Dark-resist, 2x vs Dark/Dragon/Fighting), and rebuilt every remaining-week answer around it. Reconciled the permanent memory after the Week 3 window: removed Mega Gardevoir and Gliscor, recorded the completed exchange, added Skarmory and Mega Mawile with role guidance, and updated the plan and remaining matchup priorities.

W3 lost same4 passive into Talon TW, Exca speed loss, CC drops, Protect fail, recoil suicide. Updated plan with fixes, added MegaExca Pierce tech from astra scout, set W4 bring/lead vs Weavile/MExca/BeatUp core and hold bank.

W4 draft: Farig+Garg lead, Hatt+Cofag back, Corv benched vs Zard-Y.

Added Fairy-vs-Fairy 1x and archived Bax lessons.

decisions.rationale: Lead Incin+Noivern for Fake Out into Venusaur to stop Sleep Powder and Tailwind to outrun Chlorophyll sun. Back Ceruledge Flash Fire wall/sweeper and Garchomp Rock Slide vs Zard/Dnite with EQ+Noivern immunity synergy.

Lead Dragonite and Gholdengo with Swampert and Mega Charizard Y in reserve. Dragonite's Inner Focus blocks Fake Out and Intimidate, while Gholdengo is immune to Fake Out and outspeeds the entire opposing team with Choice Scarf (223 Spe). This completely shuts down Incineroar/Garchomp lead pressure while threatening an immediate OHKO on Garchomp with 4x Ice Spinner and spread pressure with Make It Rain. Swampert provides Wide Guard and Ice Punch in the back, while Mega Charizard Y brings immense special nuclear offense.

Fake Out useless (Gholdengo Ghost immune, Dnite InnerFocus no flinch). Noivern Tailwind now risks double-target KO through sash (Espeed 31-45% + ShadowBall 42-61%). Protect preserves sash/TW for T2 while Incin Flare Blitz threatens 74-134% OHKO range on Gholdengo (better than Lariat 52-96%).

Gholdengo is heavily threatened by Incineroar's Flare Blitz / Darkest Lariat, so we switch Gholdengo out to Swampert who resists Fire and takes minimal damage. Dragonite targets Noivern with 4x Ice Spinner to break its Focus Sash, positioning Dragonite to finish Noivern next turn with Extreme Speed (+2 priority) regardless of whether Noivern sets Tailwind. Wide Guard on Swampert will also neutralize any Garchomp spread moves if opponent relies on Tailwind speed.

Tailwind is free: Noivern 192 outruns Dnite 100-132 and Swampert 80-112, only Espeed 31-45% goes first and cannot KO from full, WideGuard does not block Tailwind. Incin at 92% risks HighHorsepower 69-102% but Lariat neutral 25-46% into weakened Swampert is best chip; Flare Blitz NVE did only 25%. Get speed up now before Zard/Venu come in.

Noivern's Protect chance is drastically reduced after turn 1. Dragonite targets Noivern with 4x Ice Spinner to break its Focus Sash, preparing an Extreme Speed finish on turn 3. Swampert targets Incineroar with STAB super-effective High Horsepower to heavily damage or KO Incineroar (66-121% damage against 91% HP), removing the opponent's Intimidate pivot. Both Dragonite and Swampert have high bulk and easily survive incoming attacks this turn.

Incin 26% dies to any Ground/Water hit (HighHorse 69-102%) but still has Intimidate value, so switch first to Ceru which walls Dnite (Espeed immune, Ice 16-23%) and resists Ice Punch. Noivern 1% sash gone has no future TW value vs Espeed, so sack it to Taunt Dnite (384 TW speed outruns 100-132) to deny their Tailwind and preserve our speed edge for Ceru/Garchomp sweep.
Forced double replacement: only Incin 26% and Garchomp 100% remain. Restore Incin to slot A and Garchomp to slot B to keep Tailwind offense alive.

Dragonite's Extreme Speed (+2 priority) guarantees the KO on 1% HP Noivern before it can act (Air Slash/Taunt). Swampert's High Horsepower guarantees the KO on 26% HP Incineroar while remaining on the field, which preserves Wide Guard to completely wall Garchomp's spread moves on turn 4 even through opposing Tailwind.

Incin re-entered so Fake Out works and at 160 TW outruns Swampert to flinch WideGuard/attack before it moves. Garchomp dies to IceSpinner 97-138% + IcePunch 51-75% if it attacks, so Protect (+4 beats Espeed +2) to stay full. Sac Incin after Fake Out value to preserve Garchomp for last TW turn.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Dragonite)
decisions.rationale: Swampert uses Wide Guard (+3 priority), which blocks all three of Garchomp's attacking moves (Rock Slide, Earthquake, Breaking Swipe are all spread moves). This guarantees Dragonite cannot be double-targeted down by Darkest Lariat + Breaking Swipe, ensuring Dragonite survives and lands 4x Ice Spinner to OHKO Garchomp. Even if Incineroar Fakes Out Swampert to flinch Wide Guard, Dragonite easily survives Garchomp's Breaking Swipe from 100% HP to retaliate with Ice Spinner.

No bench so Parting Shot just debuffs. Debuff Dnite -1 before its IceSpinner (Incin 160 TW outruns 100-132) to turn 97-138% OHKO into survivable, plus Breaking Swipe spread -1 Atk to both foes for max survival vs double Ice. Beats Rock Slide damage because survival matters more at 1 turn TW left; WideGuard blocks either spread but Parting Shot still lands.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Dragonite)
decisions.rationale: Swampert uses Wide Guard (+3 priority), which cannot be flinched this turn (Incineroar already consumed Fake Out). Wide Guard 100% blocks all three of Garchomp's attacking moves (Breaking Swipe, Rock Slide, Earthquake), ensuring Dragonite takes at most single-target damage from 26% Incineroar. Dragonite at 100% HP easily survives and lands 4x Ice Spinner to OHKO Garchomp. Opponent's Tailwind ends this turn.
Position lost: 26%+20% no Tailwind vs 87%+53% plus 2 fresh including Scarf Gholdengo, Garchomp spread walled by WideGuard and 4x Ice weak, no bench. Forfeit unwinnable game1 to focus series.

reflections.summary: G1 loss: expected sun lead but got Dnite+Gholdengo into Swampert. FakeOut dead into Ghost/InnerFocus, Protect stalled T1 but T2 Tailwind cost Noivern sash and Incin Sitrus. Ceru switch-in OHKOed by HH, Noivern picked by Espeed, leaving Incin+Garchomp vs Dnite+Swampert. Garchomp all-spread walled by WideGuard and 4x Ice weak (97-138% Spinner), Tailwind expired for loss. Adjust to Clefable+Rotom over Garchomp+Ceru.
reflections.adjustment: Drop Garchomp+Ceruledge (all Garchomp damage spread walled by WideGuard and 4x Ice weak; Ceru OHKOed by High Horsepower and 76-110% to Shadow Ball). Bring Mega Clefable FollowMe + Rotom-Mow instead. Keep Incin+Noivern lead core but back with Clefable/Rotom: Fake Out Swampert stops WideGuard/attack, Tailwind goes up on sash, Rotom Leaf Storm deletes Swampert through WideGuard (single-target) and Levitate immunes High Horsepower, Clefable redirects/bounces and Moonblasts Dragonite.

reflections.summary: Game 1 was a decisive victory. Leading Dragonite + Gholdengo completely disarmed the opponent's Fake Out / Intimidate strategy. Pivoting Gholdengo to Swampert absorbed Incineroar's Flare Blitz, while Dragonite broke Noivern's Sash with Ice Spinner. Turn 3 produced a double KO as Dragonite cleaned Noivern with +2 Extreme Speed and Swampert OHKOed switching Ceruledge with High Horsepower. Swampert's Wide Guard then completely blocked Garchomp's Breaking Swipe on Turn 5 while Dragonite chunked Garchomp to 20%, prompting an immediate concession on Turn 6 with our entire team alive (4v2).
reflections.adjustment: Stick to the winning Dragonite + Gholdengo lead with Swampert and Mega Charizard Y in reserve. Be prepared for opponent to bring Clefable-Mega or Rotom-Mow to counter Swampert; Gholdengo's Make It Rain and Charizard's Sun-boosted Fire moves hard counter both adjustments.
