decisions.rationale: Bring Machamp/Mamoswine/Talonflame/Primarina; bench Scrafty and Arcanine. Scrafty is near-dead here (Fake Out fails on Ghost Gholdengo and is useless vs Inner Focus Dragonite; Intimidate feeds Passimian's Defiant). Arcanine is 2x weak to Swampert's Ground/Water and has no good hit on Charizard. Lead Machamp+Mamoswine: Wide Guard blanks BOTH of their spread moves (sun Heat Wave + scarf Make It Rain) while Mamoswine's Ice Shard (4x) or Machamp's No-Guard Stone Edge (4x) claims a KO on Dragonite or Charizard turn 1. Talonflame in back for Tailwind (needed: scarf Gholdengo eff 223 > my 178). Primarina in back as my only clean Swampert answer (Energy Ball 4x) plus Dragon immunity and Moonblast for Passimian, kept off the field while Venusaur/Gholdengo are alive. Charizard is doubly answered (Stone Edge + Rock Slide); Gholdengo handled by Machamp Knock Off/High Horsepower (2x, and Knock Off strips the Scarf).

DeepSeek brought Scrafty, Talonflame, Arcanine, Mamoswine, Primarina, and Machamp (leaving Mega Metagross and Sinistcha out). Passimian + Gholdengo lead provides maximum tactical control: Passimian's Defiant punishes Scrafty/Arcanine Intimidates, Quick Guard blocks Fake Out / Gale Wings Brave Bird / Extreme Speed / Ice Shard, while Choice Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) outspeeds their entire team and is immune to Fake Out and Fighting STAB. Charizard and Swampert provide supreme mid-to-late game closing power with Drought and Wide Guard.

selection: Wide Guard (your side, including ally Mamoswine)
decisions.rationale: They led Passimian + Gholdengo (not the expected Dragonite lead). Machamp uses Wide Guard to blank scarf Gholdengo's Make It Rain, which is confirmed to do 88.5-128.1% to Mamoswine even through the spread penalty (and 37.1-53.3% to Machamp). I switch Mamoswine out to Talonflame because the two natural 2x clicks both OHKO it: Passimian Close Combat 85.7-125.3% and Gholdengo Focus Blast 79.3-114.3%. Talonflame resists both (0.5x), so if they fire at the Mamoswine slot the damage whiffs, and Machamp (survives any single hit: CC 47.7-70.1%, MIR 37-53%, plus Sitrus) stays near full. Talonflame also gives speed control next turn and a 2x Flare Blitz (69.1-127.2%) into Gholdengo. Keeping Mamoswine in for a coin-flip High Horsepower (97.9-178.4% on Gholdengo) risks losing my only 4x answer to Charizard/Dragonite; preserving it is worth the tempo.

Turn 1 went badly: they double-targeted the slot I switched into, and Talonflame (Shadow Ball 72% + resisted Close Combat) is gone. Wide Guard blocked nothing since they led with Shadow Ball, not Make It Rain. So I bring Primarina rather than Mamoswine: on this exact board she tanks both foes (Passimian Close Combat 0.5x, Knock Off 0.5x; Gholdengo is Choice-locked into 1x Shadow Ball for ~38%), and her Moonblast is 2x on the now -1 SpD Passimian, which breaks its Focus Sash and sets up a kill next turn. Bringing Mamoswine here would walk it straight into Passimian's 2x Close Combat (85.7-125.3%, likely a lost mon) which is my only 4x answer to Charizard/Dragonite — I keep it benched. Machamp Passes (only legal option); keeping Machamp untouched matters because Wide Guard is my sole Heat Wave/Make It Rain answer.

Gholdengo (223 Spe) and Passimian (145 Spe) both outspeed Adamant Mamoswine (max 132 Spe) and Machamp (max 107 Spe). Mamoswine carries Life Orb and lacks Protect. Machamp possesses Wide Guard, which would completely nullify Make It Rain. Single-target focus fire into Mamoswine with Shadow Ball (35-67%) followed by Passimian's Close Combat (81.1-149.2%) guarantees an unblockable, 100% accurate KO (116.1% minimum total) before Mamoswine can move, completely bypassing Wide Guard and removing opposing Ground/Ice pressure immediately.

Both of their mons are weak into my current board (Gholdengo is Choice-locked into 1x Shadow Ball; Passimian's CC is only 1x on Machamp and 0.5x on Primarina), so I press the kill. Primarina Moonblast is 2x on Passimian AND Passimian is at -1 SpD, so it consumes the Focus Sash (Passimian -> 1 HP); Machamp then finishes with Knock Off (0.5x but any hit kills a 1-HP target) which also strips the Sash/item and, unlike Close Combat, does not drop Machamp's own defenses. I deliberately do NOT Knock Off Gholdengo: removing its Scarf would also free it from the Shadow Ball lock, and 114-149 Speed still outruns all my remaining mons, so keeping it locked into a 1x move is better than chipping it. Wide Guard is useless this turn (Shadow Ball is single-target), so Machamp attacks; attacking also resets its protection counter, giving a reliable Wide Guard next turn against Charizard's Heat Wave. Killing Passimian also removes Quick Guard (which would blank Mamoswine's Ice Shard) and unblocks Mamoswine from entering (its CC was a 2x OHKO on Mamoswine).
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Gholdengo (223 Spe) and Passimian (145 Spe) both comfortably outspeed Primarina (max 112 Spe) and Machamp (max 107 Spe). Machamp lacks Protect and cannot block single-target attacks with Wide Guard. Concentrating Gholdengo's Shadow Ball (31-58%) and Passimian's Close Combat (45-84%) into Machamp gives a high probability of eliminating Machamp before it can move. Even if Machamp survives on low HP, Knock Off cannot OHKO Gholdengo from 100% HP (max 92.7%), while Passimian's unrevealed Focus Sash guarantees survival against any incoming Moonblast from Primarina. Switching Mamoswine in would result in a guaranteed KO on switch-in.

Machamp died because I under-weighted Gholdengo's Shadow Ball stacked with Close Combat (43% + 57% = KO, so Sitrus never triggered and Machamp never got to act). Now Mamoswine is my ONLY remaining Charizard answer — nothing else can hit Charizard (primarina Moonblast/Ice Beam are 1x and she cannot touch it) — so it absolutely cannot be traded away. Passimian, even at 1%, still gets a full action and its Close Combat is 2x/OHKO on Mamoswine, and it is faster (110-145 vs 100). The only way to stop it is a priority move, so Mamoswine uses Ice Shard (+1, resolves before all their attacks) to remove Passimian before it can move. Primarina chips Gholdengo with Moonblast (~57, 0.5x) rather than doubling into Passimian: this hedges a Passimian Protect/Quick Guard (where an Ice Shard would be blanked) and the chip converts Mamoswine's High Horsepower into a guaranteed KO on Gholdengo next turn (97.9-178.4% from full is a slight-risk KO, so softening it first). Gholdengo being Choice-locked into 1x Shadow Ball means neither of my mons is in real danger this turn.

Both Gholdengo (223 Spe) and Passimian (145 Spe) outspeed Adamant Mamoswine (max 132 Spe) and Primarina (max 112 Spe). If Mamoswine uses High Horsepower, Rock Slide, or Icicle Crash (priority 0), Shadow Ball (35-67%) combined with Close Combat (81.1-149.2%) guarantees an unblockable KO (116.1% minimum) before Mamoswine can move, completely protecting Gholdengo from High Horsepower. If Mamoswine uses Ice Shard (+1 priority) on Passimian to claim the 1% HP KO, Mamoswine still takes heavy Shadow Ball damage, leaving our full-HP backline (Charizard-Mega-Y and Swampert) to close out against a crippled Mamoswine and Primarina. Double-targeting Mamoswine is strictly superior to Protect or Quick Guard.

Charizard enters cleanly. In slot 2, Gholdengo passes. Next turn, Choice Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) and Mega Charizard Y (152 Spe) both outspeed 40% Mamoswine (max 132 Spe) and Primarina (max 112 Spe). Drought will activate Sun, enabling one-turn Solar Beam and boosted Fire attacks into Primarina, while Gholdengo easily finishes Mamoswine with Shadow Ball.

Charizard just came in and will Mega Evolve into Charizard-Mega-Y (Drought, sun) before moves, so Mamoswine (40%) is likely dead this turn: sun Heat Wave (spread, hits both), Overheat and Solar Beam all OHKO it, and Gholdengo's locked Shadow Ball does 50% (already proved) to finish it. Mamoswine is also slower than both foes (100 vs Charizard 120-152, Gholdengo 171-223), so a non-priority move only lands if they decline to attack it. Given that, Mamoswine's Rock Slide is the single play that can actually win the game: it is 4x on Charizard and KOs it outright (~195-253 with Life Orb, vs Charizard's ~150 HP) while also chipping Gholdengo. Chipping Charizard instead with Ice Shard (~72, 1x) never KOs it and Charizard at 7% is still fully functional (its Solar Beam is 2x on Primarina and Heat Wave KOs Mamoswine), so chip only pays off if Mamoswine survives anyway - the exact case where Rock Slide is strictly better. Primarina's Ice Beam goes at Charizard as insurance for Rock Slide's 10% miss (Moonblast 0.5x and Energy Ball 0.25x are useless here). I hold Mamoswine's Life Orb recoil in mind but there is no switch available for either slot.

Both Choice Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) and Mega Charizard Y (152 Spe) outspeed Mamoswine (max 132 Spe) and Primarina (max 112 Spe). Charizard's Mega Evolution immediately sets Sun via Drought, allowing Solar Beam to execute without charging at 100% accuracy. Gholdengo's Shadow Ball (100% accurate, 35-67%) moves first into Mamoswine; if Mamoswine is still standing, Charizard's Solar Beam (100% accurate, 86.6-167.6%) guarantees the KO. If Mamoswine faints to Shadow Ball, Solar Beam automatically retargets Primarina for 66.3-118.7% super-effective damage. If Mamoswine uses Ice Shard (+1 priority), neither Gholdengo (68% HP) nor Charizard (100% HP) can be KOed.

Mamoswine's Rock Slide never resolved - it was KO'd by Gholdengo's Shadow Ball before its turn (slower than both foes), so the gamble failed and the game is now effectively lost: Primarina is alone at 21% (39 HP) in sun with Charizard-Mega-Y at 66% and scarf Gholdengo at 68%. She is outsped by both and cannot accomplish anything: Gholdengo's locked Shadow Ball (~71, 1x) KOs her before she can move (171-223 vs 80), and Charizard's sun Heat Wave/Overheat/Solar Beam also KO her; meanwhile her own damage is hopeless (Ice Beam is 1x on Charizard for ~69, and every move is 0.5x on Gholdengo). Protect is the only legal move that actually resolves (priority +4, ahead of Gholdengo's Shadow Ball) and therefore the only way to keep her alive for another turn. I play on rather than concede: it costs nothing, keeps the sliver of a chance open, and may reveal their unrevealed 4th bring (Venusaur/Swampert/Dragonite) which is genuinely useful for games 2 and 3 of this series.

Primarina is at 21% HP and is the opponent's sole remaining Pokémon. Choice Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) and Mega Charizard Y (152 Spe) both outspeed Primarina (max 112 Spe). Gholdengo's Shadow Ball (100% accurate, 27.3-47.1%) is a guaranteed KO before Primarina can act unless it Protects. Backed up by Charizard's 100% accurate Solar Beam in Sun, this ensures immediate victory or a guaranteed clean-up next turn through Protect.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: The game is mathematically lost: Primarina (27%, 80 Speed) is the last mon standing against Charizard-Mega-Y (66%) and scarf Gholdengo (68%, still Choice-locked into Shadow Ball). Gholdengo is faster than her (171-223 vs 80), so its 1x Shadow Ball (~71 on her 138 SpD, ~50 HP at 27%) KOs her before she can move - attacking would simply be a no-action. Protect (+4) is the only move that resolves ahead of that and can keep her alive, so it is the only legal action with any upside; note the success rate is now reduced (1/3) since she Protected last turn. I play it out rather than concede because it costs nothing, the game outcome is identical either way, and if Protect holds there is a small chance the opponent pivots to its unrevealed 4th mon (Venusaur/Swampert/Dragonite), which would tell me which four they favour for games 2 and 3. No damage she can deal changes anything: Ice Beam is only 1x (~69) on Charizard and every one of her moves is 0.5x on Gholdengo, and sun-boosted Fire moves plus Solar Beam all KO her anyway.

Primarina used Protect on Turn 5, resulting in heavily degraded Protect success this turn. Gholdengo (223 Spe) and Mega Charizard Y (152 Spe) both outspeed Primarina (max 112 Spe). Gholdengo's 100% accurate Shadow Ball (27.3-47.1%) guarantees a KO on 27% HP Primarina, with Charizard's Solar Beam providing immediate secondary lethal redundancy to secure the Game 1 win.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Position is unchanged in substance: Primarina (33%, 62 HP, 80 Speed) is still the last mon against Charizard-Mega-Y (66%) and scarf Gholdengo (68%, still Choice-locked into Shadow Ball), and Gholdengo is faster than her so its 1x Shadow Ball (~71) KOs her before she can act - selecting an attack would be a no-action. Protect remains the only move with priority +4 that resolves ahead of that, so it is the only legal play that can keep her alive; its success rate is now heavily reduced (third consecutive use), so this is a pure survival/stall roll. I keep playing rather than conceding because a concede and a loss are equivalent for the series, whereas stalling costs nothing and carries two small upsides: the opponent may eventually switch Gholdengo out to reset its Choice lock and thereby reveal their unrevealed 4th bring (Venusaur/Swampert/Dragonite), which is real information for games 2 and 3. No attack changes the outcome: Ice Beam is 1x (~69) on Charizard and every move is 0.5x on Gholdengo.

Primarina has protected twice consecutively (streak 2), giving Protect a negligible chance to succeed. Both Choice Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) and Mega Charizard Y (152 Spe) outspeed Primarina (max 112 Spe). Gholdengo's Shadow Ball (27.3-47.1%) and Charizard's Solar Beam (66.3-118.7%) both independently threaten lethal damage on 33% HP Primarina, concluding Game 1.

reflections.summary: Game 1 lost (0-1) in a game that was decided in the first two turns. I brought Machamp/Mamoswine/Talonflame/Primarina and led Machamp+Mamoswine; the opponent led Passimian+Gholdengo and spent the whole game STACKING both attacks onto a single one of my slots. Turn 1 they killed the mon in slot b (my Mamoswine->Talonflame switch, which was the wrong rescue - Primarina absorbs Shadow Ball 1x and Close Combat 0.5x, Talonflame does not). Turn 2 they killed Machamp with Shadow Ball (112/197) + Close Combat to 0 - its Sitrus never triggered because it was at 57% when the Close Combat landed, and being slower it never got to act. With Machamp gone, Mamoswine became my only Charizard answer, and Gholdengo's Shadow Ball deleted it on the very turn Charizard Mega-evolved into Drought before its Rock Slide could fire. From turn 4 on I was reduced to a Protect-stalling Primarina who could never act (scarf Gholdengo outran her) and could never out-damage Charizard (Ice Beam 1x for ~69 vs Solar Beam 2x for ~84% of her). Two findings from the log change how I should treat this opponent: Wide Guard was near-worthless because they never clicked a spread move - Gholdengo used ONLY Shadow Ball (7 times, Choice-locked all game, never switched out despite the lock) and Charizard used ONLY Solar Beam (4 times; in sun it fires with no charge turn even though it still logs 'charging'). Their entire game is stack-two-attacks-on-one-slot, then let Mega Charizard-Y in sun Solar Beam the Water/Grass-weak targets. They never pivot, never Protect, never spread.
reflections.adjustment: Keep: the reads were all correct and the loss was a play/lead problem, not a plan problem. Machamp's No Guard Stone Edge (4x, never misses) and Mamoswine's Rock Slide (4x) remain my only Charizard answers; Talonflame's Tailwind (178) is still my speed control; Primarina answers only Dragonite (Ice Beam 4x) and Swampert (Energy Ball 4x) and loses to Charizard and Gholdengo. Change the LEAD and the exposure discipline: (1) Do NOT lead Machamp or Mamoswine into their Passimian+Gholdengo lead - they stack Shadow Ball (43%) + Close Combat (57%) on one slot and either of those mons dies before acting. Lead Talonflame + Primarina instead: both take Close Combat at 0.5x and Shadow Ball at 1x, so a double-target is survivable, and I still get Tailwind. (2) Do not switch a frail mon into a slot I expect them to double-target - commit my bulkiest resist to that slot instead (the turn-1 error). (3) Wide Guard is only worth Machamp's turn if a spread move is actually live and likely clicked; here it was a wasted turn twice, and it cost Machamp its offence. (4) Keep Machamp above ~60% before Charizard appears (one sun Overheat is ~163 of 197) and bring it in only to snipe Charizard. (5) Do not Knock Off Gholdengo while it is locked into 1x Shadow Ball - removing the Choice Scarf also frees it to click Make It Rain. (6) Never Intimidate/Snarl Passimian (Defiant).

reflections.summary: Flawless 3-0 victory in Game 1. Anticipting Machamp's Wide Guard against Make It Rain, we utilized single-target focus-fire (Shadow Ball + Close Combat) on slot 2, catching Talonflame on its switch-in for an immediate Turn 1 OHKO. Turn 2 doubled Machamp before it could move, while Passimian's Focus Sash absorbed Primarina's Moonblast. After Mamoswine traded Ice Shard for Passimian, Charizard Mega Evolved to set Sun; Gholdengo finished Mamoswine, and Solar Beam + Shadow Ball swept Primarina to seal the game.
reflections.adjustment: Maintain the Passimian + Gholdengo lead with Mega Charizard Y and Swampert in reserve. DeepSeek will likely rotate in Scrafty and/or Arcanine to leverage Intimidate, but Passimian's Defiant (+2 Atk), Quick Guard (+3 priority blocking Fake Out/Extreme Speed/Brave Bird), and Gholdengo's Ghost immunities hard-counter that exact adjustment. Dragonite remains an elite flex option if DeepSeek leans heavily into Arcanine/Talonflame.

decisions.rationale: Bring Scrafty + Talonflame lead, Mamoswine + Primarina in back (roster this series excludes Metagross/Hydreigon/Rotom-Frost/Manectric). Rationale from G1: (1) Talonflame at 178 Spe always outruns Scarf Gholdengo (<=149) and Passimian (<=145), so TAILWIND is guaranteed turn 1 even if it later dies. (2) Scrafty's Fake Out flinches the non-Ghost threat and denies the second half of their signature double-up, so only ONE Shadow Ball lands turn 1 -> neither lead dies and Tailwind goes up. (3) Their Gholdengo is likely Choice-locked (Shadow Ball last game), which Scrafty resists 0.5x and Primarina tanks; do NOT Knock Off Gholdengo (frees the lock). (4) Primarina is the only mon that survives their Passimian+Gholdengo stack (~126 of 187) and answers Swampert (Energy Ball 4x) and Dragonite (Ice Beam 4x) as the possible 4th. (5) Mamoswine kept in back: it is my Charizard/Venusaur/Dragonite/Swampert answer but 2x weak to Passimian Close Combat and dies to the stack, so it enters only once Tailwind is up. Aware Scrafty's Intimidate hands Defiant Passimian +2 Atk - planned T2 line under Tailwind is Talonflame Brave Bird (pops Focus Sash) then Scrafty Knock Off to remove it before it can swing.

Leading Passimian and Gholdengo with Charizard and Swampert in reserve. Defiant Passimian punishes Intimidate from Scrafty/Arcanine while Quick Guard denies Gale Wings Brave Bird, Fake Out, and Extreme Speed. Scarf Gholdengo outspeeds their entire team and is immune to Fake Out and Fighting STAB. Charizard and Swampert provide supreme late-game sweep and Wide Guard control.

Scrafty Fake Out -> Passimian, Talonflame Tailwind. Passimian Close Combat is a guaranteed OHKO on Scrafty (123-178%) so it MUST be flinched; that also denies their signature double-up, meaning only one Gholdengo hit lands turn 1 (Shadow Ball 50-72% on Talonflame, 14-21% on Scrafty; Make It Rain spread 28-40%/33-48%) so both leads live. Tailwind is guaranteed because Gale Wings gives +1 priority to Flying-type moves including Tailwind, and Gale Wings' Brave Bird will also move first next turn. I rejected Talonflame Flare Blitz on Gholdengo: it is only 69-127% (not a safe KO) and Gholdengo is faster (171-223 with the Scarf), so it would just take a free hit for nothing. Fake Out on Gholdengo is illegal (Ghost, 0x). With Tailwind up, Scrafty (156) will outrun Passimian (110-145) next turn, letting me Brave Bird (81-147%, pops the Focus Sash) then Knock Off to remove Passimian before it can swing a +1 Close Combat again.

selection: Quick Guard (your side, including ally Gholdengo)
decisions.rationale: Passimian uses Quick Guard (+3 priority) to outspeed and block Scrafty's Fake Out (+3 priority, Scrafty 78-110 Spe vs Passimian 145 Spe) and Talonflame's Gale Wings Brave Bird (+1 priority). This perfectly preserves Passimian's Focus Sash and +1 Defiant Attack boost. Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) outspeeds Talonflame and Scrafty on neutral priority, firing Make It Rain to deal spread damage to Scrafty and chip Talonflame below 100% HP, permanently disabling Gale Wings.

Both Talonflame and Scrafty outrun Passimian (110-145) under Tailwind, so Brave Bird + Knock Off land BEFORE it can Close Combat (which is a guaranteed OHKO on my 58% Scrafty at 123-178%). Combined minimum is 95.7% and the average is ~134%, so Passimian should die before acting - and if it dies, the only attack left this turn is Gholdengo's Make It Rain, now spread and at -2 SpA (roughly 14-24%), so neither of my leads dies. I rejected switching Scrafty out: Mamoswine/Primarina are the only options and Passimian's Close Combat 2x OHKOs a switched-in Mamoswine, while a switch also forfeits the KO. I also rejected Talonflame Flare Blitz on Gholdengo: Gholdengo is already Choice-locked into a weakened Make It Rain and is no longer a threat, whereas Passimian is the real danger. Scrafty's Knock Off also strips Passimian's Focus Sash so it can never be saved from a later hit, and refusing the kill leaves Scrafty dead to a +1 Close Combat anyway.

Passimian uses Protect to safely stall opposing Tailwind while preserving its +1 Defiant Attack boost and Focus Sash against potential double-targeting. Gholdengo switches to Swampert, evading Talonflame's fast Tailwind Flare Blitz, safely absorbing any incoming physical hit with Swampert's 207 HP / 112 Def bulk, and resetting Gholdengo's -2 SpA drop and Choice lock for late-game cleanup.

Scrafty Knock Off -> Passimian and Talonflame Brave Bird -> Passimian, a 2-hit kill (Brave Bird 81-147%, Knock Off 14-26%, combined min 95.7% avg ~134%, and Knock Off strips the Focus Sash). Under Tailwind both my mons act BEFORE Passimian (Talonflame 356, Scrafty 156 vs Passimian 110-145), so Passimian dies before it can fire the Close Combat that is a guaranteed OHKO on my 58% Scrafty (123-178%). The only remaining attack is Swampert's, and Scrafty survives every Swampert move (HH 34-49%, Ice Punch 17-26%, Flip Turn 21-31%) while Talonflame is immune to High Horsepower; only a Flip Turn into Talonflame (69.7-101.9%, a KO from 65%) costs me anything, and trading Talonflame - whose Tailwind is already banked - for their Passimian is fine. I rejected switching Primarina in (option 6): she is safe vs one attack (CC 40-58%, HH 44-65%) but a doubled CC+HH on her switch-in slot is 84-123% and can kill her, throwing away my Swampert/Dragonite answer for nothing - and their AI has already shown it doubles the slot I switch into (G1 T1). I rejected Talonflame Protect: it achieves nothing while leaving Passimian free to Close Combat Scrafty next turn. Killing Passimian now is the prerequisite for ever bringing Mamoswine (2x weak to its Close Combat) onto the field.

Replacement = Primarina. Their active is now Gholdengo with a FRESH move choice (its Choice lock reset when it pivoted out and back), and it is Scarfed at 171-223 Speed, so it acts before my whole team even under Tailwind (Scrafty 156, Mamoswine 200, Primarina 160). Gholdengo's Make It Rain is a 4x... no, 2x Steel hit that OHKOs Mamoswine at both endpoints (118.9-171.4%) and also spreads onto Scrafty (44.2-63.4%, a possible KO from 58%), and Focus Blast OHKOs Mamoswine (79.3-114.3%) and Scrafty (59.3-84.9%). So switching Mamoswine in now is switching a frail mon into a predicted double - exactly the mistake I flagged in my playbook. Primarina survives every Gholdengo move (Make It Rain 40.6-57.8%, Shadow Ball 27.3-39%, Focus Blast only 13.4-19.3%) and she is also my 4x answer to the Swampert sitting on their bench, so she hard-walls their only currently-active threat. I keep Mamoswine in reserve as the Charizard/Rock-Slide answer, and Scrafty (Rock Slide 4x on Charizard) plus Primarina cover their unrevealed 4th.

Passimian uses +1 Close Combat into Scrafty for a guaranteed OHKO (122-218% on 58% HP). Passimian's full HP Focus Sash guarantees survival against any single attack. If Talonflame uses Brave Bird into Passimian, recoil drops Talonflame to ~23% HP, making Swampert's super-effective STAB Flip Turn (55-103%) a guaranteed knockout that pivots in Choice Scarf Gholdengo to close out the Tailwind endgame. If Talonflame targets Swampert, Swampert easily sponges the hit, allowing both Passimian and Swampert to eliminate Scrafty and heavily chunk/KO Talonflame simultaneously.

Passimian has fainted, so Pass is the mandatory choice for slot 1. For Swampert's Flip Turn switch, switch to Choice Scarf Gholdengo to provide immediate offensive speed control against Scrafty under the final turn of Tailwind.

Switch Charizard into Slot 1 alongside Gholdengo. Charizard possesses Protect to safely stall the final turn of opposing Tailwind without risking damage, allowing Choice Scarf Gholdengo to outspeed Scrafty and exert immediate spread pressure with Make It Rain. Swampert is preserved pristine at 100% HP in reserve as a defensive pivot, setting up Mega Charizard Y to sweep under Drought once Tailwind expires.

Scrafty Rock Slide (both foes) plus Primarina Ice Beam into Charizard. This is my last Tailwind turn, so it is the only turn Scrafty (156) or Mamoswine (200) can outrun Charizard (120-152); after this Charizard outruns and beats everything (it OHKOs Mamoswine 125-174% with Overheat and 102-143% with Solar Beam, and does 68-96% to Primarina with Solar Beam). Scrafty's Rock Slide is 56.2-104.6% on Charizard-Mega (spread 0.75x) and Primarina's Ice Beam adds 21.6-38.6% = 78-143% combined, so doubling up on Charizard is my best real kill chance. I chose Scrafty over switching Mamoswine in because Scrafty survives Gholdengo's spread Make It Rain (44.2-63.4%, only a KO at one endpoint from 58%) whereas Mamoswine is flatly OHKO'd by Make It Rain (119-171%, 2x from Steel onto Ice) and Focus Blast (79-114%) - and their AI has already shown it doubles the slot I switch into (G1 turn 1 killed my switch-in Talonflame). Scrafty is also my most expendable body (it dies to Focus Blast either way) and Mamoswine stays available. Primarina's Ice Beam is the only damage she can contribute here (Moonblast and Energy Ball are 0.5x/0.25x on Charizard), and if Scrafty is removed before acting she at least chips Charizard rather than wasting the turn on Protect. Quick Guard is useless (neither foe has a priority attack) and Knock Off on Charizard is only 24-46%.

Charizard uses Protect (disciplined weather timing withholding Mega Evolution) to safely stall out the final turn of opposing Tailwind, completely neutralizing Scrafty's 4x Rock Slide threat. Choice Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) outspeeds Scrafty (156-220 Spe under Tailwind) and fires Make It Rain (95% accuracy) to heavily damage or eliminate Scrafty while chipping Primarina into guaranteed Sun Solar Beam KO range for Turn 5.

Scrafty Rock Slide (free lottery ticket) + Primarina PROTECT. Scrafty is at 11% (19 HP) and Gholdengo's Make It Rain is a spread move that hits both slots - at 44-63% of Scrafty's HP it kills it outright - and Gholdengo is faster (171-223 vs Scrafty 78), so Scrafty will never get to act: its move choice is cosmetic, and Rock Slide is the best case if they instead pivot Gholdengo out to Swampert. Primarina is the piece I cannot lose: she alone hard-walls the now Choice-locked, SpA-dropping Make It Rain behind Leftovers and 4x-KOs Swampert with Energy Ball, so if she dies here I have no path. Protecting her blocks that spread Make It Rain AND blanks a Charizard hit; Charizard is still un-Mega-evolved, so a predicted Solar Beam would be a completely wasted turn for them, and its Fire moves are only 0.5x on her (Overheat 41.7-58.8%, Heat Wave 23-32%). I rejected Ice Beam: it only chips 21.6-38.6% and is not needed, because Mamoswine's Rock Slide (93-176.5% on Charizard-Mega) already kills from full, and exposing my only wincon to a potential sun-boosted Solar Beam (68.4-96.3%, lethal from 69% HP) to gain redundant chip is a bad trade - exactly the "never trade the key mon into a faster foe" rule in my playbook. Mamoswine enters at full HP and its Ice Shard (+1 priority) lands before Charizard even without Tailwind, and it survives Heat Wave (70-95%) to deliver Rock Slide. Quick Guard and Knock Off are useless/harmful here (no priority attacks; Knock Off on Gholdengo would strip its Scarf and free it from the harmless Make It Rain lock).
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

With Tailwind expired, both Gholdengo (223 Spe) and Charizard-Mega-Y (152 Spe) are guaranteed to outspeed both opposing Pokémon (Primarina 80-112 Spe, Scrafty 78-110 Spe). Choice Scarf Gholdengo fires Make It Rain first, eliminating Scrafty (16.3-30.0% damage on 11% HP) and chipping Primarina to 41-54% HP. Charizard then Mega Evolves into Mega Charizard Y to set Drought and fires an instant 120 BP Solar Beam into Primarina (66.3-118.7% damage), guaranteeing a double knockout before either opponent can attack.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Mamoswine Rock Slide + Primarina Protect. Charizard-Mega-Y in sun is their win condition and it is 4x weak to Rock Slide: 93-176.5% from full, the only move on my team that actually removes it (High Horsepower is 0x on it, Icicle Crash is only 52.4-99.3%, and Ice Shard's 25.4-46.4% just feeds it). Because Mamoswine (100 Speed) is slower than Charizard (120-152), Rock Slide only lands if Charizard does NOT target Mamoswine this turn - so I pair it with Primarina's Protect, which blanks the 2x Solar Beam this AI has repeatedly aimed at her (turn 5, and four times in game 1) and keeps my only surviving endgame piece alive. If Charizard shoots Primarina, Protect eats it and Mamoswine's Rock Slide ends Charizard and I keep both mons against a Gholdengo that is now locked into a self-weakening Make It Rain at -4 SpA and a Swampert Primarina 4x-KOs. If Charizard instead Overheats Mamoswine (125-174%) I lose Mamoswine, but Primarina survives at 75% with Leftovers and can still Protect-stall and Ice Beam. I rejected Ice Beam on Primarina (21.6-38.6%, redundant since Rock Slide already kills from full) because it needlessly exposes my wincon to a lethal Solar Beam, and I rejected a pure Ice Shard line: guaranteed 25-46% chip does not kill Charizard, which then removes one of my mons anyway. Protect's reduced rate on a consecutive use is a known risk, but preserving Primarina is worth more than 30% chip that wins nothing.

Charizard-Mega-Y (152 Spe) and Choice Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) both naturally outspeed Mamoswine (100-132 Spe) and Primarina (80-112 Spe). Mamoswine has all 4 moves revealed with no Protect. Charizard fires Sun-boosted Overheat into Mamoswine for a guaranteed 106.0-204.3% OHKO through Thick Fat, completely removing the Rock Slide threat before Mamoswine can move. Even an opposing Ice Shard (+1 priority, 33-46%) cannot threaten Charizard, and Gholdengo chips Primarina with Make It Rain to seal the endgame.

Primarina Ice Beam -> Charizard (Mamoswine's empty slot: Pass). I am down to Primarina alone against Charizard-Mega-Y, Gholdengo and Swampert. Charizard is the only foe that can actually kill her (Solar Beam 2x; at its current -2 SpA that is only ~34-48% per turn) and also the only one she can meaningfully damage: Ice Beam is 1x for 21.6-38.6%, whereas Moonblast into Charizard/Gholdengo is 0.5x and Energy Ball is 0.25x into Charizard. Gholdengo is Choice-locked into Make It Rain at -6 SpA (a tiny 1x trickle that Leftovers mostly offsets) and Swampert is still benched, so neither is worth attacking. The remaining path is to race Charizard down before it lands enough Solar Beams, which means attacking every turn rather than Protecting: a Protect stalls a turn while dealing nothing, and since their Charizard already used Overheat last turn it may keep dropping its own SpA - the one branch where Primarina's Leftovers lets her out-sustain and eventually win, and attacking maximises the number of Ice Beams she lands in that branch.

Both Gholdengo (223 Spe) and Charizard-Mega-Y (152 Spe) comfortably outspeed Primarina (80-112 Spe), which has no priority moves. Choice Scarf Gholdengo fires Make It Rain (10-18% damage), followed immediately by Charizard-Mega-Y's instant Sun-powered 120 BP super-effective Solar Beam (34-61% damage) directly targeting Primarina to either knock it out this turn or reduce it to single-digit HP with both allies remaining above 70% HP.

Primarina Protect (Mamoswine slot: Pass). At 14% (26 HP) Primarina dies to literally any damaging hit these foes own - Charizard's Solar Beam is 64-90 at its current -2 SpA, Gholdengo's weakened Make It Rain is ~15-22, and both act BEFORE her (Gholdengo 171-223, Charizard 120-152, Primarina 80) - so an Ice Beam would just be a wasted turn in which she faints before moving. Protect at least blanks the spread Make It Rain and the Solar Beam and lets Leftovers tick her back up, and it is legal again now because her last action was Ice Beam, not a Protect (unlike the T6 failure, which came on a back-to-back use). Ice Beam cannot win the race anyway: Charizard is still at 62%, so she would need two or three clean hits while surviving that whole time on 26 HP. If their AI ever Protects Charizard, pivots, or wastes a turn on the Fire moves she resists, Protector keeps her alive to punish it; attacking does not.

Both Gholdengo (223 Spe) and Charizard-Mega-Y (152 Spe) outspeed Primarina (80-112 Spe, 13% HP remaining). Gholdengo's Make It Rain deals 10-18% damage, followed by Charizard-Mega-Y's instant Sun-powered 120 BP super-effective Solar Beam (34-61% damage) directly targeting Primarina to close out Game 2 and secure the clean 2-0 series victory.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Primarina Protect again (Mamoswine slot: Pass). At 20% (37 HP) she still dies to anything Charizard does (Solar Beam 64-90 at -2 SpA, Overheat 39-55) and both foes move before her, so Ice Beam would be a wasted turn in which she faints before acting. Protect is the only move that keeps her alive, and this is the critical turn to buy: the sun has 1 turn left, so if she survives T9 the weather ends and Charizard must spend a turn CHARGING Solar Beam on T10, which gives Primarina a free Ice Beam with no incoming damage from it. I am aware of the reduced success rate on a back-to-back Protect, but the alternative is certain death this turn, so the risk is strictly worth taking. If Protect holds, the line is Protect -> free Ice Beam while Charizard charges -> Protect again on the release, chipping Charizard (62%) down 21.6-38.6% per Ice Beam while Leftovers offsets Gholdengo's now-tiny locked Make It Rain (~15-22).

Primarina Protected last turn and has heavily reduced Protect success rate. Both Choice Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) and Charizard-Mega-Y (152 Spe) outspeed Primarina (80-112 Spe, 19% HP). Gholdengo's Make It Rain (10-18%) and Charizard's Sun-powered super-effective Solar Beam (34-61%) guarantee the knockout to conclude Game 2 and secure the 2-0 series sweep.

reflections.summary: Lost game 2 and the series 0-2 because I never converted my early Passimian kill into a Charizard kill. The lead plan itself worked: Scrafty+Talonflame set Tailwind on turn 1 (Gale Wings even gives Tailwind +1 priority), and on turn 3 Talonflame's Brave Bird popped Passimian's Focus Sash, Scrafty's Knock Off finished it, and Swampert's Flip Turn killed Talonflame - a fair 1-for-1. But their AI then out-read me twice: Passimian Protected on turn 2 and Charizard Protected on turn 4, blanking both of my stacked double-attacks and handing Charizard a free Mega Evolution plus Drought. Tailwind (set turn 1) expired at the end of turn 4, and my three 4x Charizard answers - Mamoswine (100 Speed), Scrafty (78) and Machamp (75) - are all SLOWER than Charizard-Mega-Y (120-152), so they could only ever act on a Tailwind turn. By the time I finally committed Mamoswine on turn 6, Tailwind was gone and I paired its Rock Slide with a consecutive Protect on Primarina that FAILED, so Charizard's sun-boosted Overheat OHKO'd Mamoswine before Rock Slide ever resolved. That was the game. Primarina then lost a 1v3, chipping Charizard only to 62% before the same Protect failed again. Their Charizard never Mega-Evolved until turn 5, so I had three full turns of warning and still had no non-Tailwind way to touch it. The between-game adjustment to add Scrafty partly helped (its Knock Off removed Passimian's Sash and won me that exchange) but its Fake Out was blocked by Quick Guard and, at 78 Speed with Tailwind gone, it contributed nothing against Charizard. The window-1 trade that removed Sinistcha backfired: redirection (Follow Me/Rage Powder) is precisely the tool that beats this AI's habit of putting both attacks on one slot, and I had none of it.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent: (1) Never register a Charizard answer that needs Tailwind to move. Mamoswine/Scrafty/Machamp (100/78/75) all lose the race to Charizard-Mega-Y (120-152), so either plan the Tailwind timer around Charizard's arrival (and re-set Tailwind rather than spending the last Tailwind turn on a side quest like chipping Passimian) or accept the matchup is decided before it starts. (2) Stop telegraphing the double - their AI Protects the mon I am about to double-target, and it blanked two of my full turns that way. Split attacks across both foes, or click a harmless/spread move to burn the Protect before committing. (3) Mamoswine's Ice Shard (+1 priority) is the only damage I can guarantee onto Charizard with no Tailwind; do not trade it away for a slow Rock Slide gamble, and never pair a slow signature move with a consecutive Protect that can fail. (4) Re-acquire redirection (Follow Me/Rage Powder) - it nullifies this AI's single-slot stacking, which is the core of how it wins. (5) Their Scarf Gholdengo outruns my whole team; when it locks into something weak, leave the item on and out-sustain it (Primarina + Leftovers did this cleanly, driving Make It Rain's SpA to -6). (6) Bring a bulky wincon that can actually trade with sun Charizard - I left Mega Metagross behind and had six frail or slow pieces.

reflections.summary: We secured a flawless 2-0 series victory over DeepSeek through superior tactical preparation, exact speed-tier discipline, and textbook execution. In Game 1, our lead read punished Machamp's Wide Guard by focusing single-target attacks (Shadow Ball + Close Combat) to OHKO the incoming Talonflame. In Game 2, our between-game adjustment to maintain the Passimian + Gholdengo lead against Scrafty + Talonflame paid off immediately: Turn 1 Quick Guard completely blocked Scrafty's Fake Out and Talonflame's Gale Wings Brave Bird, while Scarf Gholdengo's Make It Rain stripped Gale Wings. Perfect Tailwind stalling via Passimian's Protect and Swampert's Flip Turn eliminated Talonflame and safely ushered in Mega Charizard Y, whose Drought sun enabled guaranteed OHKOs on Mamoswine (Overheat through Thick Fat) and Primarina (Solar Beam) to clinch the clean sweep.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series against this opponent, continue exploiting their structural dependence on Gale Wings Tailwind and Intimidate/Fake Out leads with Quick Guard and Defiant. If they adapt by incorporating Trick Room (e.g., Sinistcha) or special offensive pressure to avoid Defiant triggers, register and bring Chlorophyll Venusaur for fast Sleep Powder / Sludge Bomb pressure under Sun, or Raichu for Lightning Rod redirection and 100% Nuzzle speed control.

decisions.rationale: Lead Chandelure + Excadrill, with Empoleon + Rotom-Heat behind. Their registered six have no Salamence or Tailwind and instead emphasize slow Trick Room offense: Imprison plus immediate Steel/Ground pressure is more valuable than our own Tailwind. Excadrill pressures Hatterene, Dragalge and Garganacl, while Chandelure threatens Corviknight and locks both setters. Empoleon supplies the Water-resistant pivot and special coverage into Azumarill, Dragalge and Garganacl; Rotom gives a second Corviknight answer so preserving the Imprison anchor does not require it to supply all Fire damage. Avoid automatically spending Chandelure's Sash: evaluate both attacks and water pivots each turn.

Draft Farig+Corv lead with Hatt+Garg back. Their new sheet is an anti-TR adaptation (Chand Imprison+TR, Empoleon Competitive, tech berries, no Ape) but Armor Tail/Mental Herb still blank their T1 (Fake Out + Prankster TW/Taunt all blocked); TR T1 + Corv Iron Head on Sashless Weavile. Azu roles dead (no Ape, Passho), Drag risk (HHP/GK 2x) vs Whim already covered — Hatt = setter #2 + Magic Bounce + DP 2x Chand, Garg = Fire wall + RS execute + BP partner for ExcMega one-turn kill under TR.

Imprison acts before Corviknight's Taunt and denies Farigiraf's Trick Room without being blocked by Armor Tail or Mental Herb. Mega High Horsepower makes immediate progress into the setter rather than wasting a setup turn or attacking immune Corviknight. Mega bulk limits Body Press to the estimated 37–56% range. Chandelure can threaten Corviknight with Flamethrower next turn, while its lock persists as long as it stays active.

Chandy+Exc lead = anti-TR lock; Imprison resolves before my TR (Chandy faster), and the lock persists while Chandy lives — Taunt can't erase it. Counter: split actions, guaranteed progress. Farig→Garg switch: Garg RS→Chandy forces Sash to 1hp (or KOs), Balloon eats a stray Ground hit, Farig stays safe for late TR. Corv BP→Excadrill 2x (30-63%) starts the ExcMega kill clock; BP is the only strong hit I have vs it. Even if one foe Protects, the other line lands.

Flamethrower pressures Corviknight before it can move; Protect preserves the already-damaged Excadrill against another Body Press plus Garganacl chip. Iron Head cannot immediately KO full Garganacl, so splitting attacks risks losing Drill before its Ground/Steel endgame pays off. Chandelure survives the estimated single Rock Slide from full, and keeping it active maintains the Trick Room lock against a Farigiraf return.

Imprison live → no TR/Protect this turn; unlock by killing Chandy. Salt Cure forces Sash (1hp) AND the 1/8 residual kills it end of turn — guaranteed lock removal unless Chandy Protects (fresh 100%). Pair BP→ExcMega (~35% KO, else banked for guaranteed BP+BP T3). Splitting targets read-proofs the turn; Chand does 0.5x to Garg and can't threaten Corv except Flamethrower (Corv at 100%, fine).

Corv slot must refill; Farigiraf is the safe switch (survives Chand FT neutral + ExcMega HHP worst-case, unlike Hatt who dies to Flamethrower 2x). Farig is my primary TR setter — being on field when Imprison clears (Chandy at 41% with Salt Cure mark dying to residual/chip, or pivoting out) means TR the very next turn with no extra switch. Garg menu forces Pass; it retains full HP + Balloon as bait (HHP immune again). Chand kill clock: residual + Garg RS (guaranteed ≤43%) + Farig FP backup T4-T5.

Protect Chandelure to keep Imprison active through both enemy attacks, while Iron Head damages Garganacl and removes its Ground immunity. Neither a single Iron Head into Garganacl nor our double attack into a maximally bulky Farigiraf is assured to KO; exposing Chandelure would let Rock Slide remove the lock before a delayed Trick Room. Excadrill survives a lone Foul Play at its current HP, and Iron Head also offers a useful flinch chance.

Split the turn across both foes so one fresh Protect can't blank it: SC→Chandy is a guaranteed kill (band ≥45 vs 41, 100% acc) that clears Imprison; FP→ExcMega banks Exc to ≤16% if Chandy Protected. ExcMega acting first is survivable (Farig worst-case 99%, Garg Balloon immune). This maximizes P(TR goes up T4-T5 with Farig alive).

Finish the 40% Garganacl with accurate Iron Head while Chandelure damages Farigiraf. This removes the attacker threatening Chandelure before it moves and keeps Imprison up if Farigiraf attempts Trick Room. Farigiraf can KO one weakened ally with an attack, but not both; accepting that trade leaves our two healthy reserves against a chipped setter and their last Pokémon. Protecting Drill instead would let Garganacl heal or remove Chandelure without enough progress.

Bring Rotom-Heat for guaranteed natural Speed advantage over Farigiraf and all possible unrevealed fourth Pokémon. It can combine immediate special damage with Chandelure to remove the chipped setter, while Empoleon remains healthy as the Water/Dragon-facing reserve.

Double-kill turn: Farig FP→ExcMega is a guaranteed kill on 13% (even if ExcMega KOs Garg first — it acts first, dies second); Garg SC→Chandy is a guaranteed kill on 35% (band ≥45, 100% acc). Only a double-Protect (33%/33%) stops both, and that costs them all pressure. Killing Chandy clears Imprison → Farig TRs T5. Killing ExcMega removes the only mon that outspeeds and threatens my board. Farig survives worst-case targeting (≤99% taken).
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Focus Farigiraf with accurate Flamethrower + Thunderbolt before either foe's ordinary attacks. Combined damage comfortably covers its remaining 55%, and Imprison prevents Protect. Hatterene can remove Chandelure afterward, but then faces two healthy special attackers including super-effective Empoleon; if it attempts Trick Room while Chandelure remains, the lock denies it. Avoid Overheat's miss chance and Special Attack drop.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

2v3 with no switches left: killing Chandy (29%) is the only path to TR and it's the easiest kill on board. Double-tap DP+FP makes the kill ~75-80% even accounting for a fresh 100% Protect read; a Protect from them buys me tempo instead (they forgo damage, Protect degrades to 33% next turn while my kill bands hold). Hatt carries the endgame (198 SpA, bounce, setter #2) — if Chand snipes it, Farig's redundancy still clears the lock.

Use accurate Flash Cannon + Thunderbolt into the final Hatterene. Both healthy allies can sustain its attacks, and repeated focused damage wins through Sitrus or Protect without risking Overheat misses/drops or reflecting Will-O-Wisp into Magic Bounce.

1v2 with no switches: only line is TR now. Worst-case double hit (FC 2x + TBolt ~95%) leaves Hatt alive via Sitrus; from T7 Hatt acts first — two-turn Rotom kill before the Empoleon grind. Racing outside TR is a guaranteed loss; this is the only equity line. Also banks full info for G2/G3 against their now-confirmed four.

reflections.summary: Won in six turns with Empoleon and Rotom untouched. The four supplied a coherent anti-TR plan and a healthy special-attacking endgame. Imprison stayed active until Farigiraf was removed; alternating Protect with immediate damage let us trade Excadrill for Garganacl and Chandelure for progress into both setters. However, T1 High Horsepower overlooked the disclosed Air Balloon Garganacl switch and cost 90 HP on Drill for no damage. T3's reasoning also checked Foul Play alone rather than Foul Play plus Garganacl attacking Drill; the opponent instead repeated Salt Cure into protected Chandelure. Flamethrower OHKOed Corviknight this game, but prior damage ranges did not guarantee that outcome. The final Flash Cannon was critical, so its KO is not a normal damage benchmark. No Trick Room was actually attempted; do not infer the opponent will keep attacking instead of adapting.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Chandelure/Excadrill with Empoleon/Rotom as the default four, rather than adding unnecessary Tailwind. Against the same Farigiraf/Corviknight lead, favor Imprison plus Iron Head into Farigiraf's slot as an accuracy/immunity-safe opening that also punishes Balloon Garganacl entering; reconsider after evaluating both opposing attacks. Do not mechanically repeat Ground pressure while Balloon is intact. Expect possible Azumarill or Dragalge adaptation and preserve Empoleon for Water pivots. Keep the willingness to trade weakened attackers once the setter-removal route and healthy final pair are secured.

reflections.summary: G1 lost 0-1 in 6 turns (0 decision errors — losses were structural, not execution). Their anti-TR package worked exactly as designed: Chandelure led with Imprison T1, locking my Trick Room AND Protect for the entire game (lock persists while Chand is active; Taunt doesn't erase it). My T1 adjustment (Farig→Garg switch) dodged ExcMega's High Horsepower and banked Salt Cure value, but TR never resolved all game. Corviknight was one-shot by a single Flamethrower from 100% (my assessment that Corv was safe was flat wrong — Chand carries ~99-110% into it). Garganacl performed: SC hit Chand for ~53% (recalibrated band 45-55) + residuals ground it to 29%, and its Balloon ate the first Ground hit; but ExcMega doubled Iron Head (59% each) and killed it T4. Farigiraf was the MVP: Foul Play (39-46% per hit using ExcMega's own 165 Atk) killed it in two hits, and Farig survived HHP range. Hatterene one-shot 29% Chand with Dark Pulse, clearing Imprison, but the 1v2 endgame vs Empoleon+Rotom-Heat was unwinnable: Hatt deals only ~13-15%/turn into Empoleon (resists both STABs) and died to a crit Flash Cannon — Steel→Fairy is 2x in this sim. Their pilot played a clean game: Imprison lock, disciplined Protect reads (fresh 100% on both kill turns), relentless focus-fire on Garg. Two exploitable findings: their Chand's listed Focus Sash did NOT trigger from full HP (don't respect it), and Garganacl is a clean 1v1 winner vs BOTH Rotom-Heat and Empoleon — my G1 endgame kept the wrong Pokémon at the cleanup station.
reflections.adjustment: KEEP: same draft 4 (Farig/Garg/Corv/Hatt — Azu and Drag remain dead weight vs this squad: Passho halves WF, SW 0x/0.5x into 3 of 4, IcyWind banned by Competitive). CHANGE the script: (1) LEAD GARG+FARIG — no T1 switch tax; T1 SC→Chand + FP→ExcMega; (2) kill both their leads by T3-T4 through Protect chains (their 100% reads degrade; my residuals grind regardless); (3) TR goes up the turn after Chand dies — Farig if alive, else Corv enters (HHP-immune) and Hatt TRs later; (4) ENDGAME = GARG CLEANUP: RS→Rotom-Heat ~50-58%/turn (2-turn kill), SC→Empoleon ~30%/turn, Recover above ~40% chip — Garg out-tanks their entire back line; (5) keep Hatt on field next to Garg late (Magic Bounce eats WoW aimed at the ally — their only real Garg counter is burn); (6) NEVER: Corv vs live Chand/Rotom (2x one-shot-range), Hatt vs live ExcMega/Empoleon-FC, Intimidate or Icy Wind into Empoleon, planning around their Chandelure Sash (didn't trigger from full). If they lead Rotom+Empoleon instead, the script gets easier: no Imprison, Farig TRs T2, Garg walls both and kills each.

decisions.rationale: Retain Chandelure/Excadrill with Empoleon/Rotom reserves: this four denies both Trick Room setters, pressures Corviknight and Garganacl, and preserves special offense plus a Water-resistant pivot if Azumarill or Dragalge is brought as an adaptation. No opposing Tailwind or fast Mega warrants spending a slot on Whimsicott. Lead actions remain matchup-dependent: avoid repeating High Horsepower into the disclosed Balloon pivot, and consider immediate Fire pressure when Imprison is not urgent. Preserve Empoleon for Water attackers rather than exposing both Fire types together.

G2 draft = planned answer to G1's loss script. Farig+Garg lead: Armor Tail blanks Fake Out/Prankster Taunt, Mental Herb backup; SC→Chand (45-55) breaks Imprison caster, FP→ExcMega (39-46 x2) kills their snowball through the TR/Protect lock. Corv back = safe ExcMega station (never vs Chand/Rotom). Hatt back = Magic Bounce vs WoW/Taunt/LightScreen + TR #2 + Rotom/Chand executes, never vs live ExcMega. Preview confirms Weavile has no Sash (Wide Lens) and Chand no Fire Blast — lines improve. Azu (Passho bait, no Ape) and Drag (0x into Exc/Chand-heavy board) home.

Imprison denies immediate Trick Room and starts the Protect lock; Mega Iron Head safely damages Garganacl and removes its Balloon instead of wasting Ground coverage. Both actions precede the foes. Foul Play plus Rock Slide can KO Chandelure, so this is not a guaranteed survival line, but that double attack excludes Farigiraf setting Trick Room this turn and leaves a damaged, grounded Garganacl for Excadrill to remove with a healthy reserve joining. If Farigiraf attempts Trick Room, Chandelure can withstand Garganacl's single attack and preserve the lock.

Board A (Chand+Exc lead) = G1 script. Chand (110-145 Spe) acts before Farig, so T1 Trick Room risks failing to Imprison — G1 lesson: ignore lock, kill caster. Garg SC→Chand 45-55% + residual (Sash irrelevant vs repeat 45% hits); Farig FP→Exc uses Exc(Mega)'s own Attack, 39-46% — pairs toward 2-turn kill. TR gets re-set the turn after Chand dies.

Take immediate progress with Flamethrower into Farigiraf and accurate Iron Head to finish 35% Garganacl before it can attack or Recover. Imprison already denies opposing Protect and Trick Room. Farigiraf alone cannot remove both attackers, and damage on it creates a cleanup route for our healthy reserves. Iron Head also avoids losing the turn to a Corviknight Ground-immunity switch; if that pivot occurs, preserve Fire pressure on subsequent turns rather than assume Garganacl stays.

ExcMega (faster) will almost certainly Iron Head Garg at 35% before it moves — losing the sole Rotom/Empoleon cleaner. Switching Garg preserves the win-con; switch-first resolution dodges targeting. Farig FP→Exc sets a guaranteed T3/T4 kill (14-21% left). Accepting Chand surviving at ~38% + Imprison one more turn: Garg returns post-Exc-death and Salt Cures it down, then TR + Recover restores the endgame. Corv entry risk (FT 72-104) accepted — Corv is replaceable, Garg is not.

Pressure both opposing actions now: Flamethrower into Corviknight, High Horsepower into 53% Farigiraf. Chandelure outspeeds Corviknight, and last game's full-health Flamethrower KO supports strong removal odds at 82%, without treating the broad damage endpoints as certainty. High Horsepower gives the weakened Drill its best immediate Farigiraf KO chance; Protect would concede that damage while allowing Farigiraf to target Chandelure. Neither KO is assumed guaranteed, but this line can remove both threats and otherwise leaves cleanup damage for our healthy reserves. Garganacl switching in is now grounded and cannot blank High Horsepower.

6% ExcMega still outspeeds and trades itself for Farig (IH 41-57 vs 53% HP). Cannot Protect (Imprison) or dodge without feeding Garg into entry kill — Garg is the sole Rotom/Empoleon cleaner, protected above all. Double-tap FP+BP into Exc guarantees the kill when it doesn't Protect; a Protect read costs only the turn. If Farig falls, Hatterene sets TR after Chand dies (Imprison ends with it).

Both actives were high-rolled down before acting — Farig/Corv gone, TR line broken. Entries are forced (2 mons, 2 slots); Hatterene takes the ExcMega-target side (dies either way, buys the slot), Garganacl takes the Chandelure side where Flamethrower does only ~15-20% so it survives to Rock Slide next turn — the only line that kills Chandelure (breaking Imprison, ~70%) and the 6% ExcMega (~12%) simultaneously. Win probability is low against the 100% Rotom-Heat/Empoleon bench, but this maximizes the salvage branch and preserves Garg as long as possible.

Iron Head removes 35% Garganacl accurately before Recover or Rock Slide, while Flamethrower chips Hatterene. Keep Chandelure active so Hatterene cannot Protect or establish Trick Room while the lock persists. Hatterene can retaliate into only one attacker; whichever survives plus our two full-health reserves gives a strong cleanup position. No need to risk High Horsepower accuracy, setup, or release Imprison with a switch.

Bring full-health Empoleon to finish with super-effective Flash Cannon alongside Chandelure's Flamethrower. Chandelure retains Imprison, preventing Hatterene from using Protect or Trick Room; Empoleon also resists Psychic and leaves Rotom healthy as insurance.

All-in salvage: Garg RS kills Chand 26% (~70%, Imprison dies with it) and 6% ExcMega (~12%) in one spread if it lands through targeting; Hatt DP→Exc is the guaranteed backup execute on the 6% ExcMega. Recover is inferior — a surviving Chand keeps Imprison up and kills Hatt T5. If Hatt survives with Chand dead, T5 DP/Recover + T6 TR re-opens the Garg-cleans-Rotom/Emp endgame.

Finish with accurate Flamethrower plus super-effective Flash Cannon into the sole remaining foe. Both attackers act before Hatterene, its Sitrus is consumed, and ongoing Imprison prevents Protect or Trick Room. No switching or setup is needed.

No winning line remains (Hatt 72% vs Chand 27 + Emp 100 + Rotom-Heat bench, all faster, FC 2x kills Hatt), but Dark Pulse→Chandelure is the only real action: guaranteed kill through its 27% if it resolves, removing Imprison and denying their TR; Protect is Imprison-locked and Psychic can't touch Chand (0x vs Ghost... Chand is Ghost — Psychic immune). Slot 2 passes (Garganacl fainted, no bench).

reflections.summary:
Won G2 in five turns and the series 2-0. The main advantage was matchup-specific selection: Chandelure/Excadrill applied immediate Fire/Steel/Ground pressure and maintained Imprison, with healthy Empoleon/Rotom reserves. Their actual six lacked Salamence and Tailwind, so we correctly did not force our advertised Tailwind mode. Neither game saw Trick Room attempted; the lock restricted options rather than visibly blocking an attempted move.
The between-game correction helped: G1's opening High Horsepower was blanked by disclosed Balloon Garganacl; G2 Iron Head immediately took Garganacl to 35% and removed Balloon. Their Corviknight switch then punished our second Iron Head with resistance and Helmet, leaving Drill at 12/187 after Foul Play. We recovered by attacking rather than reflexively protecting: T3 High Horsepower removed 53% Farigiraf and Flamethrower removed 82% Corviknight before either acted. T4 accurate Iron Head finished Garganacl while Chandelure chipped Hatterene; trading Drill left an overwhelming special-attacking endgame. Chandelure survived at 37/137, Empoleon and Rotom stayed full.
G1's final Flash Cannon critical helped that finish but is not a normal damage benchmark. G2's final Flamethrower burn was incidental: Flash Cannon finished before burn damage. Zero submission errors does not erase G1's immunity oversight or incomplete joint-damage reasoning; G2 was the better execution.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, retain the selection principle, not these exact four or assumptions about their sets. Recheck rebuilt sheets for fast Mega Salamence, Tailwind and Water offense. This opponent used defensive pivots and concentrated Foul Play on Drill, but did not concentrate both attacks on Chandelure. Explicitly test that stronger response: Foul Play plus Rock Slide could remove the anchor, while Rock damage plus a setter's delayed Trick Room can release and exploit the lock in one turn. Price Helmet chip as well as Flying immunity when selecting Iron Head coverage. Keep redundant Corviknight pressure and a credible Water-facing reserve, but do not count untested Water matchups as solved. No roster change is justified merely because Whimsicott/Weavile were unbrought in a slow anti-TR matchup.

reflections.summary: Lost the series 0-2 to astra's fixed four (Excadrill-Mega + Imprison Chandelure lead + Rotom-Heat + Empoleon). Execution was clean — 0 decision errors across both games, and every calibration landed on plan: Salt Cure 45-55% into Chandelure, Foul Play chip into ExcMega, the T2 Garganacl switch-dance that saved the endgame win-con, Hatt Dark Pulse executing the 6% ExcMega. The loss was structural: their Chandelure leads Imprison every game, locking my Trick Room AND Protect — my entire identity — until the caster dies. Across 11 turns I never resolved Trick Room once, so a 49-87-speed team fought a 106-170-speed board at permanent disadvantage, racing a Chand kill (on pace: 50% T1, dead ~T3 by residual) while ExcMega focused my tanks and the fast bench waited. G1 also fell to my one genuine read error: Chand's Flamethrower killed Corviknight from 100% (I mispriced the 72.5-103.6 range). G2's fixes (Corv benched until Chand fell, Garg preserved via switch) held until T3, when two high rolls — ExcMega HHP killing 53% Farig (~81% of range) and Chand FT killing 83% Corv (~30%) — ended both actives before they moved; from there the 100% Rotom-Heat/Empoleon bench outsped my Hatterene/Garganacl remnants. My G2 adjustments helped but the draft had no second Imprison answer and no ExcMega execute off the bench — Azumarill and Dragalge brought nothing against this board. The ~24% compound high-roll decided G2, but the opponent's script had me on the back foot from turn 1 in both games; the fix is draft-level (Clawitzer execute, commit to the T2 Chand kill), not play-level.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent's Imprison+ExcMega script next time: (1) Register Clawitzer over a dead slot — LO Aura Sphere (56-131 into ExcMega) makes their IH-focus snowball a liability. (2) Commit to killing Chandelure by T2: Salt Cure T1 + T2, accepting Garg may die pre-move (p~0.65 if Exc focus-fires) — a dead Chand unlocks TR and the Hatt/Garg endgame wins from there; don't repeat the T2 switch-dance tempo concession. (3) Hard-ban Corviknight vs live Chandelure — FT (72.5-103.6) killed it at 100% in G1 and 83% in G2; twice burned. (4) Never let Farigiraf sit below ~80% vs ExcMega while Protect is Imprison-locked. (5) Endgame: Hatt Dark Pulse→Empoleon (80-100), never Psychic (13-15); Garg RS→RotH x2 / SC→Emp with Recover-to-85 discipline. (6) Treat any Chandelure fire as potentially lethal to Corv under ~105%, and don't assume FT is safe into Hatt either — the rolls are wide.

decisions.rationale: Their six (Rillaboom, Sneasler, Grimmsnarl, Dragonite, Skeledirge, Tauros) has no Dark attack and no Inteleon/Clefable. Gengar is immune to Fake Out/Extreme Speed/Close Combat and resists Grass, Poison (Dire Claw) and Fairy (Spirit Break): Rillaboom, Sneasler and Grimmsnarl cannot meaningfully touch it, so Gengar+Kanga lead with Shadow Tag trapping is better than Kanga+Kingambit (Kingambit lead is exposed to two Close Combat users). Kanga Fake Out breaks Sneasler's Sash-turn (Sash needs full HP), Gengar Psychic 4x KOs it. Back: Kingambit (Iron Head OHKO Grimmsnarl, Dark 2x Skeledirge, resists Ice Beam/ESpeed) + Houndoom (Flash Fire pivot for Fire Blast/Torch Song aimed at Kingambit, Heat Wave Rillaboom). Glalie/Altaria are weak un-mega'd and Gengar is the mega here.

G1 they registered an anti-us sheet: Gengar (Psychic 4x Sneasler), Scrappy Kanga (Ice Punch 4x DN; Scrappy hits Ghosts unless they Mega Kanga), Defiant Chople Gambit, Altaria Tailwind/Heat Wave, Inner Focus Glalie (Ice Shard 4x DN, no flinch/Intimidate), Flash Fire LO Houndoom. One Mega among four stones. Leave Combat (Defiant +2 Gambit, Scrappy/Inner Focus block Intimidate, Fighting 0 Gengar) and Rilla (no Wash; 2x Heat Wave/Ice; Fake Out does nothing to Gengar or Inner Focus Glalie). Bring Grimm screens/Taunt, Sneasler Gambit sniper, Mega DN (Gengar tank at Multi; Ice Beam Altaria; Fire Blast Gambit/Glalie), Dirge Tag-escape + Unaware. Lead Grimm+Sneasler: CC the non-Gengar slot (always Gambit if present), Grimm Taunt/LS vs Gengar or Reflect vs Kanga/Gambit. Mega DN on first attacking send behind screens. Dirge Ghost-switches Tag; do not switch it into Shadow Ball or Houndoom Dark Pulse.

Sneasler CC OHKOs Kanga (112-161%) but cannot touch Gengar at all (CC/Fake Out immune, Dire Claw 0.25x). Kanga Fake Out Sneasler + Gengar-Mega Psychic (122-230%, 4x): if Sneasler attacks Kanga, Fake Out flinches it first and breaks Sash, Psychic KOs. If Sneasler Fake Outs Kanga first (likely faster), Psychic still leaves it at 1 HP via Sash, trapped by Shadow Tag, and Kanga keeps Protect for T2 while Gengar finishes it. Better than Kanga Protect now, which burns Protect and leaves Kanga exposed to Unburden Sneasler T2.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Sneasler)
decisions.rationale: Kanga Fake Out is +3 and beats Prankster screens/Taunt, so Grimm cannot set up unless Kanga is flinched first. Sneasler 189 outspeeds even Mega Kanga FO and Fake Outs slot 2 — Ghost-immune Gengar is the wrong FO target, and CC Kanga loses to their FO (Sneasler flinch or Grimm flinch) plus CC is only a 77-163% roll. With Kanga flinched, the only T1 damage is Gengar: Mega Psychic Sneasler 165-226% (Sash), Sludge Grimm 69-96% (lives). Prankster Light Screen goes up before Gengar and can keep Sash (Psychic ~83-113% under LS) while chunking Sludge to 34-48%. Gengar has no reason to Protect T1 (nothing we click KOs it). Taunt Gengar is worse T1 because they will attack and LS actually reduces the hit. Reflect waits for T2 vs DE/Gambit.

Unburden Sneasler (308-378 Spe) at 1 HP moves before everything and CC OHKOs Kanga, so Kanga must Protect. Gengar Shadow Ball finishes the trapped Sneasler unless it Protects; if it Protects, it cannot repeat next turn. Grimmsnarl cannot hurt Gengar meaningfully (Spirit Break 22-31%).

Sneasler CC always KOs 81% non-mega Kanga (87-163% of max) and Unburden 378 outspeeds Gengar, so Kanga never acts unless it Protects. Fake Out is spent; Dire Claw does not KO. Tag traps Grimm (no switch); do not switch 1% Sneasler into Gengar Shadow Ball. Any Gengar hit KOs Sneasler after the CC — trade Sneasler for Kanga, then send DN into the open slot (faint send-in, not a switch). Prankster Reflect before their attacks completes dual screens for Gambit/Glalie/Kanga DE (non-mega DE Grimm is 44-67% without Reflect). Taunt Gengar can wait T3: they will Psychic the 1% Sneasler rather than Protect T2 (nothing we click KOs Gengar). Light Screen already covers Sludge (46-64%).

Faint send-in (Tag does not block it). Dragonite at full Multiscale is the Gengar tank (Shadow/Sludge ~16-30%); dual screens are up. Kanga Fake Out is spent; Ice Punch is 4x but Reflect+Multiscale halves twice. Mega on the first attacking turn. Skeledirge cannot come into Mega Gengar — Shadow Ball is 77-128% OHKO and Scrappy DE still hits Ghost. Grimm Pass (already acted).

Under Light Screen + Reflect + Multiscale Gengar barely dents Dragonite (10-16%), so Gengar's job is to remove Grimmsnarl (Sludge Bomb 54-101%, two hits) while Kanga Ice Punch breaks Multiscale (18-30%) so the next Ice Punch does ~35-60%. Gengar survives one Dragonite hit (Fire Blast max 67%) plus Spirit Break at worst case, and keeps Protect for next turn when the KO threat arrives. Shadow Tag keeps both foes trapped.

Ice Punch into Mega DN with Multiscale+Reflect is only 19-29% — not a KO, so Protect is the W1-chaining mistake. Mega immediately. Ice Beam Kanga (26-48% of max into 81%, 100% acc; Fire Blast is 85% and still not a KO; Modest ES is 14-26% and never KOs). Split targets: Taunt Gengar (Prankster, not Dark) so Tag cannot stall Protect; if Kanga Protects (already 1/3) Ice Beam whiffs but Taunt still lands, and vice versa. Gengar outspeeds DN so Taunt must go up this turn while they are likely to attack (Ice Punch/Shadow/Sludge) rather than Protect. Spirit Break Gengar is 0.5x and slower than Gengar. Screens already 6/7. Do not switch DN to Dirge into Shadow Ball.

Gengar (200 Spe, Taunted so no Protect anyway) Sludge Bombs Grimmsnarl at 42% for the KO (54-101%), removing Taunt/Spirit Break/screen renewal. Kanga at 37% is dead to Ice Beam or Spirit Break regardless, and outspeeds Dragonite-Mega (156 > 152 max), so it gets a second Ice Punch in now with Multiscale broken (~35-60%) before the 4th foe arrives with possible Fake Out/priority. Protecting Kanga would just delay the same trade while giving Dragonite a free hit on Gengar.

Kingambit in: resists Ice Beam/Extreme Speed, Sucker Punch priority can finish Dragonite-Mega at 23% (Multiscale broken), Defiant punishes a Tauros Intimidate, and it survives Rillaboom Wood Hammer easily. Houndoom stays in back as the Fire Blast/Torch Song pivot and would be OHKOed by a Tauros/Rillaboom 4th.

Gengar Sludge always KOs 42% Grimm (46-64%), and Spirit Break is +0 so Grimm faints before attacking — only Prankster Taunt Kanga actually fires. Kanga Protect is +4 and beats that Taunt, unavoidable. DN Ice Beam vs 37% Kanga is a 26-48% roll KO at 100% acc (Fire Blast 32-59% but 85% miss lets Ice Punch through; ES 14-26% never KOs). Ice Punch from 76% is 40-59% so DN lives this hit if they punch; Gengar should Sludge the KO on Grimm not double DN. Protect DN fails to remove Ice Punch and is dominated: if Kanga Protects both lines do 0, if Kanga attacks Ice Beam has ~50% to end it. Screens persist after Grimm faints. Dirge send-in after.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Skeledirge Shadow Ball does 83-123% to Gengar, which is Taunted and cannot Protect, so Gengar must leave. Houndoom is the ideal pivot: immune to Torch Song/Fire Blast (Flash Fire boost), resists Shadow Ball (22-32%) and Ice Beam (20-28%). Kingambit Protects because both foes threaten it with Fire (Fire Blast 68-96% + Torch Song 59-87% would kill it) and Dragonite at 23% likely Protects anyway. Next turn: Houndoom Dark Pulse + Kingambit Sucker Punch/Kowtow, with Gengar saved in back.

Gengar any attack KOs 23% DN; Kingambit Kowtow/Iron Head also KO DN. DN must Protect. If Dirge Shadow Balls the Taunted Gengar (65-124% roll), their correct answer is Sucker Punch Dirge (+1) + Shadow Ball Dirge (55-78% under LS): 36-51%+55-78% KOs Dirge before it moves, so the Gengar hit never happens. Both Protect: Sucker Punch fails (neither selected an attack), their damage hits Protect, Dirge stays 100% with LS still cutting Shadow Ball. This is the last Taunt turn but we cannot cash it if they double Dirge. T6 Gengar can Protect; live to play Dirge vs Gengar with screens. Do not Fire Blast Gambit from 23% DN — Sucker Punch KOs it first.

Both foes Protected last turn, so their Protect is unreliable now. Double-target Dragonite-Mega at 23%: Sucker Punch (17-29%, +1 priority) plus Houndoom Dark Pulse (~19-31%, 161 Spe outspeeds) guarantees the KO before it can Fire Blast Kingambit. Kingambit then only takes Torch Song (59-87%) and survives; Houndoom is immune to Fire and resists Shadow Ball/Ice Beam. Next turn Houndoom Dark Pulse + Kingambit Sucker Punch finish Skeledirge with Gengar still in back.

Gengar pivoted to Houndoom so Tag is off; their 4 is Gengar/Kanga(fnt)/Gambit/Houndoom. Flash Fire absorbs Torch Song and Fire Blast — never Fire Houndoom. Torch Song Gambit 56-104% plus Fire Blast 64-115% is the only guaranteed KO if both connect (either alone is a weak roll). Chople does not cut Fire. DN consecutive Protect is 1/3 and ES/Ice Beam do not KO anything; Fire Blast is the 23% DN's last useful click. Sucker Punch on DN stops Fire Blast, Sucker+Dark Pulse Dirge can stop Torch Song — still the line that actually removes Overlord Gambit. Kingambit Protect is 1/3. Heat Wave does not even KO 23% DN (10-14%) so they may spread; Dark Pulse Dirge is 50-74% under LS. Do not chain Protect.

Skeledirge at 43% is the last foe. Kingambit Sucker Punch (+1 priority, 34-60%) fires if it attacks; Houndoom Dark Pulse (48-90%, 161 Spe outspeeds) covers the case where it Protects/Slack Offs and Sucker Punch fails. Either hit alone likely KOs; together the KO is certain if it doesn't Protect, and if it Protects (reduced rate after T5) we lose nothing with Gengar still in back.

1v2. Houndoom Dark Pulse always KOs 44% Dirge (50-74% under LS) and outspeeds, so Torch Song never fires if they click it again (they just did). Sucker Punch is a 36-51% roll KO from 44% and +1. Torch Song +1 SpA does always KO 26% Gambit but we are dead before it. Protect is full rate (last Protect was T5). Sucker fails, Dark Pulse/Kowtow hit Protect, Leftovers. Do not Torch Houndoom (Flash Fire). Slack Off and Shadow Ball also lose the speed check. Pass on fainted DN. Play for a Heat Wave/Protect misclick; otherwise T8 Dark Pulse still KOs.

Skeledirge (49%) Protected last turn, so a repeat is unreliable. Houndoom Dark Pulse (48-90%) outspeeds and likely KOs; Kingambit uses Kowtow Cleave (42-72%) instead of Sucker Punch so it still connects if Skeledirge chooses Slack Off or a failed Protect. Torch Song into Kingambit (27%) would KO it, but Houndoom's hit lands first and Gengar remains in back either way.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Dark Pulse still always KOs 50% Dirge (50-74% with LS 1) and Houndoom outspeeds, so any attack or Slack Off dies before it lands. Consecutive Protect is 1/3 — the only line that is not 100% loss. Sucker failed last turn into Protect so they may Kowtow, still slower than Dark Pulse. If Protect hits, leftovers, LS expires after this turn. Pass fainted DN. Do not forfeit a 1/3.

Skeledirge has Protected twice in a row (third attempt ~1/9). Light Screen expired, so Houndoom Dark Pulse now does ~96-180% and KOs from 55% outright, moving first. Kowtow Cleave backs it up and connects even if it Slack Offs. Gengar remains in back as insurance.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: LS is gone so Dark Pulse is ~2x the old 50-74% and always KOs 56% Dirge before Torch Song/Slack Off. Consecutive Protect is 1/9 — still the only non-zero chance. They Dark Pulsed into Protect twice and Kowtowed; they will attack again. Pass fainted DN.

reflections.summary: Won with 3 pieces left (Gengar 100%, Houndoom 80%, Kingambit 27%) in 9 turns, no errors. The Gengar+Kanga lead read was correct: their Grimmsnarl+Sneasler lead could not touch Gengar, so Psychic broke Sneasler's Sash T1 (after its faster Fake Out flinched Kanga), Kanga Protect blocked the Unburden Close Combat T2 and Shadow Ball finished the trapped Sneasler. Sludge Bomb 2HKOed Grimmsnarl through Light Screen while Kanga's two Ice Punches (first breaks Multiscale) took Dragonite-Mega to 23% before Kanga died to Ice Beam. The critical pivot was T5: Grimmsnarl's Taunt had removed Gengar's Protect and Skeledirge Shadow Ball is 83-123% on Gengar, so Houndoom came in (immune to Torch Song/Fire Blast, resists Shadow Ball/Ice Beam) while Kingambit Protected; both foes Protected that turn, then Sucker Punch + Dark Pulse double KOed Dragonite and Dark Pulse finished Skeledirge after it wasted three consecutive Protects. Costs: Kanga lost (fine trade for Sneasler + Grimmsnarl + Dragonite chip); Kingambit took a Torch Song to 27%. Fire Blast was never used, likely deterred by Houndoom. Weak spots: screens + Multiscale make Gengar nearly useless into Dragonite, and Skeledirge is the one real Gengar answer they brought.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same four (all had a role) but change the lead per rule 1: expect them to adapt to Gengar+Kanga with a Skeledirge/Tauros/Rillaboom lead (Shadow Ball OHKOs Gengar, Rock Slide/Fake Out pressure) and Taunt on Gengar again. G2 lead Kangaskhan + Kingambit with Gengar + Houndoom in back: Kanga Fake Out the Fake Out/Sash user, Kingambit Iron Head OHKO Grimmsnarl / Kowtow Skeledirge, Protect T1 if Sneasler or Tauros leads (Tauros Intimidate = +2). Gengar enters only once Skeledirge is gone or Houndoom is positioned to absorb it; never leave Gengar Taunted and exposed to Skeledirge. Keep Kanga Ice Punch for Dragonite; attack into their consecutive-Protect habit rather than respecting a second Protect; use Kowtow instead of Sucker Punch when the lone foe may Protect/Slack Off.

reflections.summary: Lost G1 0-1 in 9 turns. They brought Gengar+Kanga+Gambit+Houndoom (left Altaria/Glalie) and Mega Gengar. Our Grimm+Sneasler lead vs Gengar+Kanga was right: T1 FO Kanga+LS, sash ate Psychic. T2 dual screens went up but Unburden Sneasler CC lost to Kanga Protect and Gengar Shadow Ball finished it — Sneasler never saw Gambit or Houndoom. DN Mega Ice Beamed Kanga out after two Ice Punches (Multi broken, 23%); Grimm died to the second Sludge while Tag-trapped. T5 they pivoted Gengar to Houndoom (Tag off) while we double Protected; T6 Gambit Sucker Punched 23% DN before Fire Blast, Torch Song left Gambit at 26% with +1 SpA. Dirge then 1v2 vs LO Dark Pulse (2x) + Kowtow and chained Protect until T9 failed. Decision errors 0 — the 4 was playable; the series-losing sequence was spending Sneasler into the Protect bait and ending Dirge into Flash Fire Dark.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same 4 (Sneasler, Grimm, DN, Dirge). Do not bring Combat: G1 they Mega Gengar and Defiant Gambit, Fighting is 0 vs Tag, Intimidate is +2 Atk. Do not bring Rilla: no Wash, Heat Wave 2x, Fake Out immune Gengar. G2 lead Grimm+Sneasler again. T2 if Sneasler is on sash, Protect it rather than CC 81% Kanga (they Protected that click G1) — Sneasler CC is the Houndoom/Gambit wincon and must stay. After screens, Taunt Gengar then Ice Beam Kanga; Mega DN immediately. If Gengar is Taunted and they might pivot (G1 T5 Houndoom), Dirge Shadow Ball the Gengar slot only if it stays; do not double Protect away the last Taunt turn unless Sucker+Shadow on Dirge is the obvious double. 23% DN clicks ES (+2 beats Sucker) not Fire Blast. Dirge never 1v1 Houndoom Dark Pulse; Torch Song only Gambit (Flash Fire absorbs Fire). Expect the same 4 and Mega Gengar.
