events.text: Light Screen up on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Rule 1: change the lead after a win. Kanga+Kingambit lead: Fake Out the Fake Out/Sash user, Kingambit Iron Head Grimmsnarl / Kowtow Skeledirge, Protect T1 if Sneasler/Tauros present. Gengar+Houndoom back; Houndoom pivots into Skeledirge/Dragonite Fire, Gengar closes once Skeledirge is gone.

Same 4 as G1: Grimm+Sneasler lead, DN+Dirge back. Their G2 sheet is Gengar/Kanga/Gambit/Altaria/Glalie/Houndoom — no Wash/Mence — so Rilla is unused and Combat Intimidate is blanked by Scrappy Kanga and is +2 Atk into Defiant Gambit. Dirge is the only Ghost Tag escape. T1 FO Kanga + Light Screen vs expected Gengar+Kanga mega Gengar; keep Sneasler sash for CC Houndoom/Gambit; Mega DN on first send; never Fire Houndoom.

Kanga Fake Out Sneasler: +3 priority beats Close Combat, so Sneasler either Fake Outs Kanga (no CC happens) or gets flinched with Sash broken. Either way Kingambit is safe from CC this turn, so it attacks freely: Iron Head Grimmsnarl 78-152% (halved if Prankster Reflect goes up first, still big chip). Spirit Break is resisted by Kingambit.

Kanga+Gambit is a physical lead. FO Kanga first (189 vs their FO) so they cannot flinch Grimm off Prankster Reflect or Sneasler off the Gambit sniper. Reflect must go up before Iron Head (87-125% into Grimm without it). Taunt fails vs Dark Gambit; LS waits—no specials out. Chople makes CC Gambit 70-120% a roll this turn anyway; sniping after the flinch+screen is the T2 job.

Sneasler (faster than Kanga, Sash intact) can OHKO either Kanga or Kingambit with Close Combat this turn. Kanga Protects and Kingambit pivots to Gengar (Fighting-immune, resists Dire Claw/Spirit Break) - a fully safe turn. Next turn Gengar-Mega (200 Spe) Psychics Sneasler / finishes Grimmsnarl.

Grimm 24% dies to Iron Head (58-83%) or DE (30-45%) through doubles Reflect; Ice Punch is the only save. Switch Dirge into the Grimm slot: Iron Head is 10-15%, Scrappy DE 21-31%, Kowtow 42-61%, all live. Sneasler CC Gambit (Chople 70-120% roll; berry pops even if it lives). Do not CC Kanga — guaranteed KO if they do not mega would bring Gengar onto Sneasler under Tag. Grimm 24% benches for a later LS/Taunt; do not send DN into Ice Punch.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Skeledirge Shadow Ball threatens to OHKO Gengar and Sneasler CC OHKOs every non-Gengar I have, so Gengar Protects and Mega Evolves (Shadow Tag traps Skeledirge + Sneasler for the Psychic/Sucker Punch follow-up). Kanga has no safe slot to switch into (Kingambit/Houndoom also die to CC); a second Protect (1/3) is its best salvage vs an expected CC, and it also covers a Sneasler Protect read.

Mega Gengar Shadow Ball is 83-117% into Dirge and outspeeds, so clicking Shadow Ball this turn can donate Dirge without a KO. Protect Dirge. Sneasler CC Kanga is a guaranteed KO at 84% (they already Protected; consecutive is 1/3; they mega Gengar not Kanga). Do not switch DN — Ice Beam/Fire Blast do not KO Gengar and Tag would glue DN+Sneasler with no Ghost on field. Psychic pops sash but Sneasler still KOs Kanga first or after. Next turn Dirge Shadow Balls Gengar.

Skeledirge is the only piece that threatens Gengar-Mega (Shadow Ball 83-123%) and it just Protected. Gengar moves first: Shadow Ball 75-141%. Kanga is dead to CC in any slot anyway (Protect streak 2 = 1/9), so its action only matters if Sneasler doesn't CC it - then Scrappy Double-Edge (21-37% through Reflect, moves before Skeledirge) guarantees the Skeledirge KO before it can fire Shadow Ball. With Skeledirge gone, Sneasler can't touch Gengar and Psychic/Sucker Punch clean up.

Kingambit in: Sucker Punch (+1) chips the Sash-holding Sneasler first so Gengar's Psychic then KOs it before Close Combat; Kingambit also resists Grimmsnarl/Dragonite's options and is immune to Prankster status. Houndoom would just die to CC.

They Protected both last turn so they attack this turn. Kanga Protect is ~1/9; CC into 84% is a guaranteed KO if it hits. Do not chain Dirge Protect (W1 lesson). Shadow Ball Mega Gengar (66-124%). If they Psychic Sneasler (G1 line), sash pops, Kanga dies, Dirge still fires. If they Shadow Ball Dirge it is an 83-117% race we have to take — Dirge is the only Gengar KO and cannot leave Sneasler glued without a Ghost on the field. Do not switch DN into Tag.

Dirge fainted to the predicted Shadow Ball; Kanga is down. Sneasler is Tag-glued and cannot hit Gengar, so send Mega DN (Multiscale lives Shadow/Psychic/Sludge 13-27%) not 24% Grimm (dies to Sludge). Next turn mega immediately, Sneasler CCs the incoming (Gambit/Houndoom/Glalie) or Protects if they Psychic the sash. Grimm stays for a later LS/Taunt if someone faints.

Sneasler has CC'd three turns straight and Kingambit is a 4x target, so it will very likely attack: Sucker Punch (+1) lands 19-39% first (Sash is gone once HP isn't full), then Gengar (200, fastest) Psychics for the KO before Close Combat happens. Kingambit survives a non-crit Dragonite Fire Blast (68-96%). If Sneasler Protects instead, we lose little and Protect Kingambit next turn.

Mega on first attacking send. Sneasler CC Gambit (Chople 70-120% roll, berry pops). Mega DN Fire Blast Gambit (64-115% Fire, Chople does not cut it) so the pair KOs if they do not Protect. ES is 5-10% into Steel; Ice Beam does not KO Gengar. Sneasler cannot switch (Tag). Sucker Punch first does 27-38% and does not stop CC; Psychic pops sash after, CC still fires. Protecting DN keeps Multiscale but lets Gambit live — Sucker Punch killed 23% DN in G1. Do not make 85% Fire Blast the only KO.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Gengar (fastest) Sludge Bombs Grimmsnarl for a guaranteed KO from 24% even through a Prankster Light Screen. Kingambit at 19% Protects against Fire Blast (ESpeed only does 7-10% anyway). Then 3v1 vs Dragonite-Mega: break Multiscale with Shadow Ball/Sucker Punch, Houndoom absorbs Fire Blast.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Dragonite-Mega)
decisions.rationale: ES is 5-10% and cannot KO 18% Gambit; Ice Beam is a roll. Fire Blast guaranteed KO at 18% (85% acc). Grimm 24% dies to Sludge or Iron Head, so Prankster LS first (+1) — last chance for Light Clay vs Gengar specials. Taunt Gengar loses the screen and does not stop this turn's Protect (+4). Do not Protect DN: 18% Gambit with Sucker Punch must die now. Multiscale likely breaks; that is the cost of removing Gambit.

3v1 vs Dragonite-Mega. Dragonite has Fire Blasted Kingambit's slot two turns running: switch Houndoom in to absorb it (Flash Fire boost, immune) and keep Kingambit alive as a Sucker Punch reserve; Houndoom outspeeds Dragonite (161 > 152) and resists nothing dangerous except ESpeed 37-53%. Gengar Sludge Bomb (90 BP, 30% poison chip) breaks Multiscale through Light Screen.

Gambit Protected last turn so consecutive is 1/3; Fire Blast still guaranteed KO at 18% if it hits. ES cannot KO; Ice Beam is a roll. Do not Protect as the 1v2 — Multiscale+LS lives Gengar 12-16% anyway, and the 4th (Glalie Ice Shard) must come in on remaining Multi if possible. Grimm Pass.

Multiscale broken, Dragonite 70% and poisoned. Gengar Sludge Bomb + Houndoom LO Dark Pulse (both neutral; Heat Wave is resisted) plus poison chip should finish it; if it Protects, poison ticks and we repeat next turn. Both outspeed Dragonite and it can't OHKO either.

1v2 poisoned DN, Multiscale broken. Gengar and likely Timid Houndoom both outspeed. Protect this turn then they KO from 57% next turn before we move — zero attacks. Must Ice Beam Gengar now (31-56%, 100% acc). Fire Blast Houndoom is Flash Fire immune; Fire Blast Gengar is 85% as the only hit. ES Gengar is 0. Dark Pulse+Sludge is 48-69% into 70% so we can live and fire one Ice Beam. Grimm Pass.

reflections.summary: Series won 2-0 (G1 with 3 left in 9 turns, G2 with 3 left in 8 turns). Main reason: preparation matched the matchup exactly. grok's six (open sheet) had no Dark attack, so Mega Gengar was untouchable by Sneasler/Grimmsnarl/Rillaboom and only Skeledirge (Shadow Ball) and Dragonite (Ice Beam/Fire Blast) could hurt it. Both games we brought the same four (Gengar, Kangaskhan, Kingambit, Houndoom) and the same core loop worked: Kingambit Iron Head Grimmsnarl (76% T1 in G2), Gengar Psychic 4x Sneasler, Shadow Ball Skeledirge, Houndoom Flash Fire absorbing Dragonite Fire Blast, then a double-target on Dragonite once Multiscale was broken. grok brought the identical four and the identical Grimmsnarl+Sneasler lead in both games and never adapted; they screen-spammed while losing tempo and Protected predictably (Skeledirge Protect T3 in G2 = free Shadow Ball KO T4). The between-game adjustment (swap the lead to Kanga+Kingambit, keep the back) helped: Iron Head crippled Grimmsnarl T1, and the T2 pivot Kingambit->Gengar into Sneasler's Close Combat (with Kanga Protect) gained a full free turn. Cost: Kangaskhan was sacrificed T4 (no safe slot vs Sash Sneasler CC) and Kingambit took a Fire Blast to 19% T5 - acceptable trades since Gengar+Houndoom cleaned 3v1. Zero decision errors; every turn was calc-backed. Minor imperfection: Kanga's T1 Fake Out lost the speed race to Sneasler as expected, so Kanga contributed nothing in G2; the slot itself was the weak point both games.
reflections.adjustment: Against grok in a future series: keep Gengar as the mega whenever their six lacks Dark attacks; keep the Kingambit Iron Head / Gengar Psychic+Shadow Ball / Houndoom Flash Fire package. Expect them to repeat their exact bring and lead across games - don't over-adjust; only rotate our lead. Improve the Kangaskhan slot: vs Sash Sneasler leads Kanga cannot win the Fake Out war, so consider leading Gengar+Kingambit (Kingambit Protect T1, Gengar Psychic) or bringing a different fourth if Skeledirge is absent from their preview. Plan the Sneasler answer as Sucker Punch chip + Psychic (worked T5) rather than Fake Out. If they ever bring Tauros/Rillaboom, Kingambit Defiant vs Intimidate and Houndoom Heat Wave vs Rillaboom are ready.

reflections.summary:
Lost the series 0-2 to the same four both games: Timid Mega Gengar (Gengarite Sludge/Shadow/Psychic/Protect), Jolly Scrappy Kanga (not mega; FO/DE/Ice Punch/Protect), Adamant Chople Defiant Gambit (Kowtow/Iron Head/Sucker/Protect), Timid LO Flash Fire Houndoom (Heat Wave/Dark Pulse/Snarl/Protect). They left Altaria+Glalie both games. That four fully answers our bring: Psychic 4x Sneasler, Shadow Ball 2x Dirge (Gengar outspeeds), Sludge Grimm, Ice Punch DN, Scrappy hits Dirge, Flash Fire blanks Fire, Dark Pulse 2x Dirge, Sucker after chip.

G2 they changed lead to Kanga+Gambit. T1 FO+Reflect was right; doubles Reflect only cuts 1/3, so Iron Head still 2HKOd Grimm (49/202). T2 we switched Dirge and CCd the Gambit slot; they switched Gengar into the CC (immune) while Kanga Protected — the tempo loss of the game. T3 they double Protected into our Dirge Protect. T4 Gengar Shadow Ball KO’d Dirge as Sneasler KO’d Kanga; with the only Ghost dead, Tag glued Sneasler+DN. T5 Sucker Punch chipped Sneasler off full HP, then Psychic KO’d before CC (sash is full-HP only). Fire Blast left Gambit at 18%. T6 Gambit Protected the follow-up; Grimm got LS up and died to Sludge. T7 they sent Houndoom into the Fire Blast slot (Flash Fire). Poisoned 1v2 DN died T8 after one Ice Beam to 52% Gengar.

Between-game adjustment was “same 4, FO Kanga, keep Sneasler, Dirge only Torch Songs Gambit.” It backfired: they pivoted Gengar into Dirge, anti-sashed Sneasler, and Flash-Fired the Gambit-slot Fire Blast. Combat stayed benched (Scrappy/Defiant blank Intimidate); Rilla stayed benched.
reflections.adjustment: Do not lock Grimm+Sneasler+DN+Dirge as the only 4 vs this sheet. Dirge does not wall Scrappy Kanga and cannot stay in vs Mega Gengar — if Gengar megas, Dirge Protects or leaves; never Shadow Ball into a faster Shadow Ball. Sneasler vs Gengar+Gambit: Protect the sash. Sucker-then-Psychic is their sash break; CC never fires if Psychic KOs after chip. Do not CC the Gambit slot when they can send Gengar into it. Do not Fire Blast a slot Houndoom can enter. Modest ES does not KO 18% Chople Gambit. Chople makes Sneasler CC a 70-120% roll, not a sniper OHKO. Rilla Fake Out lets Sneasler CC Gambit T1 without using FO. Rocky Helmet Combat still chips Kanga contact even though Scrappy/Defiant blank Intimidate. Bring a second Ghost (Rotom) if Tag must be escaped after Dirge dies. Never Fire Houndoom.

decisions.rationale: Lead Incin+Noivern for Intim+FakeOut to stop Talon TW (FakeOut Talon breaks GaleWings/Sash) and set our TW; back Excadrill+Rotom for MoldBreaker EQ/RockSlide + LeafStorm/Thunder synergy (Rotom immune EQ) covering Meta/Mamo/Talon/Rotom-F/Arcanine, CC/FlareBlitz for Scrafty/Meta. Bench Pincurchin (Electric walled by Mamo Ground, slow) and Tinkaton (less needed without Prim/Hydreigon).

Lead Mamoswine + Talonflame vs muse. Pincurchin's Electric Surge is their engine and Mamoswine is Electric-immune with STAB Expert Belt High Horsepower 2x on Pincurchin/Incineroar/Excadrill/Tinkaton — it removes the terrain setter turn 1. Talonflame sets priority Tailwind to win the speed war against Noivern, and her Focus Sash lets her eat one Rock Slide/Flare Blitz. Accept an Incineroar/Tinkaton Fake Out on Talonflame (Mamoswine still kills Pincurchin) — Talonflame re-sets Tailwind turn 2. Back line Metagross (immune Poison, resists Fairy/Dragon/Flying, walls Tinkaton's Play Rough and Noivern's Air Slash, Ice Punch 4x Noivern) and Rotom-Frost (0.5x Electric resist + Ground immunity, Blizzard 4x Noivern/2x Excadrill). Left home Arcanine (2x weak to Excadrill EQ and Incineroar) and Scrafty (4x Fairy from Tinkaton).

FakeOut Talon stops GaleWings +1 Tailwind/Taunt/Flare (priority +3 beats +1), letting Noivern Tailwind go up. Tool: IceShard 56-83% + Flare 10-17% = max 99% so Noivern survives even double without using Sash; HHP 31-45% into Shuca Incin safe. Denies their TW, sets ours.

Their lead is Incineroar + Noivern, not Incineroar + Pincurchin, so their Tailwind setter is on the field turn 1. Plan: deny Noivern and pop its Focus Sash. Talonflame (195 Spe) outspeeds Noivern (max 192), so Taunt resolves first and stops Noivern's Tailwind AND its Protect for 3 turns, forcing it into Air Slash only. Mamoswine's Expert Belt Icicle Crash is 4x on Noivern and will force the Focus Sash, leaving it at 1 HP so an Ice Shard/Vacuum-style priority can finish it next turn. Accepting an Incineroar Fake Out flinch on Talonflame as the main risk; even then Mamoswine still pops Noivern's Sash, and Talonflame can re-Taunt/Tailwind turn 2. Keeping Mamoswine in is fine — Thick Fat halves Incineroar's Flare Blitz to neutral, and only Close Combat is a real threat.

Noivern at 1% dies to IceShard priority, must switch; switch resolves first so incoming takes hit. Excadrill safer than Rotom vs predicted Ice into slot (IceShard 17-25% vs 24-58%, Crash ~50% vs 50-117% OHKO) since Mamo won't HHP Noivern-immune slot. Incin CC Mamo 58-106% best vs ThickFat (Flare 44-81% halved), Lariat can't KO Talon 38-75% vs 77% +sash. Preserve TW, bring Exca 308 to RockSlide Talon next.

Turn 2: their Tailwind is up (3 turns), Noivern is at 1% (Focus Sash burned) and Incineroar's Fake Out is spent. Talonflame must set my own Tailwind now to stop their doubled Excadrill/Rotom-Mow/Tinkaton from running over Mamoswine (100) and Rotom-Frost (106). I verified Incineroar cannot KO Talonflame from 77% (Darkest Lariat 50-74%, Flare Blitz 0.5x, Close Combat 0.5x) and cannot KO Mamoswine either (Close Combat 63-90%), so both of my moves resolve. Mamoswine uses priority Ice Shard (+1) into Noivern: it KOs the 1% Noivern before it can act (denying any re-Tailwind/Taunt) and, if Noivern Protects instead, it wastes its turn anyway and my Tailwind still lands. This nets me speed control plus removal of their Tailwind setter.

Mamo 17% KO by Lariat 31-57% without further Def drops/recoil. Exca 77% dies if doubled before moving (Shard priority first 17-25% then Talon guaranteed first Flare 62-96%), so Protect to scout/stall while Incin removes Mamo. Incin takes 15-23% Flare +8-12% Shard safely. Preserve Exca 77% for RockSlide vs Talon next with TW.

Turn 3 crisis: Excadrill (Mold Breaker, Life Orb) is on the field and Rock Slide is 4x on Talonflame (120-174%, guaranteed KO, and Focus Sash is dead because Talonflame is at 77%), while Iron Head/Earthquake both KO the 17% Mamoswine. Mamoswine is slower than Excadrill once Tailwind is up (Excadrill 236-308 vs Mamoswine 200), so a +0 High Horsepower would never land — it must use priority Ice Shard (+1), which resolves before anything else and chips Excadrill ~23% for free. Talonflame (390 with Tailwind) then Flare Blitz (2x on Ground/Steel) before Excadrill moves: Ice Shard chip + Flare Blitz (49.8-97.3%) reliably removes the 77% Excadrill, which is the only way to keep Talonflame alive this turn since Excadrill's Rock Slide otherwise kills it. Accept Mamoswine dying to Incineroar (it was effectively gone at 17% and has no good target: HH on Incineroar is halved by Shuca for only 30-55%). Removing Excadrill also protects Mega Metagross from Earthquake later.

Excadrill Protected and lived at 77% while Mamoswine traded itself. I send out Rotom-Frost, not Metagross: Rotom-Frost is my expendable body that can actually finish Excadrill (STAB Thunderbolt ~50-55% on Excadrill's low base-65 SpD, combined with Talonflame's Flare Blitz 49.8-97.3% that is a guaranteed kill on the 77% Excadrill next turn unless it Protects), while keeping undamaged Mega Metagross in reserve as the wincon — Metagross is 2x weak to Incineroar's Close Combat/Flare Blitz and Excadrill's Earthquake, so feeding it into this exact board is bad. Rotom-Frost also resists Electric 0.5x for their Pincurchin/Rotom-Mow if that is their 4th, and its Sitrus Berry plus 157 HP lets it eat a spread Rock Slide (2x, ~60%) and still act. Talonflame must Flare Blitz Excadrill next turn because Excadrill's Rock Slide is a guaranteed 4x KO on it. Keep Rotom-Frost away from Incineroar's Close Combat/Flare Blitz (2x, ~100% KO) by acting before it where possible.

Last own TW turn, must trade. Rock 41-77% + CC 66-125% =107-200% KO Rotom-F even through Sitrus, while Rock 93-177% breaks Talon sash to 1 and Incin last finishes 1HP? Actually Incin targets Rotom-F so Talon stays at 1. Exca 308 outruns Rotom-F 212-276 but Talon 320-390 first with 62-96% Flare vs 77% (56% KO) risk accepted; Blizzard 41-59% after Rock still lets Rock go. CC no recoil preserves Incin vs Tbolt 49-72%+Flare 15-23%.

Must replace fainted Exca; send healthy Rotom-Mow over 1% Noivern to take hits with Incin Pass. Incin 49% walls Meta (Zen immune, Mash/Ice 0.5x) and Talon Flare 0.5x, Rotom threatens Talon Thunder next. Preserve Noivern 1% for later TW sac.

Verified: Thunderbolt/Volt Switch are 0x into Excadrill (Ground) — Rotom-Frost's only hit on it is Blizzard — while Incineroar's Flare Blitz is a guaranteed OHKO on Rotom-Frost (100.6-149%) and Close Combat is 67.5-99.4%. So staying in with Rotom-Frost risks losing my only Incineroar answer. Turn order is Talonflame (390) > Excadrill (236-308) > Rotom-Frost (212) > Incineroar (160-224), so Rotom-Frost eats the Rock Slide (43-61%, Sitrus covers it) but still moves before Incineroar: Volt Switch into Incineroar chips 36-65% and pulls Rotom-Frost off the field, so Incineroar's attack loses its target and Metagross (immune-level Rock Slide 0.5x, 7-9.6%) comes in at 100%. Talonflame must Flare Blitz Excadrill — it is the only thing that can stop the 4x Rock Slide KO, and it 2x's for 49.8-97.3%. I keep Metagross un-Mega'd but safe so it can Mega Evolve next turn and use Meteor Mash 37.6-67.6% (Incineroar is at -1 Def) and Ice Punch 33.2-63.8% on Excadrill.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Opp double Rotom is guaranteed KO (Ice 60-85%+Flare 56-88%=116% min) and double Incin KOs (Meteor 37-53%+Flare 15-23%=52% min vs 49%). Protect Rotom baits preferred double Rotom (both 2x vs Rotom, 0.5x vs Incin) into block, letting Incin last Flare 74-128% vs 66% KO Meta. Volt would break Talon sash but lose Rotom for Meta trade leaving losing endgame; preserving 100% Rotom for Talon+Rotom-F next with TW expiring is higher EV.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Verified: Metagross-Mega Meteor Mash KOs the 49% Incineroar at both endpoints (49.5-90%) — it is at -2 Def/-2 SpD after two Close Combats, and Mega Metagross outspeeds both foes with my last Tailwind turn. Removing Incineroar also removes the only real threat to Metagross (Flare Blitz 2x 62-93%, Darkest Lariat 2x 44.9-67.4%) since Rotom-Mow's Leaf Storm only does 20.3-30.5% to Mega Metagross. On Talonflame I switch to Rotom-Frost rather than stay: Talonflame's Flare Blitz only does 49.7-91.2% to Rotom-Mow (no KO) and then Rotom-Mow's Thunder/Volt Switch is a guaranteed 2x KO back on Talonflame, so attacking would trade Talonflame for ~70% of Rotom-Mow. Switching keeps all three of my remaining bodies: Rotom-Frost resists Electric (takes only ~20% from a retargeted Thunder) and Rotom-Mow is no threat to either Metagross or Rotom-Frost. Next turn Mega Metagross Ice Punch (65-120%, 2x) plus Rotom-Frost Blizzard (2x) close out Rotom-Mow and the 1% Noivern.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Noivern 1% dies to any Ice (125-237%) but 192 first sets TW before dying for Rotom comeback vs Talon. Rotom dies to double Ice (Blizzard 79-116% + IcePunch 60-85%=139% min) or single Blizzard high roll, so reduced Protect to preserve 100% HP for TW turns; attacking now leaves 21% and still 1v3 vs Meta66%+RotomF100%+Talon46% with resists (Leaf 50-94% vs Frost, Thunder 35-63% vs Mega). Only path is TW+full HP+opp misses.

Incineroar is dead; only a 1% Noivern and a fresh Rotom-Mow remain against my three. Metagross-Mega Ice Punch is 2x on Rotom-Mow (65-120%, ~50-70% KO alone) and Rotom-Frost Blizzard is also 2x on Rotom-Mow (STAB, spread) while being 4x on Noivern — so Blizzard plus Ice Punch removes both foes this turn if Blizzard connects (70% acc). Rotom-Frost's Thunderbolt is only 0.25x on Rotom-Mow, so Blizzard is the right move. Even in the bad branch (Blizzard misses, or Rotom-Mow Protects with reduced success), Noivern is at 1% and Rotom-Mow cannot meaningfully threaten Metagross-Mega (Leaf Storm 20-30%, Rock/Fighting irrelevant) or Rotom-Frost (Electric 0.5x), and I have Talonflame in reserve plus two more bodies to clean up. No accuracy or coverage reason to use anything but Ice Punch + Blizzard here.

reflections.summary: Lost 0-3 (Meta66%+Frost100%+Talon46% left). T1 FakeOut Talon+TW worked but Icicle crit put Noivern to 1% (sash gone). T2 switch to Exca+CC Mamo to 17% while they set TW (lost TW race ours expires first). T3 Protect+KO Mamo good. T4 aggressive Rock+CC failed: Talon faster Flare KO'd Exca 77% (62-96% high roll) before Rock, Frost Volt 51% to Incin then pivoted to Meta (CC 34%). T5 Protect Rotom+Flare Meta read wrong: they targeted Incin (Meteor 37-53% vs -2 KO) not Rotom double, Mega'd, switched Talon->Frost, Incin died before Flare (73-128% KO would have hit). T6 TW+Protect fail, double Ice KO'd both. Frost Volt pivot + Mega bulk + Talon faster Flare were difference.
reflections.adjustment: Keep same 4 (Incin/Noivern/Exca/Rotom) bench Pincurchin (walled by Mamo) /Tinkaton (0.5x vs Meta/Talon). Keep lead Incin+Noivern vs Mamo+Talon. Change piloting: preserve Incin bulk (Flare/Lariat vs Meta, no 2x CC to -2 that made Meteor KO), Protect Exca vs faster Talon Flare KO range instead of Rocking into 56% death, double Frost before Volt pivot (Rock 41-77%+Leaf 50-94%). Play for TW parity not early trade.

reflections.summary: Game 1 won, 3-0 in bodies (only Mamoswine fainted; all four of muse's brought mons fainted). My team-preview read was wrong — I expected the Incineroar+Pincurchin terrain lead, but muse brought Incineroar/Noivern/Excadrill/Rotom-Mow with NO Pincurchin, NO Tinkaton, no terrain, no hazards and no Mega. That was fine because Mamoswine+Talonflame is a good answer to Incineroar+Noivern anyway: T1 Icicle Crash (4x, crit) forced Noivern's Focus Sash to 1% while Talonflame ate the Fake Out; T2 set my own Tailwind (guaranteed, since Fake Out was spent) and chipped Excadrill with priority Ice Shard; T3 I doubled Excadrill which exploited its Protect and cost both moves, but Mamoswine was on 17% and had no other good target; T4 Talonflame's Flare Blitz removed Excadrill and Rotom-Frost's Volt Switch chipped Incineroar to 49% while pivoting Metagross in — note the foe's Close Combat RETARGETED to the incoming Metagross, so the pivot did not dodge, but at 33% damage it was a fine price; T5 Mega Metagross Meteor Mash KO'd the -2 Def Incineroar outright; T6 Ice Punch + Blizzard swept Rotom-Mow and the 1% Noivern. No decision errors or simulator substitutions reported. Sequence discipline was the win: I never stacked both attacks into a predicted Protect after T3, and I kept Mega Metagross off the field until Incineroar's Fire/Dark 2x threat was removed.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same core four (Mamoswine / Talonflame / Metagross / Rotom-Frost) and the same Mamoswine+Talonflame lead for game 2, but expect muse to change after that loss: they registered Pincurchin (Electric Surge) and Tinkaton but didn't bring them, so either could replace Rotom-Mow or Excadrill. Do not plan around Talonflame acting turn 1 — muse opened Fake Out on her both weeks of evidence, so price Talonflame's first turn at zero and let Mamoswine carry the opening. If they lead Tinkaton, consider swapping Scrafty in for Rotom-Frost is NOT viable (4x Fairy) — bring Arcanine instead for Intimidate + Flare Blitz 2x, and use Mamoswine's Ground 2x on Tinkaton. Key correction to my own thinking: pivoting does not dodge — opposing single-target moves retarget to the switch-in, so use pivot moves for tempo/damage, not as a Protect substitute.

decisions.rationale: Same 4 per plan: lead Incin+Noivern to FakeOut Talon + TW vs Mamo+Talon, Exca+Rotom back for Rock/Volt coverage.

Game 2, leading 1-0. Repeat the G1-winning four: Mamoswine + Talonflame leads, Metagross + Rotom-Frost in back. Mamoswine is Electric-Immune and HH is 2x on Pincurchin/Incineroar/Excadrill/Tinkaton (the likely wildcard swaps), and Icicle Crash 4x forces Noivern's Focus Sash. Talonflame's turn 1 is priced at zero (they Fake Out her) but her Gale Wings Tailwind (+1) re-sets speed control and she outruns Noivern under Tailwind. Metagross held back so Incineroar's 2x Fire/Dark and Excadrill's Life Orb EQ can't reach it turn 1; Rotom-Frost held back for its Electric resistance, Blizzard 4x Noivern, and Thunderbolt pressure on Incineroar/Rotom-Mow. No notebook change needed — the existing plan covers this line.
FakeOut Talon stops GaleWings TW (FakeOut +3 beats +1), Noivern TW sets ours first; Sash covers IceShard. Per plan lead vs Mamo+Talon.

Mamoswine Icicle Crash -> Noivern: 122-228% from full, which triggers the Focus Sash, so Noivern is left at 1 HP and dies to any follow-up (Ice Shard +1 next turn, Blizzard, or Flare Blitz). Talonflame Taunt -> Noivern: she is guaranteed faster (195 vs Noivern's 157-192) at equal priority, so Taunt lands before their Tailwind and denies it for three turns, plus it kills Noivern's reactive Protect habit. If they repeat G1's Fake Out on Talonflame, Taunt is simply wasted with no loss; if they instead Fake Out Mamoswine (also plausible, to save Noivern), Taunt neuters their speed control while Mamoswine still connects. Tailwind here is strictly worse: it only cancels out their Tailwind (relative speeds unchanged), whereas Taunt denies theirs entirely and leaves me free to set Tailwind turn 2 with Gale Wings priority for a real speed edge. No notebook change.
CC 58-105% > Flare 44-81% vs ThickFat Mamo, TW Incin outruns Mamo. Switch 1% Noivern to Exca preserves re-TW, Exca gets TW boost. Talon Gale Wings inactive at 76% so no priority TW.

Mamoswine Ice Shard -> Noivern (index 7) and Talonflame Tailwind (index 0). Ice Shard is +1 priority, so it resolves before any Noivern action at priority 0 (Taunt/Air Slash/Tailwind) and kills the 1% Noivern (59.9-111.3% of max HP; it is already at 1% with the Focus Sash consumed). Noivern is immune to High Horsepower, so Ice Shard is the only reliable kill. The only thing that stops it is Protect (+4), and in that exact branch Talonflame's Tailwind still resolves because Tailwind targets my own side and is unaffected by Protect. Confirmed via compare_action_order that Gale Wings is INACTIVE at 77% HP, so Talonflame's Tailwind is priority 0 and Noivern is faster under their Tailwind - meaning a Taunt would block it; Ice Shard killing Noivern first is what protects the Tailwind. Setting my Tailwind now gives me turns 2-5 vs their 2-4, a solo-speed window on turn 5, and cancels any re-set they attempt. Removing Noivern permanently ends their Tailwind re-arm and Air Slash chip. No notebook change.
Exca dies to HHP 96-135% or high Flare 62-96%+Shard, while Flare vs Incin only 14-23%. Protect Exca to block Talon+Mamo focus, Lariat KOs 19% Mamo without CC drops or Flare recoil vs ThickFat.

Both of my active moves go into Excadrill. Mamoswine Ice Shard (index 7) is +1 priority, so it resolves before Excadrill's Rock Slide/Iron Head and before Incineroar, guaranteeing Mamoswine contributes before it dies (Mamoswine is at 20% and Excadrill's Iron Head and Rock Slide both KO it; High Horsepower would never fire since Excadrill 236-308 outruns Mamoswine 200 and Incineroar 160-224 may also). Talonflame Flare Blitz -> Excadrill (index 2): she is guaranteed to move first (390 vs 236-308). Ice Shard's ~13-18% chip lowers the pool to ~62%, making Flare Blitz (49.8-97.3% of max) a ~75-80% KO rather than ~43%. Killing Excadrill before its Rock Slide protects BOTH slots - Rock Slide KOs Mamoswine (2x at 20%) and Talonflame (4x at 77%), so this is a double-KO prevention, not just damage. Protecting Mamoswine instead only delays a doomed mon and leaves Excadrill free to Rock Slide Talonflame. Only real risk is Excadrill Protecting, which is the price of the guaranteed-approach line; splitting into Incineroar would waste Mamoswine's turn in the far more likely attack branch. No notebook change.

Send in Metagross (index 0); Talonflame passes. Metagross is the far better body to absorb this turn's fire: Excadrill's Rock Slide does only 10.2-14.4% to it (vs 46.5-104% to Rotom-Frost), and it survives Iron Head too, whereas Rotom-Frost eats 81.5-187.2% from Incineroar's Flare Blitz. Metagross also contributes real damage: Ice Punch does 24-46.5% (33.2-63.8% as Tough Claws Mega) to the 77% Excadrill, which stacked with Talonflame's guaranteed-first Flare Blitz (49.8-97.3%) makes Excadrill's death this turn highly likely and possibly before its Rock Slide resolves. I deliberately keep Rotom-Frost at 100% in back because it is my only genuine Incineroar breaker (Thunderbolt 37.1-83.5% into Incineroar's -1 SpD, while Metagross's Meteor Mash is 0.5x and Talonflame's Flare Blitz only 10-19%), so exposing it to Incineroar's Flare Blitz now would risk losing the only tool that can finish Incineroar. No notebook change.

Rock 93-176% guarantees Talon sash break to 1, Flare 73-127% (65-112% mega) heavy Meta while TW up. Covers Talon Protect (Flare still hits Meta) and Meta Protect (Rock still breaks sash). 1HP Talon next picked by FakeOut +3.
Exca fainted before Rock, Talon 45% sash intact, Meta gone. Send 100% Rotom (Volt 49% min KOs 45% to sash) over 1% Noivern; replacement turn no damage.

Metagross Ice Punch -> Excadrill + Mega Evolve (index 15); Talonflame Flare Blitz -> Excadrill (index 2). This is a guaranteed KO: the minimum evaluated rolls are 49.8% (Flare Blitz) + 33.2% (Tough Claws Ice Punch) = 83% of Excadrill's max HP, already above its current 77%, and both moves are 100% accurate. Talonflame is guaranteed to act first (390 vs Excadrill 236-308), and Mega Metagross at 260 may also outrun Excadrill, in which case Excadrill dies before its Rock Slide and Talonflame survives too. Mega Evolving is free value here: Metagross is my only stone holder in this four, it is already on the field and committed, Tough Claws raises Ice Punch from 24-46.5% to 33.2-63.8%, and the speed bump from 180 to 260 matters for both this turn and the solo-Tailwind turn 5. Metagross's Meteor Mash is only 0.5x on Excadrill and Zen Headbutt is 0.5x, so Ice Punch is by far the best move. The main risk, Excadrill Protecting, is halved by its reduced success rate after last turn's use, and if it fails the Protect they simply waste their action while both my hits land. No notebook change.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Their TW last turn both outspeed: double Rotom 117% min KOs before Volt, double Incin 35-56% vs 40% can KO before Flare. Stall TW with Incin->Noivern sac (clears -1/-1, re-Intimidates on return) + Rotom Protect (100% first use). Preserves 40% Incin + 100% Rotom for no-TW fight.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Rotom-Frost Thunderbolt -> Incineroar (index 0); Talonflame Flare Blitz -> Rotom-Mow (index 2). Both my mons move first this turn (Talonflame 390, Rotom-Frost 212, both above Rotom-Mow 116-151 and Incineroar 80-112), so all my damage lands before either foe acts. Thunderbolt into Incineroar's current 40% is 46-83.5%, a KO at both evaluated endpoints, and it is 100% accurate, so Incineroar dies deterministically. Flare Blitz into Rotom-Mow is 49.7-91.2% at 100% accuracy, leaving it at 9-50%. Crucially Rotom-Mow cannot kill Rotom-Frost: Leaf Storm caps at 49.7-74.5% and its Electric moves are only 0.5x, so Rotom-Frost is guaranteed to survive the turn at 25%+ and still hold a 65-120% Blizzard for the cleanup. I chose the deterministic split over a Blizzard line because Blizzard is only 70% accurate: missing would leave Rotom-Mow untouched at 100% while Incineroar survived to KO one of mine. Also note Incineroar at ~20% using Flare Blitz would suicide to recoil, so the residual risk is small. No notebook change.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Protect+Flare: Incin 40% survives double 24-38% max to fire Flare 99-187% (90% OHKO Frost, Sitrus only saves min), Rotom Protect blocks double Rotom 120% min KO. Preserves both for 2v1 vs Talon. Covers Frost/Talon Protect wastes.

Rotom-Frost Blizzard (index 3, hits both) and Talonflame Flare Blitz -> Rotom-Mow (index 2). Rotom-Mow dies this turn: Talonflame's 2x Flare Blitz is 35.7-68.8% and Blizzard is 65-120% on it, so the minimum combined is 100.7% - a guaranteed KO, and Blizzard is the only move on my side that can touch Rotom-Mow at all (its own Thunderbolt/Volt Switch are 0.25x). Blizzard also chips Incineroar 13.9-25.3%, leaving it around 15-26%, where Rotom-Frost's Thunderbolt (30.2-55.3%, min above that range) is a guaranteed follow-up kill. Critically, Incineroar cannot KO Rotom-Frost: Close Combat caps at 67.5-99.4% and Darkest Lariat at 36.3-52.2%, and Rotom-Frost still holds its Sitrus Berry, so Rotom-Frost survives to fire Thunderbolt; if Incineroar instead uses Flare Blitz, its own recoil (~52 HP, about 28% of its max) kills it from ~20%. Doing it the other way round (killing Incineroar first) is worse: Rotom-Mow would survive at 100% and Rotom-Frost loses that 1v1, since Rotom-Mow is faster (116-151 vs 106) and Blizzard only OHKOs it 36% of the time from full while Leaf Storm 2HKOs back. Their bench is empty (Noivern and Excadrill fainted), so killing Rotom-Mow here removes half of their remaining team outright. No notebook change.

reflections.summary: Lost G2 (6 turns) and series 0-2. Early plan worked: FakeOut broke Gale Wings TW, CC+Lariat KO Mamo, crit Flare KO MegaMeta. Decisive failures: T4 Exca Rock never fired because Talon TW 320-390 outruns Exca 308 and KO'd it, leaving Talon sash intact all game (45%->27%); T5 Noivern sac stalled TW and re-Intimidated to -2 but lost TW reset; T6 second consecutive Protect failed as warned, so Flare+Blizzard KO'd Rotom, and low-HP Flare KO'd Frost but recoil suicided Incin, leaving Talon 27% vs nothing. Same-4 adjustment preserved answers but backfired on speed – no out to Talon+Frost without Rock/Volt breaking sash.
reflections.adjustment: Future vs deepseek: do not bring same 4 passive into Talon TW. Need Rock breaker that outruns Talon under TW (Noivern TW+1 beats TW0 only if FakeOut breaks first; Exca 308 loses to Talon 320-390 so Rock never fires). Bring Pincurchin TWave to halve Talon/Meta or Tinkaton FakeOut/Encore + Skarm Sturdy TW. Never consecutive Protect (warned reduced, failed T6). With Incin <20% do not Flare (recoil suicide vs Frost left Talon 27% to win) – Lariat/protect to preserve vs Talon. Bring Thunder/Volt to break sash before Flare.

reflections.summary:
Won the series 2-0 (G1: only Mamoswine fainted, all four of theirs down; G2: won with a 28% Talonflame as my sole survivor).

Why:
1. The team-selection read was right: muse registered an Electric-Terrain/hazard shell (Pincurchin + Tinkaton) but brought the SAME four in both games - Incineroar/Noivern/Excadrill/Rotom-Mow, no terrain, no hazards, no Mega. Mamoswine/Talonflame/Metagross/Rotom-Frost covered that core directly.
2. Mamoswine was insurance that paid off sideways - Pincurchin never appeared, but Ice Shard (+1) was my only way to hit Excadrill before it moved (Excadrill outruns Mamoswine even under Tailwind) and Icicle Crash forced Noivern's Focus Sash turn 1.
3. Rotom-Frost was the MVP: Electric resist, Ground immunity, Thunderbolt on Incineroar, and spread Blizzard (4x Noivern, 2x Rotom-Mow). Sitrus plus Incineroar's inability to OHKO it with Close Combat (caps at 67.5-99.4%) let it eat a 2x hit and still fire back.
4. Their Protect is one-shot: Excadrill Protected T3 and Rotom-Mow Protected T5 in BOTH games, then it failed T6 in both. My final turn doubled Rotom-Mow, the Protect failed, and Blizzard killed it.
5. Retarget awareness: turn 5 they switched the 1% Noivern into the slot my Thunderbolt had targeted; the switch did not dodge and Noivern died for free.
6. Endgame arithmetic: I left Incineroar at ~20% because Thunderbolt's minimum (30.2%) covers it and its own Flare Blitz recoil (~28% of max HP) kills it - exactly how G2 ended.

G2 was messier: I left Mamoswine at 20% in a slot about to be doubled, then lost Mega Metagross to a crit Flare Blitz the turn after Mega Evolving. Metagross was a passenger all game.
reflections.adjustment:
Drop Mega Metagross from the muse four. It is a passenger against this core: Incineroar's Flare Blitz AND Darkest Lariat are both 2x on it and it cannot hit Incineroar back (Meteor Mash 0.5x, Zen Headbutt 0x vs Dark, Ice Punch 0.5x), and it died to a single 2x hit the turn after Mega Evolving. Register Arcanine (Intimidate blunts Incineroar/Excadrill; a second Fire body and Flare Blitz 2x on Tinkaton) or Scrafty (Fake Out + Intimidate tempo) in that slot, keeping the core Mamoswine / Talonflame / Rotom-Frost.

Concretely for a future series vs muse:
(a) Lead Mamoswine + Talonflame again, but price Talonflame's turn 1 as Fake Out bait — her Gale Wings is dead the moment she is chipped, so never build the plan around priority Tailwind while she is below full HP.
(b) Assume the same Incineroar / Noivern / Excadrill / Rotom-Mow four and treat Pincurchin and Tinkaton as not brought until proven otherwise.
(c) On any turn where I need guaranteed damage, aim at Incineroar — it runs no Protect — rather than at a foe that can blank me.
(d) After a foe's Protect succeeds, double that same foe next turn; the chain is only ~1/3 reliable.
(e) If Mamoswine is chipped below ~50%, either keep it home or cash it out with Ice Shard (+1); a 20% Mamoswine never lives to use 0-priority High Horsepower.
(f) Noivern's Focus Sash means it takes two hits — plan the chip, and expect them to switch it in as a retarget shield, which converts my single-target attack into a free KO.

decisions.rationale: Bring Garchomp/Indeedee as the opening control core: Psychic Terrain supports Follow Me while Garchomp gives immediate, reliable Ground pressure into Mega Excadrill and Rotom-Heat. Pelipper preserves a rain reset and Wide Guard option, while Mega Gardevoir is the protected endgame attacker into Annihilape absent here and the opposing Dragon/Grass threats. Avoid leading Pelipper into the revealed Rotom-Heat possibility or relying on Qwilfish's lower immediate damage.

Lead Weavile + Excadrill for immediate Knock Off/Iron Head pressure into Indeedee and fast Ice pressure into Garchomp. The actual sheet has no Trick Room or damaging Water moves: bring Whimsicott for renewable Tailwind, Light Screen and sun denial of Electro Shot/Hurricane reliability, and Rotom for special pressure plus an Earthquake-safe partner after Mega Evolution. Archaludon is Stalwart with Air Balloon, not Stamina: remove Balloon before Ground targeting. Rotom's defensive synergy and sun offense are more useful here than Hydrapple's Water resilience or a third Ground-weak attacker in Empoleon. Preview damage/order calls were unavailable, so no inferred KO or tool-verified order claims.

Use Follow Me to absorb Weavile's 4x Ice pressure and Excadrill's likely attack while Garchomp fires Earthquake. Telepathy prevents ally damage, Psychic Terrain is already active, and Earthquake is the strongest reliable pressure into Excadrill; even if Excadrill Protects, Indeedee preserves Garchomp's position and should survive the redirected hits.

Gardevoir is the best replacement: both opposing Pokémon are at 12%/8%, and it preserves immediate Fairy spread pressure for the next turn while Pelipper would add little damage and cannot prevent Weavile's likely Ice Spinner into Garchomp. Garchomp has no available action this replacement turn, so prioritize the stronger endgame attacker.

Ice Spinner targets Garchomp while Mega Iron Head targets Indeedee. Mega Drill is tool-confirmed faster than Garchomp. Spinner's evaluated damage exceeds full Garchomp HP, so Helping Hand + attack or Indeedee Protect does not freely enable a lethal Garchomp spread attack. Follow Me redirects Spinner, giving substantial combined damage into Indeedee; Iron Head also offers flinch pressure and an accurate hit. Under Follow Me, unboosted Earthquake still threatens Drill and chips Weavile, but also damages Indeedee if it survives. This accepts that risk rather than double-targeting Indeedee and exposing both attackers to a potentially lethal Helping Hand spread attack. Protecting or pivoting Drill gives up important immediate support damage, and Rotom is not safe from boosted Rock Slide.

Mega Mystical Fire is a guaranteed KO on the shown 8% Excadrill-Mega, while Garchomp's Rock Slide guarantees the shown 12% Weavile if it connects. This is the only line that can remove both threats this turn; Telepathy makes the spread Rock Slide safe for Gardevoir, and Mega Gardevoir preserves the strongest remaining endgame.

Bring the only remaining Pokémon, Pelipper, into slot 1 and pass the empty slot. The opposing Excadrill is at 8%, so preserve the chance to finish it with Hurricane while scouting the opponent's final replacement.

Keep immediate split pressure: Ice Spinner into Garchomp and Iron Head into Gardevoir. Both attacks are tool-confirmed faster than their targets even after Gardevoir Mega Evolves. Spinner threatens the KO but Rough Skin likely trades our low-HP Weavile; that is worthwhile. Iron Head ranges 96–190.2% into Mega Gardevoir, not a guaranteed OHKO, but strongly pressures removal and deals quarter damage through Protect. Either foe protecting still leaves its partner threatened, while defensive turns or pivots unnecessarily expose our healthy finishing pair. Preserve Whimsicott and Rotom for cleanup instead of trying to conserve these nearly fainted attackers.

Bring healthy Whimsicott. Against a last Archaludon, its fast Moonblast can remove Air Balloon before Drill's High Horsepower; against Pelipper it supplies weather/speed control while Rotom remains an excellent reserve. Preserve the healthy Rotom rather than expose it first to a possible Draco Meteor.

Hurricane into Whimsicott is the reliable immediate line in rain and exploits the 2x matchup; Focus Sash may leave it at 1 HP, but this still removes its full-health advantage and threatens a clean finish next turn. Excadrill's Ground attacks are immune into Pelipper.

Use accurate Moonblast + Iron Head to bring lone Pelipper into cleanup range. Whimsicott is confirmed faster; Drill also had confirmed 170 Speed, above Pelipper's entire range. Iron Head can flinch and makes progress through Protect. No support turn is needed: Pelipper has only single-target Hurricane, Whimsicott retains its Sash, and full-health Rotom is in reserve to finish with Thunderbolt if either ally falls.

Pelipper is slower and at 29%, so it must Protect this turn to avoid Excadrill's Iron Head and preserve the only win condition. Whimsicott may change weather, but surviving the turn is preferable; Hurricane can finish its 1% HP next turn if Pelipper remains available.

Repeat Moonblast + Iron Head. Moonblast's prior damage range exceeds Pelipper's remaining 28%, and Whimsicott moves first. Protect only delays the finish while Piercing Drill continues chip; no need to reveal Rotom or spend a support turn.

Pelipper cannot safely chain Protect and must remove the 1% Whimsicott now. Hurricane is the only winning action; rain is still active, so use it before another Moonblast/Iron Head sequence finishes Pelipper.

Continue the forced cleanup: faster Moonblast threatens the remaining 23%, and Iron Head chips even through Protect. Pelipper has no remaining partner, recovery, or way to attack before these moves without first surviving a turn to set Tailwind.

reflections.summary: Game 1 was lost after a strong opening trade left both opposing leads at 12%/8%, but Indeedee was exchanged for that damage and Garchomp/Gardevoir could not survive the forced follow-up. The decisive piloting error was Turn 4: after Hurricane reduced Whimsicott to 1%, Pelipper used Protect despite Mega Excadrill's revealed Piercing Drill bypassing it; Pelipper still took Iron Head damage, then died to Moonblast before finishing Whimsicott. The simulator recorded no decision errors or substitutions.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the Garchomp/Indeedee lead concept, but do not automatically spend Indeedee for spread damage if a safer support line exists. Once Piercing Drill is revealed, treat Pelipper Protect as unreliable against Excadrill and attack or reposition instead. At 1% Whimsicott, immediately use Hurricane even if Pelipper moves second; removing Whimsicott is more valuable than attempting a bypassable Protect. Consider Qwilfish over a redundant endgame slot when physical pressure and speed control are central.

reflections.summary: Won G1 in five turns, now leading 1–0, with no decision errors, substitutions or autodefaults. Fast split-target offense removed Indeedee, then both offensive threats without spending a support turn. T1 Spinner aimed at Garchomp covered Helping Hand/Indeedee Protect while Follow Me redirected it into the successful Indeedee double-up. The cost was substantial: Earthquake dealt 129/147 to Weavile and 172/187 to Mega Drill. This was a narrow survival outcome, not evidence the opening safely tanks every damage roll. T2 accepting Weavile's Rough Skin trade and attacking with 15-HP Drill removed Garchomp and Mega Gardevoir; preserving these attackers instead would have surrendered valuable tempo. Whimsicott's immediate Moonblast damage then finished Pelipper, with Iron Head making progress through its T4 Protect. Full-health Rotom remained unused. The win did not test our rain/Archaludon plan, Tailwind management, or the opponent's strongest Protect/switch responses; the T2 Gardevoir OHKO was observed, not a universal damage guarantee.
reflections.adjustment: Keep Weavile/Drill with Whimsicott/Rotom as the default four, not an automatic lock. Into the same lead, retain Spinner's Garchomp threat rather than blindly focusing Indeedee: Helping Hand plus a spread attack can punish the latter severely. Expect Protect and pivot adaptations to the T2 split KO threats, and reassess rather than assuming both foes attack again. Preserve Whimsicott if Pelipper appears early enough to establish Tailwind. Archaludon's Air Balloon must be removed before Ground attacks; it is Stalwart, not Stamina. Qwilfish Intimidate would weaken this physical opening and makes Competitive Empoleon worth reconsidering, but don't change the four solely to counter an unbrought support. No need to force sun, screens, or Tailwind when faster attacks already secure removals.

decisions.rationale: Bring Qwilfish for Intimidate/Icy Wind/Taunt control into the revealed Whimsicott, Mega Excadrill, and Weavile; pair it with Mega Gardevoir as the immediate attacker. Garchomp supplies Ground pressure but must be protected from Weavile, while Pelipper remains a concrete rain/reset resource. Omit Indeedee to avoid repeating the Game 1 support trade.

Retain Weavile + Excadrill with Whimsicott and Rotom-Heat behind. The lead threatens Garchomp, Gardevoir and Indeedee immediately, while Knock Off gives a route to remove Archaludon's Balloon. Whimsicott preserves renewable Tailwind and weather control if Pelipper appears early; Rotom supplies special pressure and a Levitate partner for Mega Earthquake. Empoleon's Intimidate insurance does not outweigh that coherent speed/weather and Ground-immune backup without evidence Qwilfish will be brought. Reassess the actual opening rather than assuming G1's narrow double survival or unprotected T2 repeats.

Use Qwilfish's reliable spread Icy Wind to damage both and collapse their Speed advantage; then Mega Gardevoir targets Weavile with super-effective Mystical Fire. Removing Weavile protects the Garchomp endgame from Ice Spinner, while the speed drop lets Gardevoir act after Qwilfish and before the slowed foes.

Keep Qwilfish in to preserve its Intimidate- and speed-control utility; replace the fainted Gardevoir with Garchomp for immediate Ground pressure into Mega Excadrill and a strong next-turn board. Pelipper would add weather but no immediate safe pressure here.

Focus Ice Spinner + Mega Iron Head into Gardevoir. Intimidate means Iron Head alone is not reliable; Spinner adds 30.9–60.8% to Iron Head's 65.1–127.3% endpoint range, strongly pressuring their only active substantial damage dealer before it acts. This is not a guaranteed combined KO at every hidden spread/roll, but is safer than exposing both attackers to Gardevoir while targeting support. Gardevoir Protect + Qwilfish Icy Wind is a real response; Iron Head still chips through Protect, and we retain Whimsicott to restore speed control rather than assuming the opening wins outright.

Do not expose Garchomp to the revealed NeverMelt Ice Ice Spinner, which has an estimated OHKO range. Icy Wind chips and further slows both foes while Garchomp switches to Pelipper; Pelipper's Drizzle creates a follow-up Hurricane opportunity and is immune to Excadrill Ground attacks.

Protect Weavile and switch Excadrill to Whimsicott. Garchomp now certainly outruns both slowed attackers; staying offensive risks losing Drill and having Icy Wind plus Garchomp remove Weavile before Spinner. Whimsicott is immune to Dragon Claw, resists Earthquake, and the calculated Rock Slide + Icy Wind endpoints total at most 69.3%, making this a defensible joint switch-in rather than single-hit insurance. This resets Drill's Intimidate/Speed drops and positions priority Tailwind alongside Weavile's Ice threat next turn. A predicted Taunt into Whimsicott would require a different continuation, not blind Tailwind.

Whimsicott is at 82% with no Protect revealed, and rain makes Pelipper Hurricane accurate. Qwilfish Icy Wind both chips it, further drops Speed, and ensures Pelipper can act before it; Pelipper then Hurricane targets Whimsicott to remove its disruption immediately.

Tailwind + Taunt Pelipper secures immediate speed control and prevents opposing Tailwind/Protect/Wide Guard. Prankster Tailwind precedes Qwilfish's Taunt or Icy Wind; with Tailwind Weavile can Taunt Pelipper before it acts even if another Icy Wind lands. Hurricane into Whimsicott would KO its already chipped HP, so this explicitly accepts a potential support trade, not presumed Sash survival. That gives a free reset-boost Drill entry under Tailwind, with Knock Off + Ground pressure available into Qwilfish and Rotom preserved for Pelipper. Avoid spending this turn on damage while both opposing speed-control moves remain unrestricted.

Bring reset-boost Mega Excadrill into the secured Tailwind. Its immediate Ground pressure plus Weavile's Knock Off can remove Qwilfish despite Sash, while Weavile retains Ice coverage for Garchomp. Keep Rotom's immunity and Pelipper pressure available as the final pivot.

Protect Qwilfish from the known Mega Excadrill Ground pressure while Pelipper applies reliable rain Hurricane chip to Excadrill. Switching Qwilfish now would expose Garchomp before it can attack, while this preserves the Focus Sash/utility turn and sets up a later Ground-pressure conversion.

High Horsepower + Knock Off into Qwilfish removes its Sash-backed Icy Wind pressure before it acts if the attacks connect. Drill attacks first, with Knock Off finishing either Sash survival or a low damage roll. If Qwilfish Protects, Piercing Drill still earns substantial chip; a Garchomp switch takes both attacks rather than receiving a free turn. Pelipper cannot currently Protect or set Tailwind and its single Hurricane is less dangerous than allowing repeated Speed drops alongside a later Garchomp return. Preserve Rotom and avoid allied Earthquake damage.

Use Qwilfish's last useful control turn to Icy Wind again, lowering Weavile enough that a following Garchomp can move first despite Tailwind. Pelipper continues Hurricane into the already-chipped Excadrill; sacrificing Qwilfish here is preferable to switching Garchomp directly into the simultaneous Ice Spinner threat.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

High Horsepower again into the now-chipped Qwilfish, while Knock Off damages Pelipper and removes Wacan for Rotom's cleanup. Qwilfish's Sash is no longer functional at 64%, so doubling it is unnecessary; even another successful Protect takes meaningful Piercing Drill chip. Garchomp switching into Qwilfish takes Ground damage and faces Spinner under the remaining Tailwind, while Pelipper cannot Protect this turn. This advances both targets without exposing Rotom or paying ally Earthquake damage.

Protect Garchomp from Weavile's lethal Ice Spinner while Pelipper uses the rain-accurate Hurricane on Weavile, the immediate threat. Excadrill's 43% HP is guaranteed to fall to Garchomp Earthquake next turn, and its Ground attacks cannot hit Pelipper.

Use accurate Iron Head + Ice Spinner to remove Garchomp before it attacks during our last Tailwind turn. Intimidated Spinner alone has a 78.1% low endpoint; Iron Head adds 31.2–55.7%, covering that shortfall without High Horsepower's miss risk. Both attackers have enough HP for their own Rough Skin contact. Garchomp Protect + Pelipper Tailwind is the strongest defensive response, but Iron Head still chips through Protect and Rotom remains available for subsequent defensive positioning. Ignoring Garchomp to chip Pelipper risks losing Drill immediately while leaving both foes alive.

Garchomp Earthquake acts before both foes now that Tailwind is gone and guarantees the KO on Mega Excadrill at 31% while also exceeding Weavile's remaining 39% at the damage floor; Pelipper is Ground-immune. Set Tailwind with Pelipper for the incoming final opponent slot.

Switch Weavile to Rotom and Iron Head Garchomp. Weavile must reset its Speed drops rather than die before Spinner; Rotom is immune to Earthquake and resists Hurricane. Drill still outspeeds unboosted Garchomp and can earn accurate damage even through Protect, although Rough Skin and either enemy attack may then KO it. Accepting that productive trade gives reset Weavile a free return to threaten Garchomp while healthy Rotom threatens the berry-less Pelipper. Protecting Drill instead would preserve HP but concede another turn with no damage against both remaining threats.

Earthquake guarantees the 19% Mega Excadrill KO and leaves Rotom-Heat untouched due Levitate. Pelipper Protects against the known Thunderbolt threat, preserving the positioning resource while Garchomp is immune to Thunderbolt and can handle Rotom next turn.

Protect Drill while Thunderbolt targets Pelipper. This burns an opposing Tailwind turn and preserves Drill as a resource while threatening a clean Pelipper KO. Full-health Rotom's calculated Rock Slide + Hurricane total is 61.5–92.1%, so it can take the combined ordinary damage, though Rock Slide flinch or Hurricane confusion remain genuine risks. Pelipper Protect may deny damage but also helps expend Tailwind. Switching low-health Weavile into either attack is much worse; keep it healthy enough to finish Garchomp after speed control expires.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Earthquake now guarantees the lingering Mega Excadrill KO, while Pelipper must Protect because Rotom-Heat's Thunderbolt is a guaranteed KO. This converts to a Garchomp-versus-Rotom endgame rather than losing Pelipper immediately; Garchomp is immune to Thunderbolt.

Thunderbolt Pelipper + Iron Head Garchomp pressures both rather than risking consecutive Protect or switching Weavile into damage. If Garchomp Earthquakes, Drill can be traded while Rotom removes Pelipper; reset Weavile then has Protect to cover the final Tailwind turn. If Garchomp instead targets Rotom, Drill threatens the chipped Garchomp, and Rotom still has full HP to take the two ordinary incoming hits. Accurate Iron Head is preferable to High Horsepower here, with contact recoil explicitly priced as an acceptable finishing trade.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Garchomp Rock Slide reliably KOs Weavile at 39% and also pressures Rotom-Heat super-effectively. Pelipper must attempt its heavily reduced-streak Protect because Thunderbolt otherwise certainly KOs it; preserving Pelipper gives the best chance to finish Rotom after Weavile falls.

Protect Weavile through the final opposing Tailwind turn and keep Thunderbolt on Pelipper. Weavile cannot safely attack before the boosted Garchomp, but after Tailwind ends its reset Speed lets it threaten a clean Spinner finish. Rotom remains full and can withstand the previously calculated joint Rock Slide + Hurricane damage barring secondary effects; removing Pelipper prevents renewed speed control. Pelipper's two consecutive Protect successes do not justify abandoning the lethal Electric target.

Rock Slide is the only action that can remove Weavile and simultaneously threaten Rotom-Heat; Garchomp is immune to Rotom's Thunderbolt. Earthquake is ineffective into Levitate Rotom, while Dragon Claw cannot address both threats.

Ice Spinner finishes 22% Garchomp before any ordinary attack: reset Weavile is confirmed faster and has enough HP for Rough Skin. Overheat supplies noncontact backup rather than an immune Thunderbolt. Garchomp Protect only delays the same winning threat; there is no remaining opposing partner or speed setter.

reflections.summary: Lost Game 2 and the series 0-2. The decisive error was not the Qwilfish control plan itself, but leading Mega Gardevoir without redirection or protection into the known Weavile + Mega Excadrill double-target: it fainted immediately, leaving Qwilfish as the only control piece and forcing a long 2v2 recovery. Qwilfish's Icy Wind did successfully remove Whimsicott and later enabled the Garchomp endgame, so the between-game adjustment partly helped, but the revised lead backfired by sacrificing the primary attacker. The endgame then required repeated Pelipper Protects against Rotom's Thunderbolt; the streak failed and Pelipper fell, while Weavile's Ice Spinner finished Garchomp.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, preserve Gardevoir or use Indeedee redirection alongside the attacker rather than exposing Gardevoir to Weavile plus Mega Excadrill. Qwilfish should still be considered for Icy Wind/Taunt, but it needs a lead partner that can survive the opening or create immediate pressure. Treat Mega Excadrill's Piercing Drill as bypassing Protect, and do not build an endgame around chained Pelipper Protects against Rotom-Heat. Bring a concrete Electric-safe plan and preserve either Pelipper or Garchomp, not both as sacrificial pivots.

reflections.summary:
Won G2 in 11 turns and the series 2–0. The main advantage was fast, concentrated Ice/Steel damage backed by a coherent finishing pair—not a rain-wall matchup. G1 removed Indeedee, then traded nearly fainted Weavile for Garchomp while 15-HP Drill removed Gardevoir. Those narrow survivals and the observed Gardevoir OHKO are not guaranteed benchmarks.

Keeping Weavile/Drill with Whimsicott/Rotom helped against the opponent's substantial adjustment to Qwilfish/Gardevoir. We changed targeting rather than forcing G1's sequence: double-targeting Gardevoir removed it through Intimidate before it attacked. Pivoting Drill reset its drops; Tailwind plus Taunt Pelipper bought time to remove Qwilfish, including High Horsepower chip through Protect. Knock Off stripped Wacan. Later, resetting Weavile and preserving Rotom let Protect bridge opposing Tailwind, Thunderbolt remove Pelipper, and faster Spinner finish Garchomp.

The adjustment was successful but costly: Whimsicott was knowingly sacrificed for one Tailwind cycle, and Garchomp Protect on our last Tailwind turn exposed Weavile to Hurricane. Pelipper established delayed Tailwind after Taunt expired. G2 T7 Iron Head's flinch helped materially; the denied move is unknown. Pelipper's second consecutive Protect succeeded, its third failed, and Rotom avoided Rock Slide flinch on the decisive T10. No critical hits or attack misses were logged. These outcomes supported, rather than prove the inevitability of, the endgame plan.

Preparation correctly followed the current sheets over stale rain scouting: Pelipper had no Water attack, Archaludon was Balloon/Stalwart, and Indeedee lacked Trick Room. Rotom proved valuable as a Ground-immune Electric finisher; Empoleon/Hydrapple and an actual damaging-Water matchup remained untested. Zero submission errors is operational success, not proof every tactical choice was optimal.
reflections.adjustment:
In a future series, re-scout the rebuilt six and sets: this opponent changed both lead and four, so neither historical Indeedee/Pelipper nor this series' Qwilfish/Gardevoir is automatic. Retain immediate focused damage and purposeful defensive pivots, but explicitly map the turn when our Tailwind and Taunt expire. Compare preserving Whimsicott or renewing Taunt with attacking into a likely Garchomp Protect; G2 T6–7 showed the cost of leaving Pelipper's delayed Tailwind route intact. Do not claim an alternative is guaranteed without pricing both opposing actions.

Competitive Empoleon merits a concrete comparison now that Intimidate/Icy Wind adaptation is observed, but replacing Rotom blindly would lose the immunity and finishing role that won this endgame. Reassess Passho and other water-specific resources against actual damaging Water coverage rather than the label 'rain.' Preserve fast attackers by resetting debuffs when that creates a winning final pair, and budget Rough Skin even on Piercing Drill hits through Protect. Continue checking cumulative damage and secondary-effect risks rather than relying on single-hit survival or favorable flinches.

decisions.rationale: Lead Choice Scarf Gholdengo and Swampert, with Passimian and Dragonite in reserve. Gholdengo (223 Spe) outspeeds every Pokemon on Claude's team, OHKOing Mega Gengar with STAB Shadow Ball and pressuring Lycanroc with Make It Rain. Swampert provides immediate Wide Guard spread denial against Lycanroc's Rock Slide and Salamence's Earthquake, while being immune to Rotom-W's Thunderbolt. Passimian (Defiant, Focus Sash) and Dragonite (Inner Focus, Lum Berry, Ice Spinner) provide elite backup against Intimidate, Sucker Punch, and Dragon/Flying threats.

Open sheets changed the scout: Gholdengo is CHOICE SCARF (171-223 Spe, outspeeds Gengar-Mega 200), Charizard is Modest 120-152 Spe, Dragonite has Tailwind, Venusaur LO Chlorophyll. Gengar cannot face a healthy Scarf Gholdengo, so Kingambit + Rotom-W lead (both take Make It Rain 12-37%, Rotom immune HHP, Kingambit Protect T1 vs Passimian CC, Rotom WoW Passimian / Thunderbolt Charizard) with Gengar + Houndoom in back (Houndoom Flash Fire pivot into Charizard, Dark Pulse Gholdengo; Gengar Energy Ball Swampert, closes once Gholdengo is gone). Lycanroc dies to Make It Rain/CC/Earth Power/Giga Drain; Salamence feeds Passimian Defiant and dies to Ice Spinner/Ice Punch.

Kingambit poses an immediate Sucker Punch threat (70-102% OHKO risk on Gholdengo) before Gholdengo can act. Switching Gholdengo to Passimian executes at +6 priority, blanking Sucker Punch entirely or comfortably tanking resisted Dark STAB (20-30%), while preserving Scarf Gholdengo at 100% HP for endgame cleanup against Gengar/Salamence. Swampert uses High Horsepower on Kingambit, bypassing Chople Berry to deal 55-94% massive super-effective damage.

Scarf Gholdengo moves first; Focus Blast (63-90%) + Swampert HHP (53-79%) into Kingambit is the obvious double and kills it, and Trick would steal Chople. Kingambit Protects T1 (also blocks Trick), Rotom Thunderbolts Gholdengo 31-58% so next turn Kowtow (69-126%) is a guaranteed KO and Sucker Punch (57-104%) almost always is; Rotom takes only 10-13% from Make It Rain and is HHP-immune. We also scout Gholdengo's Choice lock: if locked into Focus Blast, pivot Kingambit -> Gengar (Fighting immune) next turn.

Passimian (145 Spe) is guaranteed to act before Rotom-Wash (106-138) and Kingambit (70-102). Even if Kingambit uses Sucker Punch (+1 priority), it deals at most 24.9% to Passimian's remaining 28% HP, guaranteeing Passimian survives to deliver Close Combat (64.7-113.1% through Chople Berry). Swampert's High Horsepower (55.1-93.7%) provides an airtight double-target to guarantee Kingambit is removed this turn, even through Protect failure or maximum defensive rolls, securing board control.

Send in Choice Scarf Gholdengo to pair with Swampert. At 223 Speed, Gholdengo outspeeds every possible Claude Pokémon (Mega Gengar 200, Mega Salamence 189, Lycanroc 180, Houndoom 161, Rotom-W 138). Bringing Gholdengo immediately neutralizes any Mega Gengar Shadow Tag threat against Swampert (Gholdengo is immune to trapping and OHKOs Mega Gengar with STAB Shadow Ball before Gengar can use Energy Ball on Swampert). Preserves Dragonite with Lum Berry in reserve.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Passimian at 28% outspeeds Kingambit; CC 65-96% (Chople) + HHP 53-79% kills Kingambit if both land, Sucker Punch only does 14-25% (no KO), and Gengar switching into the slot is OHKO'd by HHP (140-207%). Only Protect (1/3) can save Kingambit against the likely double; against a Passimian Protect/Quick Guard turn it costs nothing. Rotom Thunderbolts Passimian to remove the Close Combat user (Sash already broken) whether or not Protect succeeds.

Kingambit lost the 1/3 Protect. Gengar comes in: it outspeeds Swampert and Energy Ball OHKOs it (95-206%), and it is immune to nothing here but Rotom is Ground-immune so HHP has only the Gengar slot to aim at - Gengar can Protect next turn to scout Gholdengo's Choice lock or Charizard's entry Protect. Houndoom would be OHKO'd by HHP/Flip Turn with no immediate payoff; keep it for the Charizard Fire-move pivot.

Choice Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) is guaranteed to act before Mega Gengar (max 200 Spe) and targets Gengar with STAB super-effective Shadow Ball (69.5-128.9%). Gengar threatens an immediate 4x Energy Ball OHKO on Swampert; switching Swampert to Dragonite resolves at +6 priority before Mega Evolution activates Shadow Tag. Dragonite easily absorbs any incoming attack (4x resists Energy Ball, 2x resists Water) while preserving Swampert at 100% HP with Sitrus Berry for late-game positioning.

Scarf Gholdengo (171-223) moves before Gengar; Shadow Ball 79-140% and Swampert HHP 140-207% both threaten the Gengar slot, so Gengar Protects (no mega yet - keep the option) to scout Gholdengo's Choice lock. Rotom Thunderbolts Gholdengo 31-58% so Houndoom Dark Pulse (64-141%) or Gengar Shadow Ball finishes it next turn; Rotom is HHP-immune and takes 10-13% from Make It Rain.

Gengar burned Protect on Turn 3 and cannot reliably Protect consecutively. Gholdengo is Choice-locked into Shadow Ball into Gengar (69.5-128.9%). Dragonite pairs this with Ice Spinner into Gengar (28.1-54.1%), creating a combined 97.6-183% damage bracket that heavily threatens to eliminate Mega Gengar this turn. Furthermore, if Claude attempts to switch Gengar out to Salamence, Ice Spinner deals 4x super-effective damage (OHKO). Swampert remains at 100% HP in reserve to clean up the endgame.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Paralysed Gholdengo (85-111 Spe) is now outsped by Gengar; Shadow Ball 66-148% kills it from 44% before it moves, and Mega Evolving now is safe since the Scarf threat dies (Dragonite Extreme Speed can't touch Gengar; Shadow Tag then traps Swampert for Energy Ball). If Gholdengo switches to Swampert, Shadow Ball still does 32-69%. Rotom Thunderbolts Dragonite (Inner Focus, no Multiscale) for neutral chip; WoW would be cured by Lum.

Dragonite (50% HP) is a prime target for Gengar's Shadow Ball or Rotom's Thunderbolt. Dragonite uses Protect (+4 priority) to safely nullify any damage directed at its slot. Swampert uses High Horsepower into Gengar-Mega (87.4-168.9%), securing an instant OHKO on Gengar's remaining 48% HP if Gengar attacks Dragonite. If Gengar uses Protect, Dragonite avoids taking Rotom's Thunderbolt while Swampert easily sponges any incoming attack with Sitrus Berry, setting up an overwhelming Turn 6 position where Gengar cannot reliably Protect again.

Gengar-Mega (200) moves first and Energy Ball is a guaranteed OHKO on Swampert (102-185%), removing the HHP threat before it acts; Swampert has no Protect. Rotom Thunderbolts Dragonite (29-52% vs 50% left) for a coin-flip KO; even if Dragonite trades Ice Spinner into Gengar, Houndoom (161 > Dragonite) Dark Pulses it next turn and ESpeed can't OHKO Houndoom or Rotom.

Swampert has fainted. Dragonite (50% HP) must target 48% HP Gengar-Mega with Ice Spinner (28.1-54.1%) as the sole path to victory. Gengar is immune to Extreme Speed, and Protect has reduced accuracy from consecutive use. If Gengar uses Psychic or rolls low on Shadow Ball, Dragonite survives to land Ice Spinner for the KO.

Dragonite is their last mon at 50% and Protected last turn (1/3 chance to repeat). Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball 34-60% moves first, Rotom Thunderbolt 29-52% follows; combined 63-112% almost always KOs. Ice Spinner can KO Gengar at 48% only at high rolls and Gengar is immune to Extreme Speed; Houndoom remains as backup.

reflections.summary: Game 1 was lost 0-1. We successfully eliminated Kingambit on Turn 2 via Passimian Close Combat and Swampert High Horsepower. However, a Turn 3 10% paralysis from Rotom-Wash's Thunderbolt crippled Choice Scarf Gholdengo's Speed from 223 to 111, allowing Mega Gengar (200 Spe) to move first on Turn 4 and KO Gholdengo. Mega Gengar then revealed Energy Ball to OHKO Swampert on Turn 5, closing out the game. Mega Charizard Y and Chlorophyll Venusaur are the decisive adjustment for Game 2, completely exploiting Gengar's special moveset and Rotom-Wash under Sun.
reflections.adjustment: Pivot to Sun core: Mega Charizard Y + Chlorophyll Venusaur + Passimian + Gholdengo (or Dragonite). Bench Swampert due to confirmed Gengar Energy Ball. Venusaur in Sun (264 Spe) outspeeds Mega Gengar (200 Spe) and Rotom-W, 4x resists Energy Ball, resists Electric, and OHKOs Gengar with Earth Power. Passimian provides Defiant and Quick Guard against Kingambit.

reflections.summary: Won G1 in 6 turns, 3-1 on mons (Kingambit lost). Open sheets revealed Scarf Gholdengo (171-223 Spe, outspeeds Gengar-Mega), so the plan of Kingambit + Rotom-W lead with Gengar/Houndoom back and delaying the mega was correct. Rotom-W was the MVP: Thunderbolt hit Passimian T1 (through their Gholdengo->Passimian pivot), killed it T2, then chunked Gholdengo to 44% AND paralysed it - the para is what let Gengar outspeed and KO Gholdengo T4 before mega-committing; without it Gholdengo would still have moved first with a 79-140% Shadow Ball, so that step was luck-assisted and the fallback (Houndoom Dark Pulse / second Protect gamble) must be planned for G2. Kingambit died T2 to the CC + HHP double after a 1/3 Protect failed; it had no safe slot (Gengar/Houndoom switch-ins die to HHP/CC), so the loss was structural, not a misplay - but leading it into a Passimian + Swampert board is what created that. Gengar-Mega closed cleanly: Energy Ball OHKO Swampert (which has no Protect), Shadow Ball finished Dragonite the turn after its Protect. Their bring surprised: Gholdengo, Swampert, Passimian, Dragonite - Charizard and Venusaur stayed home. Zero decision errors.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same four (Gengar, Kingambit, Rotom-W, Houndoom) - all had a role and Salamence/Lycanroc are still bad into Scarf Gholdengo/Passimian/Swampert - but change the lead per Bo3 rule: Rotom-W + Gengar (Gengar immune to CC/ESpeed/Focus Blast; Protect T1 vs Scarf Shadow Ball; Rotom Thunderbolt Gholdengo/Passimian) with Kingambit + Houndoom back, so Kingambit enters only after Passimian or Swampert is gone. Don't rely on paralysis: Gengar megas only once Gholdengo is dead, para, or locked into a move Gengar resists/is immune to (Focus Blast/Make It Rain); otherwise Houndoom Dark Pulse (64-141%) or Kingambit Kowtow does the Gholdengo kill. Expect them to adapt: Charizard may come in G2 (Houndoom pivot / Rotom Thunderbolt 53-114%) and Gholdengo may Trick or Make It Rain instead of Shadow Ball into a Protect.
