decisions.rationale: Lead Mega Charizard Y and Chlorophyll Venusaur with Passimian and Choice Scarf Gholdengo in reserve. Charizard Y's immediate Mega Evolution sets Sun via Drought, boosting Modest Venusaur's Speed to 264 via Chlorophyll. This cleanly outspeeds Claude's entire team (Mega Gengar 200, Mega Salamence 189, Lycanroc 180, Rotom-W 138, Kingambit 102). Venusaur threatens an immediate Turn 1 Earth Power OHKO on Mega Gengar and Giga Drain on Rotom-Wash / Lycanroc, while Charizard Y's Sun Heat Wave melts Kingambit and neutral targets. Passimian (Defiant, Focus Sash, Quick Guard) and Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe, immune to Shadow Tag) provide flawless backup against Sucker Punch, Lycanroc, and endgame cleanup. Swampert is strictly benched due to Gengar's confirmed Energy Ball.

G2 after a win: change the lead, keep the four that won. Lead Gengar + Rotom-W: Gengar Protects T1 to scout Scarf Gholdengo's lock (Shadow Ball 79-140% threat) while immune to CC/ESpeed/Focus Blast; Rotom Thunderbolt Gholdengo 31-58% or Passimian if it pivots in, takes Make It Rain only 12-20%. Back Kingambit (walls locked Shadow Ball/Make It Rain, Kowtow finishes Gholdengo) + Houndoom (Flash Fire vs Charizard, Dark Pulse Gholdengo). Lycanroc dies to Make It Rain/CC/Swampert; Salamence feeds Passimian Defiant and dies to Ice Spinner - both stay home.

Charizard uses Protect + Mega Evolve (Choice 15) to set Drought safely while completely nullifying Rotom-Wash's super-effective Thunderbolt (68-102% OHKO risk) and any Gengar offensive targeting. Charizard Y's Drought instantly activates Venusaur's Chlorophyll, doubling its Speed to 264 before moves resolve under Gen 9 dynamic Speed mechanics. This ensures Venusaur acts BEFORE Timid Mega Gengar (200 max Spe). Venusaur uses Earth Power into Gengar (Choice 3), dealing 129-152 damage (2x super-effective, ~70% OHKO chance). If Gengar uses Protect, Charizard takes 0 damage and Venusaur comfortably absorbs Rotom-W's resisted Thunderbolt (13-16%), leaving our Sun sweepers in full control for Turn 2.

New lead Charizard + Venusaur (sun). Once Charizard megas, Drought makes Venusaur 200-264 Spe (outspeeds Gengar) and LO Earth Power does 91-135% to Gengar (74-112% mega) - Gengar Protects T1 to scout and avoid the OHKO. Rotom is immune to Earth Power, resists Heat Wave (29-41%), and Thunderbolt does 56-102% to Charizard-Y - the priority is removing Charizard to kill the sun so Venusaur becomes slow (100-132 < Gengar/Houndoom). Risk: Charizard Protects on entry-turn as in G1 pattern, or Solar Beam/Giga Drain on Rotom (89-125% / 74-111%) - acceptable since Gengar is the obvious Earth Power target.

Venusaur (264 Spe in Sun via Chlorophyll) is guaranteed to act first among all Pokémon on the field. Venusaur targets Gengar with Earth Power (Choice 3), threatening an immediate 70% OHKO (70.1-137% damage) before Gengar can attack. Gengar cannot safely Protect after using Protect on Turn 1 (~33% success rate). Charizard-Mega-Y (152 Spe) is guaranteed to outspeed Modest Rotom-Wash (106-138 Spe) and targets Rotom-Wash with 1-turn Sun Solar Beam (Choice 5), dealing 85.4-156.8% (144-196 damage) to OHKO Rotom-Wash before it can use Thunderbolt. This simultaneous offensive pressure threatens to remove both of Claude's active Pokémon on Turn 2 while keeping Charizard safe from Thunderbolt damage.

Charizard Protected on entry (pattern 4/4), so it cannot Protect reliably now. Sun Venusaur (200-264) outspeeds Gengar regardless, and no switch is safe: Houndoom eats Earth Power 77-116%, Kingambit eats Heat Wave 105-149%, double Protect is 1/3. Best EV is to kill Charizard and end the sun: Gengar megas (SpD up, EP 74-112% / Heat Wave 75-105% instead of OHKO ranges, Shadow Tag traps) and Shadow Balls Charizard 32-58% before it moves; Rotom Thunderbolt 56-102% finishes (88-160% combined). If they redirect Venusaur to Giga Drain Rotom expecting another Gengar Protect, Gengar survives and Charizard dies. Without sun, Venusaur drops to 100-132 and Gengar/Houndoom outspeed it.

Both leads fell; forced double replacement. Kingambit and Houndoom come in. Next turn: Houndoom absorbs Heat Wave (Flash Fire), Kingambit must Protect vs Heat Wave; Houndoom sun Heat Wave hits Venusaur 2x.

Charizard uses Protect (Choice 7) to guarantee its survival at 100% HP against any potential Sucker Punch or Dark Pulse double-target, completely blanking Sucker Punch (which fails against non-damaging moves). Meanwhile, Chlorophyll Venusaur (264 Spe in Sun) is guaranteed to act before Houndoom (126-161 Spe) and Kingambit (70-102 Spe). Venusaur targets Houndoom with 2x super-effective Earth Power (Choice 4), dealing 62.6-118% damage. This either eliminates Houndoom immediately or reduces it to critical HP while preserving Charizard at 100% HP for Turn 4, where Charizard's Sun Overheat (179.7-329.1%) guarantees Kingambit's demise.

Kingambit is OHKO'd by Heat Wave (105-149%) and Overheat (195%+), so it Protects. Houndoom is Fire-immune and its sun Heat Wave does 89-161% spread to Venusaur (90%), a KO on all but the minimum roll; Sucker Punch chip would not add anything if Kingambit dies. Risk: sun Venusaur (200+) Earth Powers Houndoom first for 77-116%; if it targets Kingambit's Protect instead, Venusaur dies and Flash Fire may also proc off Heat Wave.

Kingambit is the sole remaining Pokémon on Claude's team. Charizard-Mega-Y (152 Spe) targets Kingambit with Sun-boosted Overheat (Choice 1), which guarantees an instant 179.7-329.1% OHKO at all rolls even through Chople Berry. Venusaur (264 Spe in Sun) backs this up with super-effective Earth Power (Choice 3, 52.7-94.9%). Kingambit used Protect last turn, so consecutive Protect has an overwhelming ~67% failure rate. Even if Kingambit uses +1 priority Sucker Punch, both Charizard (100% HP) and Venusaur (81% HP) easily survive to deliver their lethal attacks and close out Game 2 with a decisive 4-0 sweep.

Kingambit alone vs Charizard-Y + sun Venusaur is lost; it moves last except with Sucker Punch, so Sucker Punch Charizard (34-65%) is the only move that lands before Heat Wave/Overheat kills it. Charizard Protected last turn so a repeat is unlikely. Playing on rather than conceding in case anything more is revealed for G3.

Charizard uses fresh 100% Protect (Choice 7) to completely blank any potential Sucker Punch aimed at its slot, guaranteeing Charizard takes 0 damage and remains conscious. Venusaur (71% HP) is guaranteed to survive even a maximum roll Sucker Punch from Kingambit (42.6-60.6% = 66-94 damage vs 110 remaining HP, leaving at least 16 HP). Venusaur (264 Spe in Sun) uses 100% accurate super-effective Earth Power (Choice 3), dealing 52.7-94.9% to Kingambit's remaining 23% HP to guarantee the final KO and close out Game 2 with a flawless 4-0 sweep.

Overheat missed; Charizard is at 38% and Sucker Punch does 34-65%, a near-certain KO before it moves. Kingambit (23%) dies to Earth Power regardless, so take the Charizard KO - it also forces their third Pokémon to be revealed for G3 scouting. If Charizard Protects, nothing else would have mattered anyway.

reflections.summary: Flawless 4-0 victory in Game 2 to tie the series 1-1. The Sun core adjustment executed with perfection: Charizard-Mega-Y's Turn 1 Protect + Mega Evolution safely deployed Drought, enabling Chlorophyll Venusaur (264 Spe) to immediately control the field. On Turn 2, Venusaur's Earth Power and Charizard's 1-turn Solar Beam executed a simultaneous double KO on Mega Gengar and Rotom-Wash. On Turn 3, Charizard Protected while Venusaur flat OHKOed Houndoom with Earth Power. On Turns 4-5, Venusaur absorbed Sucker Punch and dismantled Kingambit with Earth Power, closing out the game without losing a single Pokémon.
reflections.adjustment: Maintain the dominant Sun core (Mega Charizard Y + Chlorophyll Venusaur + Passimian + Choice Scarf Gholdengo). For Game 3, prepare for Claude potentially bringing Lycanroc (Focus Sash, Rock Slide, Accelerock) and Salamence (Salamencite, Intimidate) to counter Charizard. Passimian's Defiant punishes Salamence's Intimidate and Quick Guard completely blocks Lycanroc's Accelerock and Kingambit's Sucker Punch, while Choice Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) outspeeds Lycanroc, Mega Salamence, and Mega Gengar.

reflections.summary: G2 lost 0-4 in 5 turns. Gemini completely changed its bring: led Charizard + Venusaur (sun) - neither was brought in G1 - and never revealed its other two. Our four (Gengar, Rotom-W, Kingambit, Houndoom) was structurally lost at preview: three of the four are Ground-weak and LO Chlorophyll Venusaur (200-264 Spe in sun, outspeeds Gengar-Mega) Earth Powered five turns in a row for KOs on Gengar-Mega (T2, from 74-112% range), Houndoom (T3) and Kingambit (T4-5, crit finish); Charizard-Y Solar Beam OHKO'd Rotom T2 (89-125%, Rotom's only threat to it) and Charizard Protected on T1/T3/T5 (every other turn, pattern now 5/5 on entry turn). Only damage dealt: Kingambit Sucker Punch 62% on Charizard-Y; Overheat missed once. T1 Gengar Protect scout was fine but T2 had no safe line: every switch-in died to EP or Heat Wave, so the mega+Shadow Ball gamble was the least-bad option and lost to speed. The real error was the preview bring - 'keep the four that won' against an opponent who rebuilds its four between games, while their sheet openly showed Venusaur EP + Swampert HHP vs our three Ground-weak mons.
reflections.adjustment: For G3 change the four, not just the lead: bring the Ground-immune pair Salamence (Salamencite) + Rotom-W as the lead - Venusaur's Earth Power hits neither, Salamence-Mega Double-Edge OHKOs Venusaur (117-265%) and Passimian, and takes Heat Wave only 34-59%; Rotom Thunderbolts Charizard the turn after its Protect (it Protects on entry and every other turn). Back Kingambit (Gholdengo/Dragonite wall) + Gengar (Gholdengo/Swampert killer). Decide the mega from their lead: Charizard/Venusaur/Passimian visible = Salamence megas; Gholdengo/Swampert/Dragonite lead = Gengar megas later and Salamence stays base Intimidate/Tailwind. Never again bring 3 Ground-weak pieces vs a sheet with LO Chlorophyll Venusaur + Swampert; Houndoom sits this one out (dies to EP, HHP, CC and sun Venusaur outspeeds it). Expect them to rebuild again - cover both their G1 and G2 fours rather than reading one.

Back Kingambit (walls Gholdengo/Dragonite, Kowtow Gholdengo) + Gengar (Energy Ball Swampert, Psychic Sash Passimian). Leave Houndoom (EP/HHP/CC bait) and Lycanroc. Mega chosen by their lead per next_game_plan; they rebuild their four every game so this covers all six.

Charizard uses Protect + Mega Evolve (Choice 15) to safely establish Drought while completely neutralizing incoming threats (Rotom-Wash's 68-102% Thunderbolt and Salamence's 88-123% Double-Edge). Drought immediately boosts Chlorophyll Venusaur to 264 Speed before moves resolve under Gen 9 dynamic speed mechanics, outspeeding Mega Salamence (189 max Spe) prior to any Tailwind setup. Venusaur attacks Mega Salamence with 100% accurate STAB Sludge Bomb (Choice 0), dealing 38.6-71.2% damage. If Salamence sets Tailwind, it is crippled to 29-61% HP; if Salamence attacks Venusaur, the combination of Sludge Bomb and 33% Double-Edge recoil deals 68-101% total damage while preventing Tailwind entirely.

Bring in Choice Scarf Gholdengo (Choice 1) to replace the fainted Venusaur. Gholdengo's effective Speed of 223 outspeeds both 13% HP Mega Salamence (154-189 Spe) and Rotom-Wash (106-138 Spe), ensuring Gholdengo moves first next turn to immediately finish off Mega Salamence before it can set Tailwind or attack, while Mega Charizard Y (152 Spe) in Sun threatens Rotom-Wash with Solar Beam (85.4-156.8%). Passimian remains held in reserve with Focus Sash and Quick Guard.

T1 vs Charizard+Venusaur: Salamence megas and Double-Edges Venusaur (OHKO 126-237%; if Venusaur Protects, Charizard is on Protect cooldown T2). Rotom Protects: Charizard Protects on entry (5/5) so Thunderbolt is wasted, and Protect dodges Giga Drain 74-111%/Solar Beam. Salamence-M takes at most Sludge Bomb 46-70% this turn. T2: Rotom Thunderbolt Charizard-Y + Salamence Double-Edge Charizard (67-126%) if Venusaur is gone.

Choice Scarf Gholdengo (effective Speed 223) comfortably outspeeds 13% HP Mega Salamence (154-189 Spe) and Modest Rotom-Wash (106-138 Spe). Gholdengo uses 100% accurate STAB Shadow Ball (Choice 1) into Mega Salamence, dealing 28.7-53.5% to guarantee the knockout from 13% HP before Salamence can act (denying Tailwind or Double-Edge recoil) while preserving +0 SpA without Make It Rain's 5% miss chance. Charizard-Mega-Y (152 Spe) acts before Rotom-Wash (106-138 Spe) and executes 1-turn Solar Beam in Sun (Choice 5) into Rotom-Wash, dealing 85.4-156.8% super-effective damage to eliminate Rotom-Wash after its Turn 1 Protect.

Charizard cannot Protect this turn (used T1). Salamence-M 13% is dead to recoil or any hit anyway, so spend it: Double-Edge Charizard-Y 67-126% + Rotom Thunderbolt 56-102% = KO if Salamence moves (Gholdengo Scarf 171-223 vs 189 uncertain; it may also not MIR). Protect would only preserve a mon that can't act again vs a faster locked Gholdengo. Rotom risks Solar Beam 89-125% but Kingambit/Gengar switch-ins die to sun Heat Wave + MIR, so Rotom attacks. Next: Kingambit walls locked MIR Gholdengo (17-25%), Sucker Punch/Thunderbolt finish Charizard.

Forced double replacement: Kingambit + Gengar (base, no mega available). Gholdengo is locked into Shadow Ball (resisted by Kingambit, kills Gengar); Charizard is on its usual T3 Protect. T3 plan: Gengar Protect, Kingambit Kowtow Cleave Gholdengo 63-141% (or Sucker Punch 53-116%, no Passimian seen).

Charizard-Mega-Y uses fresh Protect (Choice 7) to safely absorb all incoming pressure (Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Gengar's attacks), keeping Charizard at 100% HP in Sun. Choice Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) outspeeds un-Mega'd base Gengar (143-178 Spe) and targets Gengar with 100% accurate 2x super-effective STAB Shadow Ball (Choice 1), dealing 80.2-155.6% to eliminate Gengar or reduce it to critical HP. Passimian remains untouched at 100% HP with Focus Sash to provide Turn 4 Quick Guard spread/priority shutdown against Kingambit.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Gengar Protects the locked Shadow Ball (79-140%). Kingambit Kowtow Cleave Gholdengo 63-141% (highest KO chance, still hits if Gholdengo pivots; Sucker Punch fails on a switch). Charizard Protected T1 and follows a T1/T3/T5 Protect rhythm, so this is the best turn to expose Kingambit to Heat Wave. If Gholdengo dies: T4 Gengar Shadow Ball + Kingambit Sucker Punch Charizard (can't Protect twice); if Charizard Heat Waves instead, Kingambit Protects next turn when possible.

selection: Quick Guard (your side, including ally Charizard-Mega-Y)
decisions.rationale: Passimian executes Quick Guard (+3 priority, Choice 0) to establish complete immunity against Kingambit's Sucker Punch (+1 priority), rendering Kingambit incapable of priority revenge-killing or chipping either ally. Gengar (143-178 Spe) cannot OHKO Charizard-Mega-Y (max 47.7% from Shadow Ball into 100% HP). Charizard-Mega-Y (152 Spe) comfortably outspeeds Kingambit (70-102 Spe) and unleashes Sun-boosted spread Heat Wave (Choice 0), dealing 98.6-179.4% super-effective damage to delete Kingambit and 65.3-129.6% damage to simultaneously eliminate or heavily cripple un-Mega'd Gengar, securing the match and series victory.

Charizard can't Protect but its Heat Wave/Overheat OHKOs Kingambit in sun and they double the Kingambit slot (CC 65-96% through Chople) -> Kingambit Protect. Gengar outspeeds Passimian and Psychics it to its Sash (54-105%): T5 Kingambit Sucker Punch (+1) kills the 1-HP Passimian before CC unless Quick Guard/Protect, Gengar Protects Heat Wave. Charizard's T1/T3/T5 Protect rhythm gives Kingambit a chance to reach T6 (sun over: Heat Wave spread 53-74%), where Shadow Ball 28-48% + Sucker Punch 34-65% and priority win the Charizard endgame. Shadow Ball on Charizard now leaves Passimian CCing every turn, which Kingambit can't survive.

selection: Quick Guard (your side, including ally Charizard-Mega-Y)
decisions.rationale: Passimian deploys Quick Guard (+3 priority, Choice 0) to completely shut down Kingambit's only priority avenue, Sucker Punch (+1 priority), guaranteeing that neither ally can be damaged before acting. Charizard-Mega-Y (152 Spe) comfortably outspeeds Adamant Kingambit (70-102 Spe) and unleashes Sun-boosted STAB Overheat (Choice 0), dealing an astronomical 179.7 - 329.1% super-effective damage to secure an unavoidable flat OHKO through Chople Berry, eliminating Claude's final Pokémon and winning the game and series 2-1.

Kingambit alone vs Charizard-Y 100% (Heat Wave disabled by Cursed Body; Overheat 130-273% still OHKOs, 90% acc) + Passimian 6% (Sash gone). Charizard's T1/T3/T5 Protect rhythm makes this the turn to act: Sucker Punch Passimian (+1 priority) kills it before Close Combat unless Quick Guard/Protect, keeping Kingambit at 100%. Sucker Punch Charizard fails if it Protects and Kowtow is blocked. Then T6 Protect the Overheat, T8 Sucker Punch race needing misses; low odds but the only line.

reflections.summary: We won Game 3 (5-2 turns, 2-0 remaining) to close out the series 2-1. After dropping Game 1 to a 10% paralysis roll and Gengar's tech'd Energy Ball on Swampert, our tactical adjustments across Games 2 and 3 proved decisive. In Game 2, leading Mega Charizard Y and Chlorophyll Venusaur produced an unanswerable 4-0 sweep via dynamic speed. In Game 3, Claude adapted by bringing Mega Salamence and leading it alongside Rotom-Wash. We anticipated the speed battle: Charizard safely set Drought via Protect + Mega Evolution, while Venusaur (264 Spe in Sun) struck Mega Salamence with Sludge Bomb to 40% before falling to Aerilate Double-Edge, which recoiled Salamence down to 13% while preventing Tailwind. Choice Scarf Gholdengo (223 Spe) entered to clean up Salamence with 100% accurate Shadow Ball while Charizard's 1-turn Solar Beam flat OHKO'd Rotom-Wash. When Kingambit and Gengar entered, Passimian deployed consecutive Quick Guards (+3 priority) to completely shut down Kingambit's Sucker Punch, enabling Charizard to melt Gengar with Heat Wave and delete Kingambit with Sun Overheat (179-329% OHKO) to secure the series victory.
reflections.adjustment: Against Claude in future matchups, anticipate their proactive Game 3 counter-bring (such as Mega Salamence with Aerilate Double-Edge or benched Lycanroc) to challenge Drought/Sun control. Leading Charizard + Venusaur remains exceptionally strong due to dynamic speed, but when an opposing physical Flying/Rock Mega is present, leading Passimian + Gholdengo or immediately pivoting Gholdengo into physical Flying attacks offers an even safer damage mitigation line than trading Venusaur for heavy chip/recoil.

reflections.summary: G3 lost 0-4 in 5 turns; series lost 1-2. The G3 prep read the matchup correctly: Gemini re-led Charizard+Venusaur as predicted, the Ground-immune Salamence+Rotom lead blanked Earth Power, and T1 went to plan (Mega Salamence OHKO'd Venusaur while Rotom Protected through Charizard's entry-Protect turn). Two things lost it. (1) Salamence's cost of the KO was underbudgeted: a high Sludge Bomb roll (60%) plus 27% Double-Edge recoil left it at 13%, a one-shot piece. (2) T2 I bet the game on a speed coin flip - Scarf Gholdengo 171-223 vs Salamence-M 189 - by double-attacking Charizard (Double-Edge + Thunderbolt only KOs if Salamence moves) instead of hedging with Rotom -> Kingambit (Solar Beam 20-28% on Kingambit, Rotom kept). Gholdengo was faster, Salamence died before moving, Solar Beam OHKO'd Rotom, and the game became Kingambit + base Gengar (no mega) vs sun Charizard-Y + Scarf Gholdengo + Sash Passimian. Kowtow KO'd Gholdengo and Psychic broke Passimian's Sash, but Heat Wave/Overheat OHKO both my remaining pieces; T5 Sucker Punch into a repeat Quick Guard broke my own playbook rule (Kowtow on the 6% Passimian was correct, though Overheat still wins). Series-level: the G2 adjustment (new lead, same four) backfired - Gemini rebuilt its whole four into Charizard+Venusaur sun, which OHKOs three of my Ground-weak pieces, 0-4 without landing a hit. G3 fixed the read but not the resource math. Root cause: no clean answer on my roster to Charizard-Y sun + Chlorophyll Venusaur + Scarf Gholdengo speed tiers; the better G3 T1 was Salamence Tailwind (378 under TW beats Scarf Gholdengo 223 and sun Venusaur 264) on Charizard's Protect turn, then Double-Edge Venusaur + Thunderbolt Charizard T2 with Rotom moving before Solar Beam. Lycanroc, the Fire-resist Rock Slide answer, was never brought all series.
reflections.adjustment: Against Gemini again: expect Charizard+Venusaur (+Scarf Gholdengo, Sash Passimian) every game once it has worked; it rebuilds its four game to game, so cover the whole six rather than the last four. Lead Salamence + Rotom-W again but T1 Salamence sets Tailwind (not Double-Edge) on Charizard's guaranteed entry-Protect turn with Rotom Protect; T2 under Tailwind Salamence-M outspeeds Scarf Gholdengo and sun Venusaur: Double-Edge Venusaur, Rotom Thunderbolt Charizard before Solar Beam. Bring Lycanroc over Gengar as the second Charizard answer (Rock Slide OHKO, resists Fire, Sash vs Earth Power) since Gengar never got to mega in G2 or G3. Never double-attack when the KO depends on a speed tie - switch the partner to the wall instead. Never Sucker Punch while Passimian is out (Quick Guard repeats without failing). Budget Double-Edge recoil (~27% of Salamence per OHKO) plus the expected hit before deciding Salamence is safe for a second turn.

events.text: Light Screen up on P2's side
Light Screen ended on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Bring 4: Farig+Corv lead, Cofag+Bax back. Sneasler is gone from grok's six, voiding Hatt's 4x-Psychic execute and Cofag's CC-blank roles — so Hatt benches and Cofag returns as TR-backup setter + screen-proof Night Shade grind (50 flat, beats Clef Magic Guard + Grimm Light Clay) + Fake Out immunity (preview-verified 0x) + neutral Draco tank for DNite-M. Bax-M is the DNite-Mega closer (HH+IC guaranteed OHKO through Multiscale, tool-verified 100-209.6) and the Torch Song sponge (0.5x, +1 Atk each). Garg sits: its Fire-wall job is duplicated by Bax-feed and its grind by Night Shade. Lead script unchanged: Armor Tail blanks Rilla Fake Out T1, no Taunt/Imprison threat exists in their set, so T1 TR is near-guaranteed; Corv IH double-taps either Fairy 2x through Clef's Follow Me. Only real dangers: Inteleon's unredirectable LO Sniper Snipe Shot/Ice Beam pre-TR (TR makes it act last) and Draco into Farig/Bax — answer is immediate HH+IC pair execute the turn after DNite-M enters.

G1 vs TR Mega Bax. Lead Grimm+Clef: Prankster screens still go up through Armor Tail; Follow Me eats Ice Crash/Dragon (Clef Ice 1x, Dragon 0). Back Mega DN (Timid Draco is the Bax roll; EQ immune; mega on first attacking send) and Rilla (only real Garg breaker — WH roll in Grassy; Knock Farig/Hatterene items). Leave Inteleon (last under TR) and Dirge (Garg is unbreakable without Grass/Water). Do not Fire Bax, Ghost Farig, status Hatterene, contact Cofag, TWave under TR, or Fake Out while Farig is in.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: T1: Farig Trick Room (resolves last, inversion starts T2) + Corv Iron Head at Grimmsnarl. Armor Tail already blocks their only priority angles; their set has no Taunt/Imprison, so TR is guaranteed to resolve. Aiming IH at Grimm is strictly best: Clef Follow Me redirects it onto Clef (2x either way), and if Clef doesn't FM, the screen setter eats ~24%. TW aimed anywhere on my side is harmless-to-helpful under TR.

Farig almost certainly TRs; Corv Iron Heads a Fairy (2x). Prankster Reflect (+1) goes up before Iron Head and is not blocked by Armor Tail. Follow Me (+2) then pulls the Iron Head onto Clef after Reflect is up: Clef lives 36–54% even on HH, ~24–36% without, and Grimm stays intact to click LS T2. Do not TWave — TR makes para-Spe drop give them first action. Do not attack; Moonblast does not stop TR and Fairy is 0.5 into Corv.

T2 double-execute on Clefable (73%): Farig Psychic (28.7-52.9) + Corv Iron Head (23.8-44.7 thru Reflect) = 52.5-97.6 — dies at most rolls; surviving >6% leaves it in NS/IC range next turn. Killing Clef removes Follow Me shielding before their nukes (DNite-M/Inteleon) enter, and removes the only Moonblast threat to Farig. A fresh-Protect read costs one TR turn, but a split-target turn cannot kill anything and I re-execute vs the 33% chain.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Clefable)
decisions.rationale: TR 4, Reflect 7. Grimm must click LS now: Hatterene LO Gleam is 77–109% into Grimm (spread, FM does not save) and LS cuts it to a live; also cuts Farig/Hatterene Psychic into Clef. Clef Protect: already 74%, Grimm is Psychic-immune so they can only Psychic Clef — Protect blanks Iron Head/Psychic/Ice Crash on the magnet and keeps HP for later FM vs Bax. Do not TWave in TR. Do not Moonblast Corv (0.5). Farig chip can wait one turn; dual screens then DN/Rilla.

Re-execute Clefable at the 33% Protect decay: Psychic (28.7-52.9) + IH (23.8-44.7) sum 52.5-97.6 vs 73% — kill at most rolls, and killing it NOW matters strategically: Follow Me would redirect my Bax Icicle Crash away from DNite-Mega onto Clef when the dragon enters T4-T5. Grimm keeps SpiritBreak only (30-43% into Farig worst case both attacking; Farig survives at ~19% floor). If Clef chains Protect into 11%, I re-execute T4.

Dual screens up, TR 3. They doubled Clef into Protect; another Psychic (22–32% LS) + Iron Head (24–36% Reflect) from 74% does not KO (floor ~6%). Do not chain Protect (1/3). Do not TWave in TR. Fairy is 0.5 into Corv so both hit Farig: Spirit Break 22–40% + Moonblast 22–42% (SpA drop) while Grimm still moves before Corv in TR. If they pivot Bax into Farig slot, Fairy is 2x and the double can roll the mega. Keep Clef for later FM; DN waits until Bax is actually in (Draco is 0 vs Normal/Steel).

Farig Protect (fresh 100%, saves 39% HP from lethal Spirit Break/Moonblast) + Corv Iron Head -> Clefable: min 23.8% vs 20% remaining = guaranteed kill unless Clef fresh-Protects (possible after streak reset). If blocked, T5 re-execute at 33% decay. Corv is safe all turn (SB 9-14, MB 13-20 into it). Preserves Farig as the Helping Hand engine for the DNite-M execute next turns; also preserves Psychic PP (its DNite chip role).

Clef 21% dies to Iron Head (24–36%) and Ice Crash (25–34%), so it cannot FM Bax anymore. Psychic -1 SpA is only a max-roll KO. Spirit Break 22–40% and Moonblast 22–42% each only high-roll the 39% Farig; together min+min 44% guaranteed KO and Armor Tail drops. In TR Clef/Grimm move before Corv so Moonblast lands, then Clef faints — correct trade. If they pivot Bax into Farig, Fairy double is 70–119%. Do not Protect (Clef is a ghost). Do not hit Corv (Fairy 0.5). Do not TWave in TR.

Clef dead after Farig Protect + Iron Head. Farig still 39% Armor Tail. Rilla Knock Off is 51–95% and always KOs from 39%; WH also KOs. DN Draco is 0 vs Normal Farig and 0 vs Steel Corv, and is last in TR — Multiscale waits for Bax. Grimm Pass. Next: Knock Farig unless they pivot; Fake Out once Armor Tail drops.

T5 (last TR turn): Farigiraf switches to Cofagrigus — resolves before all attacks, saving 39% Farig from Rilla's Knock Off (2x)/Wood Hammer outside TR next turn; Farig is benched and untouchable until the HH+IC execute turn. Corv Iron Head chips Grimm to 51-74 (through Reflect), setting up the T7-T8 Cofag NS + Corv IH kill. Cofag blanks Rilla's whole physical kit (Fake Out 0x fails, WH likely 0.5x) and re-sets TR on T6 after it absorbs their hits at 45 Speed. Bax stays benched — bringing it in now means eating DNite-M's entry Draco (68.2-101.9, potential OHKO) with no attack in return.

Armor Tail still up — do not Fake Out. Knock Off Farig is 51–95% and always KOs 39%. Spirit Break Farig first in TR (22–40%) can already roll the KO; if it does, Knock may retarget Corv and strip Occa. If they stay, Farig dies and Armor Tail drops. If they pivot Bax into Farig, Fairy 32–55% + Knock 13–22%. Farig Protect is only 1/3. Brave Bird Rilla 40–62% through Reflect does not KO. Do not WH Corv (0.25). Do not contact a guessed Cofag pivot over the Farig KO. Last TR turn — attack.

Cofagrigus at 15% Protects (fresh 100% chain — SB/Knock Off would kill it before its -7 priority could ever resolve TR outside Trick Room; Protect banks its body for the Skele-contingency). Corv Iron Head chips Grimm to 0-20% (26-49 thru Reflect) — one more IH kills it T7 guaranteed, and Grimm's death is the prerequisite for safely re-entering Farigiraf (the only HH/TR engine). Bax stays benched at 100% — its whole value is meeting DNite-M/Inteleon with fresh HP, not soaking Grimm's 2x Spirit Breaks. No enemy priority exists anymore (Prankster stripped by Mummy), so Protect-switches are safe.

Cofag 14%: Spirit Break always KOs if it stays; TR is -7 so it dies before TR. If they pivot Bax into that slot, Spirit Break is 32–55% 2x Fairy (Knock only 13–22%). Rilla Protect covers Ice Crash 57–78% and Brave Bird 40–62%. Do not double Cofag (Protect at 14% is likely). Do not switch Grimm to DN — Corv Iron Head 7–11% would break Multiscale then Ice Crash 4x KOs. Grimm 47% lives Iron Head 26–40% through Reflect. Fake Out is not first-turn. Both already Mummy. Never Fire Bax.

T7: Cofag→Bax switch (spent 20% Cofag exits safely; 100% Bax enters without acting, dodging all targeting) + Corv IH→Grimm (~98% kill at 26% HP). Worlds: if they save Grimm by swapping in the 4th, my IH redirects to Rilla and the 4th enters fresh — but it can't act until T8, when Bax IC+Corv chip breaks Multiscale and priority IS finishes ~96%; vs Inteleon, IC+IS/BB doubles kill it inside two turns while it only ever moves first once; vs Skele, Bax soaks Torch Song (0.5x, +1 Atk each). If Grimm stays, it dies T7 and the 4th enters T8 into the same trap. Farigiraf (39%) stays benched as the TR/HH bank for a grind scenario.

Grimm 26% is KO’d by Ice Crash always and by Iron Head on a high roll — Protect (full rate). Corv outspeeds so Grimm cannot attack. Rilla Knock Off always KOs 20% Cofag if it stays (TR is -7). Cofag Protect is 1/3; still take the 2/3 KO. Do not chain Rilla Protect. Do not switch Grimm to DN (Iron Head 7–11% breaks Multiscale). If they pivot Bax, Knock is 13–22% and Grimm Protect covers Ice Crash on Grimm; Rilla lives Ice Crash 57–78%.

selection: Earthquake (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: Baxcalibur Mega Evolves and EQ-spreads: Corv is Flying-type = 0x from EQ, so the spread safely hits both foes — EQ→Grimm (1x, ~32-62 thru Reflect) + Corv IH→Grimm (26-49) = 58-111, guaranteed kill on 32% Grimm unless it chains Protect (33%). Rilla takes a light EQ chip. If they instead swap Grimm out for the hidden 4th, my IH redirects onto the entrant and EQ still chips both — the T9+ kill stack (IC→IS priority finish) handles every hidden monde. Megavolving now: 249 Atk raises every future IC by ~15% with no downside (everything relevant outspeeds Bax anyway).

Reflect is the last turn. Grimm 32% cannot attack before Corv Iron Head. Do not switch DN now: Iron Head 7–11% breaks Multiscale, then next turn Ice Shard without Multi/Reflect KOs before Draco. Let Grimm Spirit Break Bax (32–55% if it lives) and likely faint; send DN after attacks are spent. Next turn Multi intact, Timid 167 Draco always KOs 84% Bax before Ice Crash; Ice Shard through Multi is 43–61% and DN still Dracos. Rilla Protect (full rate) covers Ice Crash 57–78% / Brave Bird. Do not chain Grimm Protect (1/3). Never Fire Bax.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Baxcalibur Protects (fresh chain) to bait the Draco: if DNite Dracos into the block, its self-drop applies even when blocked -> -2 SpA, making every future Draco/FB survivable by Bax's 90% HP. Corv Brave Birds DNite through Multiscale (9-15) — any damage permanently breaks Multiscale, converting next turn's Icicle Crash into a full-power 111.8-194.4 guaranteed kill. Corv tanks everything else DNite/Rilla have (Draco 0.5x via Steel, FB 27-46 thru Occa, WH 0.25x). Rilla's Protect chain is at 11% and its damage into my pair is negligible; the win line is DNite-M dead by T11, Rilla by T12.

Mega on first attacking send. Timid 167 Draco goes before Ice Crash; Ice Shard 43–61% through Multiscale does not KO so Draco still fires. Draco is 85–150% into 90% Bax (low roll lives ~5%), so Knock Off 13–22% after (Rilla 105 > likely Brave 96) guarantees the KO and retargets Corv if Draco already KOs. Never Fire Bax. Do not chain Rilla Protect (1/3). Do not Draco Corv (0.5 Steel). 90% acc is the remaining risk; Protect Bax would punish the double but they EQ’d last turn and DN is a 4x Ice target.

Execution turn: Bax-M Icicle Crash -> DNite-Mega. Multiscale is broken and Bax is at full-power 249 Atk: min band 111.8% vs 83% remaining = guaranteed kill on hit; only a fresh DNite Protect (lethal-read habit) delays it one turn at 33% decay. DNite's -2 SpA makes its entire moveset survivable into Bax (worst combined ~76%), and Rilla's Protect is also decayed. Corv Brave Birds Rillaboom (2x, 30-50) to put it in one-turn-kill range for T11 while Sitrus can only heal once.

Multiscale is broken; Ice Shard 86–121% always KOs 84% DN and Ice Crash is 181–250%. Protect (+4) beats Ice Shard (+1). Draco is only a roll vs 96% (85–150%) and would never fire if Ice Shard KOs first. Rilla Knock Off 13–22% chips Bax (Protect is 1/3 for them); next Draco then KOs. Never Fire Bax. Do not chain Rilla Protect. Do not Draco Corv.

T11: Bax IC -> DNite-M (broken Multiscale + 249 Atk: min 111.8% vs 83% = guaranteed kill unless 33% Protect or 10% miss; both leave a T12 re-execute at 11% chain). Corv BB -> Rilla (full-power 2x, 30-50 vs 62% -> 12-32) pre-positions the final kill: T12 Bax IC one-shots Rilla guaranteed. Corv cannot die this turn (max inbound 46 with Occa intact) and DNite's -2 SpA neutralizes its offense into my 80%/75% cores. Win projected T12.

Corv's menu locked to Pass this phase (sim split the decision after Bax's faint), so locking the fainted-slot fill first: Cofagrigus enters — the only mon that survives Rilla's Wood Hammer (0.5x) to bank a Night Shade on the -4 SpA dragon; if it eats Knock Off/Fire Blast instead, Farigiraf re-enters T13 safely against the crippled dragon. Corv's Brave Bird -> Rillaboom comes on the follow-up selection.

Bax 79%: Draco 85–150% always KOs if it hits. DN 167 outspeeds Ice Crash so the KO lands before Crash. Ice Shard would KO DN first — unavoidable without chaining Protect (1/3). They just Crashed into Protect so Crash/EQ is more likely than Shard. Never Fire Bax. Rilla 62% dies to Ice Crash and is a Brave Bird roll — Protect keeps the 2v2 after Bax faints. Knock cannot finish 79%. 90% acc is the remaining risk.

Full-bank turn: Cofagrigus Protects (fresh 100% — their kill-read on the 20% body is blocked; if the chain fails later it dies as a sac absorbing a DNite action) while Corv Roosts to ~97% with Occa intact — with their SpA at -2, Corv's worst inbound is 46/turn vs Roost's ~50, making it mathematically unkillable while it Brave Birds Rilla out over two turns (62 -> 12-32 -> dead) and then grinds the 83% dragon at 18-30/turn. No risk window exists this turn in any branch.

Bax dead. Cofag 20% TRs at -7 so it dies first if we hit it. Rilla Knock Off always KOs; if Corv 119 Brave Birds Rilla out (roll from 62%) before Knock, DN Ice Beam 13–25% is the 100% acc backup roll. Do not Draco Ghost 0 or Steel 0.5 at -2 SpA. Fire Blast Corv is Occa + -2 = 15–27%, not this turn. Do not chain Rilla Protect. If they Protect Cofag both fail — still correct vs TR. Knock also KOs Farig 39% if they pivot. Already Mummy.

Cofag Night Shade -> DNite-M (50 flat if it survives to its -7 slot, ~45-55% odds given they keep targeting the 20% body) + Corv Brave Bird -> DNite (18-30): combined 68-80 leaves the 83% dragon at 3-15% and Corv finishes T14 in every branch. Killing the dragon first also defuses the only damage that threatens my squad (-2 FB 27-46); Rillaboom's 8-25/turn into Corv is unbeatable by Roost alternation. If Cofag dies instead, Farigiraf's forced entry is disposable and Corv still 1v2-sustains to the win.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Cofag Protect is 1/3 — do not double it. Knock Off still always KOs 20% if they stay/TR/Shadow Ball, and always KOs Farig 39% on a pivot. DN Fire Blast Corv (Occa + -2 is 15–27%) still hits if Cofag Protects and burns Occa for later. Ice Beam Cofag is only a roll. Do not Draco Ghost 0 / Steel 0.5. Do not chain Rilla Protect; Brave Bird is a roll from 62% but finishing Cofag before TR matters more. Already Mummy.

Farigiraf's fresh Protect (100%) nullifies the guaranteed kill-read on its 39% body (Rilla Knock Off/Wood Hammer both lethal; DNite Draco also lethal) and banks it for a T15 Helping Hand. Corv Brave Birds Rilla to 12-32 (Sitrus gone). T15: HH-boosted BB (45-75) ends Rillaboom guaranteed; then the -2-SpA dragon falls to Corv BB + Farig Psychic grind by ~T17 with Corv's Roost outpacing all inbound damage. Even if Farig dies T15, Corv 1v1-sustains indefinitely.

Knock Off always KOs 39% Farig (Rilla 105 > Farig 100, and TR is -7). Armor Tail then drops. Brave Bird is a roll KO on both DN 50% and Rilla 62%; they just BBed DN so Protect DN. Do not Draco Farig (Normal 0). Fire Blast Corv is 29–54% at -2 85% and risks losing DN for chip. After Farig faints we 2v1 Corv 71% with Occa gone. Fake Out still dead while Farig is in.

Corv Roosts back to 100% — with their SpA at -2, their best damage (FB 30-38) cannot out-pace Roost alternation, so the 2v1 is a locked win; Farigiraf Psychics the dragon to 25-35%. T16: BB (recoil-safe at full HP) + Psychic ends it; even a miss/Protect only delays to T17 at 11% chain odds. No reason to gamble Corv's 51% body on the faster line when sustain guarantees the same result.

1v2. Draco is 0 vs Farig Normal and 0.5 vs Corv. Ice/Fire at -2 cannot KO 39% Farig (12–28%). Fire Blast Corv 29–54% vs 50% is the only KO chance (85% acc, Occa gone). If Corv faints, Psychic 30–45% from 50% leaves DN alive for one more turn. Do not chain Protect (1/3). Pass on fainted Rilla.

Checkmate geometry: DNite-M at 12% can kill exactly one of my two Pokémon per turn, and both of my attackers guarantee the kill on 12% (Corv IH 13-22, Farig Psy 13-23 — T15's roll calibrated the floor). Double-targeting the dragon: if it attacks, the survivor executes; if it fresh-Protects, both attacks still land next resolution... actually if it Protects both are blocked but its 33% chain then dies T17 to the survivor. Every branch ends with DNite dead by T17 and at least one of my mons standing. No protect-banking needed when the board is already won.
Psychic always KOs 13% DN; Fire Blast cannot KO 58% Corv at -2 (29–54%). Attack first (167) anyway — Fire Blast Corv is the only chip. Draco is 0 vs Farig. Protect only delays the KO. Pass Rilla.

reflections.summary: WON Game 1 in 16 turns, 0 decision errors. The draft (Farig+Corv lead, Bax-M+Cofag flex; Hatt/Garg benched) was correct against the revealed screen-stack: Grimm+Clef led, Rilla third, DNite-M closer — Inteleon and Skeledirge stayed home, so their brought-4 rotates. T1 Trick Room was unconditional (their T1 is always screens/Follow Me — never an attack). Clefable died T4 through Follow Me + a fresh Protect read; the Mummy chain on T5 stripped Grimmsnarl's Prankster and Rillaboom's Grassy Surge permanently, a free recurring value engine; Grimm died T8 to the Mega-EQ spread (Corv immune to EQ = free spread) plus Iron Head. Two expensive lessons: (1) my damage bands understated their DNite-M SpA by ~2x — a -2 SpA Draco killed my 80% Bax-M on T11, the only real error-adjacent moment (predictable from Protect-war mechanics: their fresh Protects on every lethal read meant my IC was blocked T10 and Bax couldn't re-Protect at 33%); (2) Cofag's -7 Night Shade never resolved because Rilla's faster Knock Off killed it first. The endgame was textbook: Cofagrigus's two Protect turns absorbed four foe actions, Corv sustained 1v2 via Roost alternation (their -2 SpA Fire Blast rolled 35-55% vs Roost's ~50%), Rilla fell T14, and the 12% dragon died T16 to Corv's Brave Bird. Corviknight is the game MVP: 0.5x Draco typing + 0.25x Wood Hammer + Roost math made it literally unkillable in the endgame.
reflections.adjustment: KEEP: the draft, lead, and Corv-sustain endgame. FIX for G2 — the DNite-M protocol: (1) never let Bax-M end a turn below 100% vs a fresh-stage DNite-M; under TR the guaranteed kill is IS-chip first (22.7-41 thru Multiscale, priority) THEN Farig HH + Bax IC (guaranteed vs <=84% remnant), or Corv-BB breaks Multiscale then full-power IC; (2) if DNite-M enters while TR is down, Bax stays benched — Corv is the wall (0.5x Draco via Steel, 0.25x WH) and wins the Roost-race, so there is no need to force Bax in; (3) anti-Protect discipline: they fresh-Protect every lethal read, so execute on 33%/11% chain turns and use Protect/switch/HH on 100% turns instead of wasting double-attacks. Consider Garganacl over Cofagrigus only if they bring Skeledirge+Inteleon heavy; Cofag's Mummy-strips and Protect-absorption remain the default.

reflections.summary: Lost G1 0-1. They brought Farig+Corv+Bax+Cofag (left Hatterene/Garg). Screens T1-2 were correct vs Iron Head/TR; T4 double Farig into Protect sacrificed Clef and Farig lived 39% all game. Then we contacted Cofag (Mummy stole Prankster+Surge), crit Iron Head flinched Grimm, and Corv Iron Head locked the Grimm slot. Bax Protect on DN entry wasted Draco; we still KO’d Bax next Draco from 79%. Endgame: Corv Roost+Brave Bird stalled, Farig Protect ate Knock, Rilla died, -2 SpA DN could not break Farig (Dragon 0 vs Normal) or 58% Corv. Dirge was boxed and would have resisted Iron Head (0.5), Ice (0.5), Shadowed Cofag, and Torched Corv without contact.
reflections.adjustment: G2 bring Grimm+Dirge+DN+Rilla (leave Clef/Inteleon). Lead Grimm+Dirge into Farig+Corv so Iron Head hits a 0.5 resist, not 2x Fairy. Never contact Cofag. Never double a chipped Farig/Cofag — they Protect. Knock Farig only when Protect is unlikely; Dirge Shadow Cofag. Mega DN Draco Bax only after they spend Protect, and keep a Dark hit for Farig so -2 SpA DN is not the closer. If they bring Garg G2, Rilla WH is already on the 4; if they drop Cofag for Hatterene, Dirge still Shadows.

events.text: Light Screen up on P2's side

decisions.rationale: G1-validated bring-4: Farig+Corv lead (their T1 habit is screens/FM, never attacks — TR lands free behind Armor Tail, which also blanks Rilla FakeOut/Prankster Taunt if Rilla plays; Corv executes frail Grimm and tanks Inteleon/Rilla chip). Bax-M back = guaranteed DNite-M answer (IC one-shots through Multiscale with HH). Cofag back = Night Shade out-grinds Skeledirge Protect/Leftovers chains + SB 2x. Inteleon+Skele are newly in play range but my four covers all six: Corv (Grimm/Rilla/Inteleon chip), Bax (DNite-M), Cofag (Skele grind), Farig (TR core). No lead change warranted on registration alone.

G2 4: Grimm+Dirge lead, DN+Rilla back (leave Clef/Inteleon). G1 they led Farig+Corv and Iron Headed the Fairy every turn; Dirge takes Iron Head 0.5 and Ice Crash 0.5, Shadows Cofag without Mummy contact, Torches Corv after Occa, Unaware vs Bax. Grimm Prankster Reflect still goes up through Armor Tail. Rilla Knock is the Farig closer (39% always KO; Draco is 0 vs Normal). DN Timid Draco is the Bax answer after they spend Protect. Inteleon is last under TR; Clef was the Iron Head magnet and died before FM Bax. T1 Reflect; never contact Cofag, never Fire Bax, never Ghost Farig.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: Script T1: Farig TR (Armor Tail blanks any Prankster Taunt; Herb backup; their T1 is passive screens — TR resolves free after attacks). Corv IH -> Grimm: 38.6-74.1 verified, grinds the frail screen-setter; Torch Song inbound worst case 28.5-42% into full-HP Corv — safe to take one, and under TR Corv+Farig act first from T2. Skele is Cofag/Night Shade bait later (SB 0x vs Farig, nothing Farig can damage).

G1 script: Farig TRs, Corv Iron Heads the Fairy. Prankster Reflect (+1) is not blocked by Armor Tail and goes up before Iron Head; Grimm lives 39–59% raw and ~26–40% through Reflect (HH still not a KO). Dirge Torch Corv eats Occa (G1 Fire was dead until it was gone) and +1 SpA; Unaware still ignores a Thermal Exchange boost if they spicy-switch Bax. Do not Shadow Farig (Normal 0). Do not LS first — Iron Head/Brave Bird/Ice Crash are physical. Do not switch DN/Rilla into this Iron Head.

Reflect is up (7t) and Skele is +1: Corv at 60% dies to the Torch Song stack if it stays (T2 15% snap at +1, near-certain vs +2). Rotate Corv to Cofag before damage: switches resolve first, Cofag acts FIRST under TR (45) — Shadow Ball 2x into Skele (46-105%, no LS up yet) with NS 50-flat as the screen-proof fallback. Cofag takes Torch at neutral ~30-36% and blanks Spirit Break chip; Mummy strips Prankster if Grimm makes contact. Farig Protect banks the pivot turn, keeps the TR clock (expires ~T5, Cofag is the re-setter). Corv is preserved for the post-Skele Grimm execute and endgame.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Skeledirge)
decisions.rationale: TR 4, Reflect 7. +1 Torch always KOs 59% Corv and Dirge moves first under TR, so Iron Head/Roost never fire if they stay. They may Protect — LS still goes up (Prankster, not blocked). LS is mandatory insurance: Hatterene LO Gleam is 77–109% into 74% Grimm (Fairy 2x Dark) and always KOs without LS; with LS Grimm lives. Farig Psychic Dirge 36–53% lives either way. Do not Spirit Break Farig (Cofag Mummy on contact). Do not Shadow Corv (roll, not a KO). Iron Head through Reflect from 74% is 26–40% so Grimm lives if Corv Protects and attacks. If they spicy-switch Bax into Torch, Unaware ignores Thermal Exchange; Ice Crash Grimm through Reflect 22–32% lives.

The board forces this: Skele at +2 makes T4+ Torches lethal to every mon I have (Farig 75-112% at +3, Cofag/Corv worse), so Bax's entry window is NOW — it uniquely survives the +2 Torch (56.5-84.1) and converts it to +1 Atk via Thermal Exchange. Cofag's fresh 100% Protect blanks the kill-read Torch aimed at its 48% self and forces all single-target fire onto Bax. If they double-focus Bax (Torch+SB = 102-151) it dies, but that requires them to SB the fresh Dragon over the obvious 48% Cofag — at most a coin flip, and the branch keeps Farig 100% + Corv 60% intact either way. NS into Skele is only 24-28% (verified) — no fast kill exists, so banking material beats spending it.

Dual screens up, TR 3. +2 Shadow Ball always KOs 47% Cofag (123–230%) with no Mummy contact; Torch also KOs but Thermal Exchange if they pivot Bax into that slot — Shadow chips Bax 53–95% instead. Do not Spirit Break Cofag (Mummy). Spirit Break Farig: 22–40% and −1 SpA if they stay; 38–67% 2x if they pivot Bax into Farig. Farig Protect is 1/3 so do not double Farig. Do not double Cofag (G1 they Protect the KO-range mon). Psychic Dirge through LS is 24–35%; Cofag Shadow Dirge 37–57%; Grimm lives Iron Head/Ice Crash through Reflect. Rilla Knock Farig is 51–95% not a KO and Fake Out is blanked; DN Draco is 0 vs Normal/Ghost — stay.

selection: Earthquake (all adjacent, including ally Cofagrigus) + Mega Evolve
decisions.rationale: No defensive line survives the Torch clock (it kills one Torch-vulnerable active per turn; Bax at 47% and Cofag at 48% are both dead-walking), so the play is max burst: Cofag SB (45 — acts first) + Bax MEGA EQ into Skeledirge = 51.9-104.5%, an ~8% same-turn kill and a Skele left at 0-48% on average for the T5 EQ #2 finisher. The EQ self-chip drops Cofag to 10-16% — the designated Torch sac — so if their Torch targets Cofag (the read I want), Bax survives at 47% with Mega online for the T5 kill and the DNite-M execute. If they Torch Bax instead, I still banked ~38% on Skele and pivot to the Corv-BB Grimm kill. Holding Protects would just concede the race.

Both burst mons died to a crit before the EQ landed — 2v4 now, and the only kill range left on the board is HH-boosted Brave Bird into the 73% Grimm (43.5-83%). Taking the swing while TR is still up (my mons act first) is the only line with any win equity left; banking Protects or chipping Skele (Corv BB only 13-16%) concedes outright. Farig and Corv enter via free forced-fill and get their full actions this turn.

Their 4 is Farig/Corv/Bax/Cofag. Armor Tail is down but Fake Out requires Rilla already in — do not switch Grimm into Ice Crash. Do not double 46% Bax (G1 they Protect the KO-range mon). Spirit Break Bax is a 38–67% roll from 46%; +2 Shadow always KOs 47% Cofag (Cofag Protect is 1/3 after T3). If they Protect Bax, Shadow still removes Cofag. If they attack, Grimm lives Ice Crash 22–32% through Reflect and Dirge lives EQ 27–38% + Cofag Shadow 37–57%. Never Spirit Break Cofag (Mummy). Never Torch Bax (Thermal Exchange). DN Draco is last under TR and G1 they Protected Bax on DN entry — leave Multiscale for after TR.

Max-value line while TR inversion lasts: Farig HH (+5, first) boosts Corv BB -> Grimm to 43.5-83% (kill ~25% incl. crit range; otherwise Grimm 17.5-44 for next-turn pressure). BB over IH for the kill band; recoil leaves Corv 42-51% — acceptable in a 2v4 where any Torch kills anyway. Skeledirge is unkillable with remaining tools (BB->Skele 13-16%).

Last TR turn, Armor Tail back, no bench for them. +2 Torch always KOs 59% Corv so they Protect it (G1/G2 they Protect the KO-range mon). Spirit Break 22–40% + Torch Farig 58–108% always KOs 100% Farig if it stays — removes Armor Tail. If they attack with Corv instead, Farig still dies and Grimm lives Iron Head 26–40% through Reflect. Do not Shadow Farig (0). Do not Spirit Break Corv (0.5). Do not switch Rilla (Fake Out blanked, no attack this turn). Dirge lives Psychic 24–35% from 55%. After Farig dies, +2 Torch still KOs Corv even through Roost (115–209% from full).

No survival line exists: Torch (+3) and SB both kill Corv from full HP, so Roost/Protect only delay one turn. Max expected value is the BB into 42% Grimm (~51% kill, possibly a 3v1 board for a turn) before Corv is inevitably removed. Farig's slot is fainted with no bench — pass.

2v1 Corv 48%, Armor Tail gone, TR over. +3 Torch is 143–261% and always KOs even if they Roost to full first (they outspeed). Only Protect saves them. Grimm 43% dies to crit Iron Head (57–89%) or crit Brave Bird (43–65%) — Protect covers the crit. If they Protect, Torch fails and we click it T7 at 1/3. Do not Spirit Break Corv (0.5). Do not switch Rilla into Brave Bird 2x. Do not chain this as a 1v2 — Dirge is the KO.

reflections.summary: Lost Game 2 in 6 turns (series 1-1). The harness logged 0 decision errors, and the in-game lines were defensible: T1 TR landed free with an IH chip on Grimm; T2's Corv-to-Cofag pivot was correct (Torch at +1 was a 15%+ snap on 60% Corv and lethal at +2); T3's Bax-entry + Cofag-Protect bait made Skeledirge waste a turn and stay at +2. The real loss happened at DRAFT: I brought Farig/Corv/Bax/Cofag for the expected Grimm+Clef script, and grok rotated to Grimm+Skeledirge — a board my four structurally cannot beat. Skeledirge's Torch Song (+1 SpA per use, sim bands ~2x my estimates) killed Cofag at +1 (52%) and would have killed every remaining mon from full by +3; nothing in my four deals real damage to it (Bax IC 0.5x, Psychic attackers 0x into Fire/Ghost, Corv 2x), and Garganacl — the registered Torch-resist + Salt Cure grinder — was left home. The T4 all-in (Cofag SB 52% + Mega EQ) was the best remaining line and lost to a live critical Spirit Break that killed Bax before its EQ resolved, then Skele's SB removed Cofag — a double death that made it 2v4, unwinnable. Positive takeaways: TR script worked (T1 free vs their passive screen T1), the Protect-bait read on T3 was right, and I identified the band inflation and crit reality live. The fix is roster-level, not play-level.
reflections.adjustment: G3 (series decider): swap GARGANACL in over Cofagrigus — it is the only registered answer to a Torch-stack board (0.5x resist + Salt Cure residual grind that beats Protect/Leftovers chains; Rock Slide 2x = 37-77 per dmg-book, Reflect-halved) while Cofag proved chippable (52% at +1 Torch). Bring Farig/Garg/Bax/Corv; Hatterene stays home (Psychic is 0x into Dark AND Ghost here — no damage vs their Dark/Ghost core; its Fairy 0.5x Torch-resist is real but Garg does the same job with bulk). Keep Farig+Corv lead (Grimm always leads; Armor Tail covers Rilla-FakeOut and any Prankster; TR T1 free). Draft law going forward: build for the registered six's worst-case board, not the observed lead, because grok rotates the Grimm partner every game.

reflections.summary: Won G2 in 6 turns, series 1-1. Same 4 both games (Farig+Corv+Bax+Cofag; left Hatterene+Garg). Grimm+Dirge lead was the G1 fix: Iron Head hits 0.5 Dirge not 2x Fairy, T1 Reflect+Torch ate Occa, dual screens, never contacted Cofag, never Torched Bax. T4 crit Spirit Break KO’d Mega Bax and Shadow KO’d Cofag; T5 doubled Farig (Corv was the Protect/HH+BB) and Torch KOed it; T6 Protect Grimm (crit IH/BB range) +3 Torch KO’d 48% Corv. DN and Rilla never entered. 0 decision errors.
reflections.adjustment: G3 keep Grimm+Dirge+DN+Rilla; leave Clef (Iron Head magnet) and Inteleon (last under TR — they have not dropped Farig). Lead Grimm+Dirge again vs Farig+Corv. T1 Reflect+Torch Corv. Shadow Cofag, Spirit Break Bax, double Farig if Corv is the Protect. Bring Rilla for Knock/Garg and DN as Bax backup. If they finally lead Hatterene, LS+Dirge Shadow. If they drop Farig, Inteleon becomes live — they have not.

events.text: Light Screen up on P2's side
Light Screen ended on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Series decider (1-1). Their G3 six: Rilla/Inteleon/DNite-M/Skele/Grimm/Clef — Sneasler+Tauros out, Inteleon+Clef in. Draft for the worst case: Farig+Corv lead (Grimm always leads; this registration has NO Taunt/FakeOut on Grimm, and Armor Tail blanks Rilla FakeOut/Grassy Glide → TR lands free T1; Corv IH executes Grimm 2x, walls Draco). Back: Garg (Torch 0.5x wall — the G2 Torch clock is what killed us — RS 2x Skele + SC grind) and Bax (DNite-M execute: HH+IC one-shots through full Multiscale; never fields outside TR). Hatt benched: Psychic is 0x vs Dark/Ghost board (Grimm/Skele) so her offense is neutered; Cofag benched: no Sneasler to blank.

G3 1-1: same 4 as G2 — Grimm+Dirge lead, DN+Rilla back, leave Clef (Iron Head magnet) and Inteleon (last under TR; they have not dropped Farig). They led Farig+Corv both games and Iron Head the Fairy every T1; Dirge takes IH 0.5 and Ice 0.5, Shadows Cofag without Mummy, Torches Corv after Occa. Grimm Prankster Reflect still goes up through Armor Tail. T1 Reflect+Torch Corv. Rilla Knock is the Farig closer; DN Timid Draco is Bax backup. If they finally lead Hatterene, LS+Dirge Shadow. Never contact Cofag, never Fire Bax, never Ghost Farig.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Corviknight)
decisions.rationale: G2-repeat lead confirmed (Grimm+Skele). Farig TR T1 — free, their T1 is screens (no Taunt/FakeOut on this Grimm reg). Corv IH→Grimm (2x; observed ~73-76% thru Reflect, 2 IHs kill). Skele Torch→Corv ~40% with Occa per G2 evidence — acceptable; T2 Garg pivots in as Torch wall while IH executes Grimm under TR.

G1/G2 script: Farig TRs, Corv Iron Heads the Fairy. Prankster Reflect (+1) is not blocked by Armor Tail and goes up before Iron Head; Grimm lives 39–59% raw and ~26–40% through Reflect (HH still not a KO). Dirge Torch Corv eats Occa and +1 SpA. Do not Shadow Farig (Normal 0). Do not LS first — Iron Head/Brave Bird/Ice Crash are physical. Do not switch DN/Rilla into this Iron Head. Never Torch Bax if they spicy-switch — Unaware still ignores Thermal Exchange if they do.

Torch +1 → Corv (2x, Occa gone) is lethal per G2 scaling — mandatory exit. Garg enters as the Torch wall (0.5x ~25-35%, Recovers to 85). Farig spends the free TR turn on verified chip: Psy→Skele 1x 31.3-57.5% before any Light Screen comes up, putting Skele at ~42-69% for the T3 Garg RS combo (kill T3-T4 inside TR). Farig survives worst-case lone Spirit Break (29.5-42.7); double-focus risk this turn is low (their all-ins target Mega threats).

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Skeledirge)
decisions.rationale: TR 4, Reflect 7. +1 Torch always KOs 59% Corv and Dirge moves first under TR, so Iron Head/Roost never fire if they stay. They may Protect or pivot Cofag (G2 T2) — LS still goes up (Prankster, not blocked). LS is mandatory insurance: Hatterene LO Gleam is 77–109% into 74% Grimm even through Reflect and always KOs without LS. Farig Psychic Dirge 36–53% lives. Do not Spirit Break Farig (Cofag Mummy on contact). Do not Shadow Corv (roll, not a guaranteed KO). If they spicy-switch Bax into Torch, Unaware ignores Thermal Exchange; Ice Crash Grimm through Reflect lives. Iron Head through Reflect from 74% is 26–40% so Grimm lives if Corv Protects and attacks.

Skele at +2 is the win-clock: +3 Torch→Farig is lethal-range, +4/+5 outscores Garg's Recover. Aggro line (RS+Psy now) drops Garg to ~45-55% where a +3 Torch read kills it, and a Skele Slack Off (heals ~50) escapes the TR window entirely. Instead: Farig Psy→Skele (20.9-38.5 thru LS → Skele ~45-62%) + Garg Recover (Torch→Garg only 27.7-41.5, Garg stays ~65-78, full after next Recover). T4-T5: RS+Psy kills Skele inside TR; Farig Protects once chipped (Torch→Farig 53.3-79.3 = death if chipped). Grimm (74%, no recovery) is the post-Skele cleanup target via SC/Corv.

Dual screens up, TR 3. 4th is almost certainly Bax (mega both games; Garg replaced Cofag as the Fire pivot). Do not double Farig: G1/G2 they Protect the KO target, and +2 Torch Farig into a Bax switch is Thermal Exchange. Spirit Break Farig is 22–41% if they stay (−1 SpA) and 38–67% 2x if they G2-clone Bax into that slot. Torch Garg is 28–49% into 76% (not a KO) but +3 SpA makes later Farig/Corv Torches lethal; +2 Torch already always KOs 59% Corv. Do not Shadow Farig (0). Do not Spirit Break Garg (16–27%). Do not send Rilla yet — Garg 55–87 always moves first under TR so WH gets Protect/Recover, and showing Grassy telegraphs it. Dirge lives Psychic 24–35% and Rock Slide 21–33% through screens; HH+RS is the only KO range. Never contact Cofag, never Fire Bax.

Kill-window turn: only max chip (RS 19.4-34.1 + Psy 13.9-25.7 at -1 SpA) threatens Skele (→~1.5-28%) before the Torch stack (+6 kills even full Garg) ends the race. Safe alternatives (Protect/Recover) were simulated — they never out-patch Slack Off+Lefties and lose the Garg race by T6-T8. Under TR Garg acts before Skele, so T5 = Recover-then-eat-+4-Torch; Farig Psy then kills most of the remaining range. Targeting inertia (Torch hit Garg twice) makes Torch→Farig the low-probability line.

+3 Torch always KOs 68% Farig (72–135%) and Armor Tail drops if they stay; Dirge lives a single −1 Psychic 24–35% or Rock Slide 21–33%. Do not double Farig — 68% is Protect range (G1/G2). Spirit Break Garg still chips 16–27% if Farig Protects. Bax into Farig is a 65–117% Torch roll plus TE — they kept Farig three turns so stay/Protect is more likely than the T3 switch they skipped. Do not send Rilla yet: FO is blanked while Farig is in, and if Farig faints this turn T5 Rilla FO Garg is live. Dirge 55% dies to combined Garg-first + Psychic on some rolls; taking that risk for the Armor Tail KO. Never Shadow Farig (0). Never Fire Bax if they finally pivot.

Dirge died to Rock Slide + Psychic before Torch. Send Rilla not DN: WH always KOs 53% Garg, Knock Farig 51–95% into 68% is a roll, Grassy on entry. DN is last under TR, Draco 0 vs Farig, and Ice Crash 4x. Armor Tail still up — no Fake Out until Farig faints. Grimm Pass.

Positioning turn before the T6 re-set: Farig Protect (Armor Tail also blocks any Fake Out — Rilla's W1 T1 habit is a wasted move vs me; Farig must not be chipped below 68 before facing KnockOff 57.3-81.9), Garg Recover under TR (acts before Grimm/Rilla) to ~full so it can eat SB and Lefties/terrain heal toward T6 Protect. Rilla's WH (83.1-120 on Garg) and KnockOff (57.3-81.9 on Farig) make T6 the forced gamble turn — max safety now maximizes Farig's re-set survival odds.

Last TR turn. Fake Out is blanked by Armor Tail. Garg 55–87 always Protects (+4) before Rilla WH, so WH Garg is the Protect they click after seeing Grassy. Spirit Break 22–41% + Knock 51–95% = 73% min vs 68% Farig — always KOs if they stay and Armor Tail drops. Do not double Garg. WH Farig is only a roll (62–114%) and recoil with Dirge already dead. If they Protect Farig both fail — acceptable vs the more likely Garg Protect. If they pivot Bax into Farig, SB is 38–67% 2x. Rilla lives Psychic 19–27% and Ice Crash 48–68% through Reflect+Sitrus. Never FO. Never WH Corv 0.25.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Garganacl)
decisions.rationale: Forced re-set turn: TR-less endgame loses the tempo war to Rilla 105-137, and Farig is my only setter in-game. Armor Tail blocks Fake Out field-wide, Garg's Protect blocks the WH kill (83.1-120), so the only live risk is Knock Off→Farig (~32% death at 74% HP) — the cheapest achievable gamble, and terrain already healed Farig 68→74 to shrink it. Garg Protects (never attacks vs live Rilla).

TR over, Rilla 105 outspeeds both. Garg Recovered to 100% — Recover is useless so they Protect (+4 before WH) or Salt. WH Garg is 91–154% a roll vs 100% if they greedy Salt/RS; if they Protect, Spirit Break Farig still lands (Farig Protect is 1/3 after T5). Do not double Farig again (they just showed Protect). Knock+SB is 73% min vs 74% not a KO; WH Farig is a roll. Fake Out is gone (not first turn). SB Bax 38–67% if they finally pivot. Never WH Corv 0.25. Screens still up; Rilla lives Psychic 19–27% and Salt 9–13%.

Zero-risk consolidation: Farig Protect is fresh (blocks the SB that can't quite kill it but chips it into lethal range), and Garg exits at 100% rather than risking a 33% Protect-fail into Wood Hammer (36% death). Corv enters action-less but walls their entire remaining offense (WH 0.25x, SB 0.5x, KO survivable on 60%), banking Garg as the full-HP FB-wall for the DNite-M endgame. T8-T9: Corv IH kills Grimm (51-99 once Reflect expires), ending the SB pressure permanently.

TR 4, Garg Protect is 1/3, Farig Protect is full again. Knock Off is 51–95% vs 48% Farig — always KOs if they stay (they TRed last turn instead of Protecting at 42%). Spirit Break Farig covers the Bax TR-entry (38–67% 2x) and still chips if they stay. Do not WH Garg: even under TR a 1/3 Protect still blanks it, and Knock Farig is the guaranteed KO. Fake Out is not first-turn. SB Garg 16–27% does not KO 100%. If Farig Protects both fail — they just declined Protect at this HP. Armor Tail drops if Knock hits.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Corv is my only sustainable piece and must survive both the Rilla BB-recoil grind and the DNite-M entry (FB→Corv 54-92 kills a chipped bird) — Roost now banks it near-full. Grimm is terrain-sticky (killable only at ≥86 rolls while it heals +6/turn), so the kill order is Rilla first (BB 60-80 post-Reflect ×2 + Farig HH) and Grimm later. Farig Protects chain-fresh (33%) to block the coordinated SB+KO kill attempt; even on fail, SB (max 42.7) can't kill 55%.

WH always KOs 55% Farig (62–114%); Knock is only a roll (51–95%). Farig Protect is 1/3 — do not double it. Grimm lives Iron Head 26–40% through Reflect from 80% (crit still lives). Reflect has 1 turn left — Prankster refresh to 8 vs Corv physical and possible Bax. Do not WH Corv 0.25 or SB Corv 0.5. Do not send DN into Iron Head this TR (Multiscale breaks, Fire Blast 59% is a roll 58–106% 85%). Brave Bird Rilla 40–62% lives + Sitrus. Fake Out not first-turn. If Farig Protects, we still keep screens.

The planned Rilla kill: HH (+1.5x) + Brave Bird (2x, no Reflect) ≈ 90-120% — Rilla to ~25-35 after Sitrus, dead to T10's plain BB. Under TR Farig (72) and Corv (87) both act before Rilla (105-137); Corv takes ~30-40 recoil but is at 100 (recoil-safe). Grimm's terrain-heal expires after this turn — it'll be a static ~92 target for the T13 HH+Bax-M execute. Farig's Psy is worthless (-2 SpA) but HH is unaffected; this is its best remaining use, accepting the ~45% KO-read risk that exists on any non-Protect turn regardless.

Interface locks slot 2 to Pass (forced-fill consumes the structure). Bax enters as the fill (Mega + IC→Rilla kills 39% Rilla if the fill-mon acts this turn, else T11 under TR still resolves before Rilla). Corv passes; at 77% it survives the full inbound (SB 16-24 + KO/FakeOut ≤35) and the hidden entry-mon can't exist yet (no foe death this turn unless Bax kills Rilla — in which case FB→Corv 39% death risk is accepted rather than burning Garg's wall value or losing the Rilla execute).

reflections.summary: G3 won in 25 turns, closing the series 2-1. Three pillars decided it. (1) The G2→G3 adjustment worked: Garganacl in for Cofagrigus answered the exact loss-cause — Garg walled Skeledirge's Torch Song stack (0.5x) while Farig's Psychic + Garg's Rock Slide executed Skele on T4, killing the +1-per-use clock that beat us in G2. (2) Bax-Mega converted a 15%-HP body into their closer: entered via forced-fill (free + full action), chipped fresh Dragonite for 87% through full Multiscale (4x band live-confirmed), then priority Ice Shard traded it for the kill on T13 — after that their board had no burst left. (3) The T18-T25 endgame was the Roost-grind: Corv solo 1v2 against Grimm+Rilla's 20-Protect spam, Fake Out flinches and Grassy sustain, but their HP was fully static (no recovery, Sitrus consumed) and Roost-PP is effectively infinite — kills landed exactly on their 11%-Protect windows as mapped (Grimm T24, Rilla T25). Between-game adjustments helped; the structural cost was the draft's missing second TR setter — Farig died T9 to a 15% Wood Hammer read and no TR re-set existed after T11, nearly opening the door the grind had to close. One self-identified index slip (T17 submitted [4,3] for [3,4]) cost about a turn. Decision errors by the simulator count: 0.
reflections.adjustment: Against grok in a future series: (1) Cofagrigus is a MUST-bring every game — a second TR setter converts the T12+ endgame from a grind into a kill; never repeat the Farig-only draft. (2) Assume Protect-spam: plan kills around their chain (attack on 11% windows, bank on fresh chains — Roost/Protect instead of wasted 57% reads); their spam gives me free tempo turns, so patience is strictly better than reads. (3) Garganacl never attacks or fields off-Protect while a live Rillaboom can Wood Hammer (terrain-boosted 83-120 = lethal-on-read); Rilla dies to Corv Brave Bird once Reflect drops. (4) Expect their pool to churn every window (they swapped Sneasler+Tauros for Inteleon+Clef this week, fielding neither) — re-scout the registered six each time; Grimm-lead + screens + DNite-M closer is the stable spine. (5) Post-Farig, always double-attack or Protect — Fake Out flinch steals any single-threaded kill turn. (6) When their board has no recovery (verify items: no Lefties = grind wins automatically), Corv's Roost-cycle is a guaranteed win — play slowly, never rush.
